    #include <zlib/ZmAssert.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZxdpAlloc.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZxdpUMem.hh>
    
    namespace Zxdp {
    
    BufPool::BufPool(unsigned n, unsigned bytes) {
      count = n;
      size = bytes;
    }
    BufPool::~BufPool() { ZmAssert_(!unsigned(m_used)); }
    
    void BufPool::init(
      ZmRef<UMem> arena, uint64_t offset, unsigned stride, unsigned prefix, unsigned first)
    {
      ZmAssert_(!unsigned(m_used));
      m_active = 0;
      m_arena = ZuMv(arena);
      m_offset = offset;
      m_shift = __builtin_ctz(stride);
      m_prefix = prefix;
      m_first = first;
      m_tx = offset >= m_arena->layout().rxLength;
      m_head = 0;
      // Same non-sharded payload-overlay slist initialization as ZmHeap arenas.
      for (unsigned i = count; i; --i) {
        auto p = backing(i - 1);
        reinterpret_cast<ZmAtomic<uintptr_t> *>(p)->store_(m_head.load_());
        m_head.store_(uintptr_t(p));
      }
      m_active = 1;
    }
    
    uint8_t *BufPool::alloc()
    {
      if (ZuUnlikely(!unsigned(m_active))) return nullptr;
      uintptr_t p;
    loop:
      p = m_head.load_();
      if (ZuUnlikely(!p)) return nullptr;
      if (ZuUnlikely(p & 1)) { ZmAtomic_acquire(); goto loop; }
      if (ZuUnlikely(m_head.cmpXch(p | 1, p) != p)) goto loop;
      ++m_used;
      m_head = reinterpret_cast<ZmAtomic<uintptr_t> *>(p)->load_();
      if (m_tx) m_arena->txSlot(*this, slot(reinterpret_cast<void *>(p))).refs = 1;
      return reinterpret_cast<uint8_t *>(p);
    }
    
    void BufPool::free(void *packet)
    {
      auto id = slot(packet);
      ZmAssert_(id != NoSlot);
      if (m_tx && --m_arena->txSlot(*this, id).refs) return;
      auto p = backing(id);
      uintptr_t next;
    loop:
      next = m_head.load_();
      if (next & 1) { ZmAtomic_acquire(); goto loop; }
      reinterpret_cast<ZmAtomic<uintptr_t> *>(p)->store_(next);
      if (m_head.cmpXch(uintptr_t(p), next) != next) goto loop;
      // Final accounting follows publication; no mapping access follows it.
      ZmAssert_(m_used--);
    }
    
    unsigned BufPool::slot(const void *packet) const
    {
      if (!m_arena) return NoSlot;
      auto begin = uintptr_t(m_arena->data()) + m_offset + m_prefix;
      auto address = uintptr_t(packet);
      if (address < begin) return NoSlot;
      auto offset = address - begin;
      auto id = offset>>m_shift;
      auto within = offset & (stride() - 1);
      return id < count && within < size ? unsigned(id) : NoSlot;
    }
    bool BufPool::owns(const void *packet) const { return slot(packet) != NoSlot; }
    bool BufPool::writable(const void *packet) const
    {
      auto id = slot(packet);
      return m_tx && id != NoSlot && unsigned(m_arena->txSlot(*this, id).refs) == 1;
    }
    uint8_t *BufPool::backing(unsigned id) const {
      ZmAssert_(m_arena && id < count);
      return m_arena->data() + m_offset + (uint64_t(id)<<m_shift) + m_prefix;
    }
    
    } // namespace Zxdp
    # Build, test, and development
    
    Part of the repository guidance mapped in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
    
    ## Build system
    
    ### Module layout
    - The Z modules are bundles of libraries and programs
    - Every Z module is succinctly named `z*`, e.g. `zu`, `zdb`
    - Z libraries scope naming with a corresponding prefix, e.g. `Zu`, `Zdb`
    - Every Z module has these required subdirectories:
      - `src`: library and program source code
      - `test`: unit tests using `ZuTest`/`ZuTestUtil` and emitting TAP
    - A module may also have these optional subdirectories when it has content of
      the corresponding role:
      - `util`: utility programs and scripts used by `itest`, `interop`, or `bench`
      - `itest`: integration tests using `ZuTest`/`ZuTestUtil` and emitting TAP
      - `example`: dependent programs demonstrating use of the module
      - `bench`: benchmark harnesses
      - `interop`: external interoperability framework testing
    - The standard directories are not an exhaustive allow-list. Additional
      module-specific directories are permitted as documented exceptions when a
      distinct facility does not fit a standard role; for example, `zdb_pq/ext`
      contains a PostgreSQL extension, follows PostgreSQL/PGXS naming, and is built
      after the standard directories. Document each exception in the module's
      README or `GUIDELINES.md`, including its naming and build convention.
    - `test` is for isolated unit tests. Tests which launch complete programs,
      require multiple services, exercise persistence or networking end to end, or
      require environment setup belong in `itest`. Tests specifically exercising a
      third-party implementation or conformance framework belong in `interop`.
    - Repository-owned unit and integration test programs use
      `ZuTest`/`ZuTestUtil`, emit valid TAP, and run from the corresponding
      directory's `make test` target. Shell scripts may be fixtures invoked by a
      ZuTest driver; external harness scripts in `interop` may remain native.
    - `util` is independently buildable. `itest` may depend on programs or scripts
      built by `util`; `util` must not depend on `itest`.
    - Module build traversal sequence is: `src`, `test`, `util`, `itest`, other
      directories in dependency order
    - Headers should be organized as a directed acyclic graph with idempotent
      inclusion guards. Tail inclusion should NOT be used unless there is an
      exceptional reason. Circular depndencies should be avoided by factoring
      out common code (example: `ZmFn_.hh` is factored out from `ZmFn.hh` to
      avoid inducing circular dependencies in dependents).
    
    ### Build configuration
    - use the `configure` wrapper named `z.config` to reconfigure the build
      - usage: `z.config -h`
    - Linux executables and shared libraries use zstd-compressed DWARF at link time
      - requires a linker and debugger with zstd-compressed ELF debug-section support
      - retains full debug information; existing input objects can be reused
    - this is a hierarchy of Makefiles that **intentionally** do not automatically rebuild dependencies in other directories
      - use a top-level `make -j8` to ensure all dependencies are rebuilt/refreshed
    - add external dependencies in `configure.ac`
      - use `PKG_CHECK_MODULES` if the dependency is in pkg-config, falling back to dependency-specific `m4` if not
    - always recompile with `make -j8`
      - if not rebuilding everything, if library code has changed in a layer under development, always rebuild `src` before dependent `test`/`util`/`itest`/`example`/`bench`/`interop`, e.g. `make -C zquic/src -j8`
      - always build default target `all` before `make test`, e.g. `make -C zquic/test -j8 && make -C zquic/test test`
      - after build type has changed (release, debug, asan, etc.) do a top-level `make clean && make -j8` to rebuild
      - release-build verification must be configured through `z.config`; after configuring the release build, run top-level `make clean` and then top-level `make -j8` so all dependent Z libraries and tests are rebuilt consistently
      - do not verify a release build by manually compiling selected modules or by rebuilding only dependent subdirectories; that can mix stale objects, stale generated dependency files, or libraries built under a different build type
    - no warnings in build
      - they should be suppressed in the code if false-positive
    
    ## Acceptance
    - test suites must pass
      - clang: address sanitizer, leak sanitizer
      - valgrind: memcheck with leak checking
    
    ## Debugging
    - use `libtool exec` to run programs from `src`, `test`, `util`, `itest`,
      `example`, `bench`, or `interop` under debugging tools within the source tree
      - do not run the binaries in  `.libs` directly - library paths will be incorrect
      - `libtool exec` should be used to run `gdb`, `valgrind`, etc.
    
    ## Quick commands
    
    - `./z.config /opt/z` configures the build with a prefix; use `./z.config -h` for options. Common flags include `-c` to rerun `autoreconf`, `-d` for debug, `-L` for clang, `-G` to disable Gtk, `-P` to disable PostgreSQL, and `-M` for MinGW.
    - `make -j8` builds all enabled modules plus their test binaries.
    - `make install` installs libraries/headers into the configured prefix.
    - `make test` runs tests.
    - Use `libtool exec` to run source-tree test binaries under `gdb`, `valgrind`, and similar tools; do not run binaries from `.libs` directly.
    - Some optional features (for example libbfd backtracing) require external builds; see [README.md](../README.md) for platform-specific steps.
    
    
    ## Testing Guidelines
    - Tests are built as standalone binaries under each module’s `test/` directory.
    - Run specific tests directly from the build tree, for example
      `./zt/test/ZtArrayTest` or `./zdb/itest/zdbsmoketest`.
    - Use `ZuTestUtil` and underlying `ZuTest` for TAP-emitting unit tests.
    - No top-level coverage target is defined; document any new test entry points in the module `test/` directory.
    
    
    ## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
    - For small commits, use a single commit-message line of 94 characters or fewer.
    - For large commits involving multiple changes, use a single overview line followed by `- ` bullets, one for each significant change. Keep each line to 94 characters or fewer.
    - Large global renames or cleanups may be summarized as such.
    - For PRs, include a short summary, list touched modules, and note tests run plus platform/toolchain details.
    
    
    ## Dependencies & Configuration Notes
    Core dependencies include `libck`, `hwloc`, `pcre`, and `zpicotls`. Canonical `flatbuffers` and `flatc` are used only by explicit FlatBuffers interop targets. Optional components include `libpq` (PostgreSQL) and `gtk+3`; enable/disable via `z.config` (`-P`, `-G`) or `configure` flags.
    Add external dependencies in `configure.ac`; use `PKG_CHECK_MODULES` when the dependency is available through pkg-config, falling back to dependency-specific `m4` logic when needed.

    void Stack::start()
    {
      mx()->rxRun([this] { start_(); });
    }
    
    void Stack::start_()
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (ready()) { mx()->pluginStarted({}); return; }
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped);
      m_state = Starting;
      m_returnQueued = 0;
      m_ingress->rxFrames->reconcile();
      m_error = {};
      bool busy = m_ingress->pool.used();
      for (auto p = m_providers; p; p = p->nextProvider) busy |= p->pool.used();
      if (busy) {
        m_state = Stopped;
        mx()->pluginStarted(ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "retained packet pools are busy"));
        return;
      }
      m_backend = Zxdp::Instance::create({.interface = m_interface, .netmask = m_netmask,
        .txPools = &m_providers->pool, .rxPool = &m_ingress->pool,
        .rx = [this](uint8_t *p, unsigned n) { received(p, n); },
        .spin = m_spin, .scheduler = mx(), .txSid = m_txSid,
        .txStopped = [this] {
          mx()->push([this] { senderStopped(); }, mx()->txThread());
        }}, m_error);
      if (m_backend && m_backend->ready() && m_backend->mtu() == m_mtu) {
        m_current = m_backend.ptr();
        m_state = Running;
        mx()->pluginStarted({});
        return;
      }
      if (!m_error) m_error = "interface geometry changed before packet startup";
      m_startFailure = true;
      m_state = Stopping;
      mx()->txRun([this] { stopTx(); });
    }
    
    void Stack::stop()
    {
      mx()->rxRun([this] { stopRx(); });
    }
    
    void Stack::stopRx()
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (m_state == Stopped) { mx()->pluginStopped({}); return; }
      m_state = Stopping;
      if (m_cxns) {
        m_endpointDrain = true;
        m_cxns->stop([this] { m_endpointDrain = false; stopEndpoints(); });
      } else stopEndpoints();
    }
    
    void Stack::stopEndpoints()
    {
      // Existing wake calls finish before Tx closes the backend's wait descriptor.
      // The closed instance itself stays retained until the stopped lifecycle ends.
      m_current = nullptr;
      __atomic_thread_fence(__ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); // publish the gate before observing users
      if (!m_routePending) {
        ZmAssert_(!cxnAdmission().total);
        mx()->txRun([this] { stopTx(); });
      }
    }
    
    void Stack::stopTx()
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->txThread()));

    Architecture review supports the chosen virtual boundary, but the following decisions should be resolved before implementation. These are proposed resolutions, not author approvals.
    
    1. **Blocker — Architecture / packet ownership: `net_ring` loopback conflicts with dedicated Rx backing.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:24–26,79–82`; `zxdp/INTERFACE.md:14,17–29`; `zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.cc:55–60`. The official ring PMD enqueues/dequeues original mbuf pointers and ignores its configured Rx mempool. Consequently, ordinary loopback returns Tx backing, which cannot safely be returned through the dedicated `rxPool`. [DPDK v25.11 ring implementation, lines 72–98 and 146–155](https://github.com/DPDK/dpdk/blob/v25.11/drivers/net/ring/rte_eth_ring.c#L72).
    **Mitigation:** Specify the ring test arrangement and ownership treatment explicitly. A fixture can consume transmitted mbufs and inject separately constructed Rx-pool packets; any fixture copy must be identified as test machinery. Do not silently copy in the production backend or treat Tx-origin pointers as Rx-pool allocations. Use PCAP input to independently exercise production Rx provisioning.
    
    2. **Blocker — Architecture / admission: the commit hook requires backend-owned reservation.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:35–39`; `zxdp/INTERFACE.md:35–45`; `zxdp/src/Zxdp.cc:378–394`. DPDK Tx burst can accept fewer packets than requested. Calling the hook immediately before burst therefore cannot guarantee acceptance. [Official ethdev API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    **Mitigation:** Define acceptance as reservation/publication into a bounded, preallocated backend submission queue, serviced by the existing scheduler sender slot. Reserve metadata and submission capacity before invoking the hook; retain unsent entries after a short burst. Define post-acceptance device failure through existing instance failure/close behavior. This adds internal provisioning derived from pool counts, without duplicate public sizing.
    
    3. **Blocker — Architecture / retirement: count-based cleanup is insufficient to identify packet leases.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:35–39,74–76`; `zxdp/src/Zxdp.cc:483–515`; `zxdp/src/ZxdpUMem.hh:38–43`. DPDK cleanup may be unsupported and reports counts, not packet identities. [Official ethdev API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    **Mitigation:** Choose a concrete direct-slot retirement mechanism, such as preallocated external-buffer shared-info callbacks, and assign its execution/thread ownership. DPDK invokes that callback when all attached mbufs detach. [Official mbuf API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api/rte__mbuf_8h.html). Keep the external-buffer submission lifetime distinct from the caller lease, so retained caller ownership does not prevent observing driver release. Specify how callback retirement reaches Tx-owned `pending`/active bookkeeping without cross-shard mutation. Test retirement with no further sends and no incoming traffic.
    
    4. **Major — Architecture / teardown: software queues require explicit draining.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:37,79–82`; `zxdp/src/Zxdp.cc:239–291`; `zxdp/src/Zxdp.hh:85–89`. The ring PMD close path frees owned ring storage without dequeuing and freeing its queued mbufs. [DPDK v25.11 ring close implementation](https://github.com/DPDK/dpdk/blob/v25.11/drivers/net/ring/rte_eth_ring.c#L267).
    **Mitigation:** Specify which component owns and drains each software ring before port/ring destruction. Close must separately resolve backend submission entries, PMD-held mbufs and fixture/peer-held mbufs. Preserve backing through final caller return; do not infer retirement from port closure. Include close with an undrained ring and repeated create/close in acceptance tests.
    
    5. **Major — Resource economics / idle receive: blocking cannot depend only on the wake eventfd.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:41–44`; `zxdp/INTERFACE.md:81–97`; `zxdp/src/Zxdp.cc:400–432`. Rx interrupts are optional in DPDK. [Official ethdev API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    **Mitigation:** Define the supported wait strategy for each initial PMD and its CPU cost. A wake-only indefinite wait prevents discovering subsequent packets. If a polling fallback is required, explicitly resolve its relationship to the spin-then-block contract and latency priorities. Test packet arrival after entering idle independently of explicit wake pulses; preserve counted wakes under continuous traffic.
    
    6. **Major — Resource economics / capacity: physical pool count and descriptor count need a sizing equation.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:24–26,43–44`; `zxdp/src/ZxdpUMem.cc:48–99`; `zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.hh:34–35`. Device descriptor limits can adjust requested counts. [Official descriptor adjustment API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    **Mitigation:** Derive descriptor counts and bounded mbuf/shared-info/submission metadata from the existing pool inputs. Document actual setup memory, headroom/alignment and minimum usable pool sizes. Distinguish descriptors from packet credits; reject unsatisfiable configurations during setup. Specify behavior when caller-held Rx packets exhaust the pool, and prevent driver caches from stranding all usable credits. No new public sizing fields are necessary.
    
    7. **Major — Architecture / abstraction completeness: virtualizing `Instance` leaves allocator coupling unresolved.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:9–13,30–33`; `zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.hh:60–70`; `zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.cc:19–29,51,59,83–90`; `zxdp/src/ZxdpUMem.cc:27–40`. `BufPool` depends directly on AF_XDP `UMem` layout and lease state. A derived DPDK instance alone cannot provide its storage semantics.
    **Mitigation:** Define the shared arena/slot lifetime boundary alongside the virtual instance boundary. Keep pool allocation/free and direct-slot writable queries allocation-free and constant-time; avoid a second unrelated allocator implementation. Also specify DPDK meanings for `ifindex()`, `zeroCopy()`, queue telemetry and `netmask`, which are currently tied to Linux link/BPF behavior.

    1. **Major — UX & Developer Ergonomics: failure and cleanup need one actionable workflow.**
    Evidence: `concepts_brief.md:46–49`; current `Zxdp.hh:55–57,85–89` distinguishes null creation failure, a non-ready handle retaining pending rollback, successful close, pending retirement, and close errors. Removing the error argument without defining its replacement leaves callers unable to diagnose failure or safely retain cleanup responsibility.

    # Zxdp AF_XDP and DPDK backends
    
    * **Author:** Huw Rogers
    * **Date:** 2026-11-16
    * **Status:** Working hypothesis; seven brainstorming lenses completed. Proposed resolutions below await design/readiness confirmation; no source implementation has begun.
    
    ## Overview
    
    Make `Zxdp::Instance` a virtual interface implemented by AF_XDP and DPDK.
    Remove the base class's `InstanceData *m_data`; make backend operations pure
    virtual. Add `ZtEnumNS(uint8_t, Backend, AF_XDP, DPDK)` and `Backend::T backend`
    to `Params`. Add the namespace factory `ZmRef<Instance> instance(const Params
    &params)`, which switches on `backend` and creates the corresponding derived
    instance. Use the merged AF_XDP implementation as the behavioral reference.
    
    Represent interface configuration with:
    
    ```cpp
    struct If_AF_XDP { unsigned index = 0; };
    struct If_DPDK { /* DPDK device selection; exact fields to be designed */ };
    ZuDerive(If, (ZuUnion<void, If_AF_XDP, If_DPDK>));
    ```
    
    `Params::interface` becomes `If interface = {}`. The caller supplies `txPools`
    and singular `rxPool`; these determine packet storage and ring provisioning.
    Do not duplicate that provisioning in `If_DPDK`.
    
    ## Analysis
    
    The objective is to let callers use AF_XDP or DPDK through the same raw-packet
    boundary while preserving the merged AF_XDP behavior. This is a backend extension,
    not a transport stack. The baseline contract is [zxdp/INTERFACE.md](zxdp/INTERFACE.md):
    separate caller and submission leases, a borrowed synchronous commit hook,
    scheduler sender service, counted receive wakes, queue telemetry and retryable
    shutdown. Backend-specific mechanisms may differ; these ownership guarantees may not.
    
    ### Confirmed decisions
    
    The author selected the virtual `Instance` boundary with no base `m_data`, pure
    virtual backend operations, the exact `Backend` enum and `Params::backend`, the
    one-argument namespace factory, and the tagged `If` representation above. Caller
    `txPools` and singular `rxPool` determine packet storage and ring provisioning.
    Software DPDK tests remain in scope. These choices are not reopened by the reviews.
    
    ### Proposed resolutions from the reviews
    
    These are recommendations, not additional author approvals. Blockers below block
    implementation readiness, not further brainstorming.
    
    1. **Admission — blocker.** Reserve capacity in a bounded, preallocated DPDK
       submission queue and acquire every required metadata credit before invoking
       `commit`. False cancels that reservation without a submission lease; true
       publishes unconditionally. Reuse the scheduler sender slot to pass accepted
       entries to the poll-mode driver (PMD), retaining unsent entries after a short
       burst. Service immediately without an intentional batching delay. A later
       device failure follows instance failure/close handling; it cannot turn an
       accepted send into a rejected send. DPDK burst admission can be partial, so
       placing the hook immediately before the driver call is insufficient.
       [DPDK ethdev API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    
    2. **Driver release — blocker.** Evaluate preallocated per-slot mbuf and external
       buffer shared information with a private release callback mapped directly to
       the slot. The callback indicates final detachment of driver-visible mbufs;
       caller ownership remains a separate lease. Publish release identity through
       a bounded preallocated handoff to the caller's Tx owner before changing its
       pending/active lists. `pollTx()` drains that handoff and counts retired
       submissions; `writable()` follows retirement, never enqueue success. Final
       caller return may run on any thread. The external-buffer API supports such
       callbacks, but supported PMDs, cleanup progress with no further traffic,
       DMA registration and callback contexts still require proof.
       [DPDK mbuf API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__mbuf_8h.html).
    
    3. **Shared backing — major.** Factor the smallest backend-neutral arena/slot
       lifetime component beneath the existing `BufPool`. Today it retains `UMem`
       and directly accesses its layout and `TxSlot`; a virtual instance alone does
       not remove this coupling ([ZxdpAlloc.hh](zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.hh),
       [ZxdpAlloc.cc](zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.cc)). Keep direct slot lookup, the existing
       payload-overlay recycling list and allocation-free packet operations. Keep
       XSK registration and DPDK registration private to each backend. Pool-held
       backing must survive instance close until the last caller packet returns.
       This needs no general allocator framework or second unrelated pool API.
    
    4. **Capacity — major.** Derive descriptor requests, submission credits and
       mbuf/shared-info metadata from existing pool counts and sizes. Validate the
       adjusted device limits, alignment/headroom and minimum useful Rx capacity at
       setup. Account for caller-held Rx packets and driver caches; distinguish
       descriptor capacity from packet credits. Reject unsatisfiable configurations
       with the selected device and offending pool constraint. Add no public ring
       sizing in `If_DPDK`.
    
    5. **Device/EAL lifecycle — major.** Prefer a named, already-created Ethernet
       device in `If_DPDK`. The application or test fixture initializes DPDK's
       process-wide Environment Abstraction Layer (EAL) and creates virtual devices;
       ordinary instance close must not tear down EAL or unrelated ports. Specify
       exclusive queue/port ownership during binding, release of resources configured
       by the instance, and reuse after close. Validate backend/tag mismatch, an unset
       interface and absent device once on the cold path. Keep arbitrary EAL arguments
       and PMD-specific tuning outside the selector.
    
    6. **Factory failure — major.** Preserve the exact one-argument factory. Retain
       the baseline distinction between null after completed rollback and a non-ready
       handle owning pending rollback. The owner retains that handle and schedules
       `close()` retries; it releases ownership only when retirement is complete.
       Recommend existing cold-path error logging for setup cause, backend/device,
       native operation and cleanup status, with runtime errors still surfaced by
       `close()`. The precise diagnostic convention and a minimal caller example must
       be settled before caller migration. Do not add a completion callback or silently
       discard a partially initialized instance ([current factory](zxdp/src/Zxdp.cc)).
    
    7. **Receive idle behavior — major, unresolved feasibility gate.** Preserve one
       Rx owner, counted preposted/concurrent wakes, prompt interruption under load,
       and return only for wake or device failure. PMD Rx interrupts are optional;
       indefinitely waiting on only the wake eventfd would miss subsequent packets.
       Prefer real packet-arrival notification where supported. For ring/pcap, select
       and validate an arrival mechanism or an explicitly described bounded polling
       fallback, including its idle CPU and latency cost and its relationship to the
       spin-then-block contract. Do not claim this resolved by a wake-only test.
       [DPDK Rx interrupt contract](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    
    ### Common API meanings to settle in the design
    
    Keep existing operations pure virtual; document backend results so callers do not
    need backend switches. This proposed matrix identifies the minimum semantic work.
    
    | Operation | AF_XDP reference | Proposed DPDK treatment / remaining detail |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `ifindex()` | Linux interface index | Return unavailable sentinel (proposed `0`) for software-only ports; never substitute a DPDK port ID. |
    | `mtu()`, `mac()` | Queried Linux link values | Use configured device values where meaningful; define software-port values and unavailable results before coding. |
    | `zeroCopy()` | Negotiated XSK mode | Specify an equally precise DPDK meaning; no physical DMA claim from ring/pcap results. |
    | `netmask` | Destination selection compiled into XDP | Preserve configured packet selection; choose a shared parser/software predicate or reject unsupported masks at setup. Never silently ignore them. |
    | `allQueues()` | Identified Rx/fill/Tx/CQ ring views, retained after close | Enumerate actual backend queues with documented units/final views; no fabricated hardware CQ or unsupported zero-valued statistic. |
    | `pollTx()` | Tx-owner CQ retirement count | Tx-owner drain of actual release records; sender consumption is a separate event. |
    | `stopSender()`, `close()` | FIFO sender barrier, safe retirement, retryable close | Quiesce producer/sender, resolve queued and PMD/peer-owned mbufs, retain final caller backing; no timeout-based reclamation. |
    
    Use existing queue views and cold diagnostics first. Additional owner-local
    counters or close-phase views are optional only when necessary to diagnose a
    specific test failure; a new tracing/observability subsystem is outside scope.
    
    ## Goals vs. Non-Goals
    
    * **In-Scope Goals:** Virtual Instance API; backend enum and namespace factory;
      tagged interface parameters; AF_XDP and DPDK implementations in zxdp; migration
      of affected callers; pool-driven provisioning; software DPDK tests; preservation
      of admission, ownership, service and shutdown contracts.
    * **Out-of-Scope Non-Goals:** A transport stack or application runtime; duplicate
      public ring sizing; compatibility shims; new sender threads; hot-path allocation,
      packet searches or payload staging; a general allocator or tracing framework;
      claims of physical NIC DMA, offload or wire-latency validation from software tests.
    
    ## Alternatives Weighed
    
    * **Rejected by author:** Separate ring configuration in `If_DPDK`; multiple
      `rxPools` (that spelling was a typo). Keep pool-driven provisioning and singular
      `rxPool`.
    * **Not recommended:** Hook immediately before `rte_eth_tx_burst()`; no reservation
      protects the no-refusal promise. A bounded internal admission queue adds metadata,
      one ownership phase and possible backpressure queueing, but preserves the contract
      without copying. Derive its capacity from pools.
    * **Not recommended:** Treat enqueue success, descriptor consumption, or a cleanup
      count as packet-specific retirement. The proposed direct-slot release callback
      avoids searches; costs include external-buffer metadata, registration constraints,
      a cross-owner handoff and a stronger teardown proof.
    * **Not recommended:** Duplicate the pool allocator or force DPDK through XDP page
      geometry. A narrow common storage/lease component preserves the existing invariant
      with less duplicated lifecycle logic.
    * **Receive alternatives still open:** PMD notification versus bounded polling.
      Notification needs driver support; polling trades idle CPU and arrival latency.
      The inventive lens found no false compromise requiring a different architecture.
    
    ## Key Decisions & Staging for Next Steps
    
    Confirmed decisions are listed above. All new resolutions remain proposals;
    Goldfish completion is not author approval or implementation readiness.
    
    1. **Contract and feasibility:** Specify the API matrix, factory diagnostic
       workflow, named-device/EAL ownership, capacity equations and per-PMD Rx wait
       strategy. Prove the direct-slot release mechanism and no-traffic cleanup for
       the initial supported PMDs. Record producer, sender, Rx and retirement owners.
    2. **AF_XDP first:** Introduce the virtual boundary, enum, tagged parameters,
       namespace factory and shared backing seam together with every affected caller.
       Preserve AF_XDP behavior before adding DPDK. Search all factory/interface users,
       including Zutcp, zxdp utility/unit/integration tests and Zutcp pool integration.
       Propagate the intentional API/ABI break without shims and rebuild dependents.
    3. **DPDK implementation:** Add the narrow selector and pool-derived resources,
       admission/service path, retirement handoff and retryable teardown. Add the
       dependency through repository configure/pkg-config conventions. Keep existing
       scheduler ownership and bounded service turns.
    4. **Shared contract validation:** Reuse admission, ownership and lifecycle cases
       across backends. Test rejected send and hook cancellation; caller return before
       and after driver release; retained packet mutation/retransmission after retirement;
       no-traffic completion; Rx exhaustion; preposted/continuous-traffic/wait-transition
       wakes; packet arrival after idle; failed setup with rollback pending; two instances;
       and repeated close/recreate with shared EAL. Build/test according to
       [docs/BUILD.md](docs/BUILD.md), keeping environment-dependent cases in `itest`.
    
    ### Software fixture boundary
    
    Use `net_ring` for controlled in-process mbuf transport/ownership and `net_pcap`
    for deterministic capture input/output. A normal ring loopback exchanges original
    mbuf pointers and ignores its configured Rx mempool; therefore Tx-origin backing
    cannot be returned through the dedicated `rxPool`. Prefer a controlled peer that
    consumes/releases Tx mbufs and separately injects Rx-origin packets, plus PCAP
    input for independent Rx-provisioning coverage. Any fixture copy is test machinery,
    not production payload staging. Explicitly drain queued mbufs before ring destruction;
    the v25.11 ring close path does not do this for the fixture.
    [Official ring source](https://github.com/DPDK/dpdk/blob/v25.11/drivers/net/ring/rte_eth_ring.c).
    
    Distinguish accepted, peer-dequeued and peer-released states; packet equality alone
    does not prove retirement. Record tested DPDK version/PMDs. Physical hardware
    validation remains separate. [Ring guide](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/nics/ring.html),
    [PCAP guide](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.03/nics/pcap_ring.html),
    [EAL parameters](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/linux_gsg/linux_eal_parameters.html),
    [local testing context](dpdk_loopback.md).

All seven Goldfish reviews completed. Updated the [concepts brief](/home/count0/src/z/concepts_brief.md) with findings and proposed resolutions.

The main issues are:

- Reserve submission capacity before invoking the commit hook.
- Track actual per-packet driver release before recycling backing.
- Account for `net_ring` returning Tx-origin buffers instead of dedicated Rx backing.

The proposals preserve your API choices and pool-driven provisioning. Factory diagnostics and idle receive behavior still need design decisions. No source code changed.

Which objections or proposed resolutions would you like to refine?

## User

note: zpicotls has been updated and installed on this local system

explain "commit hook"

## Assistant

The **commit hook** is the optional `CommitFn` already present in the merged API:

```cpp
bool send(uint8_t *packet, unsigned length, const CommitFn &commit = {});
```

It lets the caller publish its own state immediately before the packet becomes visible to the device—for example, recording that a TCP segment is outstanding before a peer can acknowledge it.

The sequence is:

1. Zxdp checks the packet and reserves submission capacity.
2. It calls `commit()`.
3. If the hook returns `false`, Zxdp cancels admission without acquiring a submission lease.
4. If it returns `true`, Zxdp publishes the submission with no further refusal.

The hook runs synchronously inside `send()`. It is optional and is not a transmit-completion callback.

The DPDK concern is that `rte_eth_tx_burst()` can accept fewer packets than requested. A reserved internal queue would let Zxdp honor the hook’s promise while retrying driver submission afterward.

Noted that the updated zpicotls is installed locally.

## User

why does `zxdp` need that? why can't the caller just run the commit block before calling send?

## Assistant

Because `send()` can reject the packet when submission capacity is exhausted.

Running the block first would publish caller state for a packet that might never be submitted. The caller would then need to undo that state, potentially after another thread had observed it.

Running the block after a successful `send()` has the opposite race: the device could transmit and a peer could respond before the caller records the submission.

The hook places the caller’s state update **after admission is guaranteed, but before packet publication**.

It isn’t essential to raw packet I/O. It supports callers that need this ordering. A separate reserve/commit API could provide the same guarantee, with more public API and explicit reservation ownership.

## User

what's the DPDK issue with send and `commitFn`?

## Assistant

AF_XDP lets Zxdp reserve a descriptor **before** calling `commitFn`. Once the hook returns true, publishing that descriptor cannot fail.

DPDK’s `rte_eth_tx_burst()` combines admission and submission. Even for one packet, it may return `0` because the queue is full. It offers no equivalent portable reservation step. [DPDK API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html)

That leaves an ordering problem:

- Call `commitFn` first: it may commit caller state, then DPDK refuses the packet.
- Submit first: the packet may become visible before caller state is committed.

The proposed internal queue resolves this by reserving its capacity before the hook. After true, Zxdp accepts responsibility for the packet and retries DPDK submission as needed. That preserves the existing contract, at the cost of another bounded queue.

## User

could `zutcp` be modified to use a `bool send(..)` where the return indicates success/failure?

## Assistant

I’ll check where Zutcp uses the hook and whether it can safely move that work around a plain `bool send()`.

    the logger thread and keep metadata capture inside `ZutcpLOG`. Unknown/removed
    frame types fail admission and produce a packet-drop event. Close output may
    piggyback a pending ACK without waiting for its delay timer.
    
    Initial token framing, Retry bootstrap/parameter state and the `NEW_TOKEN` and
    `HANDSHAKE_DONE` facilities are removed. Payload length follows the CIDs directly
    in the Initial header; do not restore a token-taking writer overload or a
    confirmation-control slot. Bootstrap still creates its routing CIDs, without
    generating reset tokens. Reset-token transport parameters, their codec and
    parameter-event logging are removed. The separate reset-token and path-challenge types, CID rotation controls/tables,
    migration APIs/settings/diagnostics, candidate-path state/timers and endpoint
    rebinding are removed. Bootstrap routing uses the fixed local CID plus the
    original destination CID, with bounded router tombstones. The server records its
    peer tuple on Rx at successful bootstrap and drops packets from other tuples
    before packet admission. Tx keeps its own peer destination. Preserve ordinary
    MTU, ECN and initial send-budget accounting. Opening that initial budget on
    establishment does not create a candidate path or validation exchange.
    Native endpoint wiring is implemented; complete the remaining ownership,
    admission/control and owner/race gates. The copied migration guidance below is
    historical.
    Keep Zi types, adapter state and mx scheduler integration in Zutcp. Zxdp owns
    its required configurable spin-before-epoll `rx()` and interrupting `wake()`.
    Delegate the plugin hooks to that pair; use the raw named-parameter pool/callback
    interface in the updated plan.
    Stack owns native local address/port membership on Rx. Bind/unbind there; dispatch
    validates TCP integrity and advances the original registered Rx view without
    copying payload or taking an endpoint reference. Remove membership before draining
    the endpoint's raw callbacks. `Stack::resolvePath` uses an existing mx worker
    outside Rx/Tx and posts completion to Rx. Native setup must provide that worker,
    drain every accepted setup callback and fence its generation before owner release.
    Stack stop waits for pending setup before the Tx/backend drain. No blocking route
    lookup or independent protocol owner thread belongs on the packet path.
    
    Reuse Clang/debug/ASan for development and acceptance with leak detection enabled.
    Apply `../REBUILD.md` dependency order, freezes, batching and build reuse with the
    author's ASan override; avoid unnecessary clean builds. Separate optional release
    profiling and any non-ASan Memcheck build from the active development tree.
    
    # zutcp supplementary guidelines
    
    These guidelines are the audit checklist for code changes in `zutcp`.  They
    supplement the repo-wide rules in `../GUIDELINES.md`; follow both when editing
    or reviewing `zutcp` code.  Implementation discovery and source navigation live
    in `README.md`.
    
    # General zutcp
    
    - Keep QUIC runtime work on the owning Rx or Tx thread.  Do not add locks to
      make non-owner access convenient.
    - Keep protocol state changes close to the RFC mechanism they implement.
      Cross-thread entry points should snapshot only destination-owned metadata and
      immediately post to the owning thread.
    - Use existing `Zutcp` protocol enums, fixed-size protocol values, Z socket
      address types, and module-local helpers before adding ad hoc string or STL
      representations.
    - Debug text logging is unrelated to qlog.  Use `ZiLOG(Debug, ...)` for debug
      text and keep qlog instrumentation behind `ZutcpLOG`.
    
    # Buffers
    
    `Zutcp` exposes UDP packet allocator classes and ordinary plaintext allocation aliases through
    `Zutcp.hh`. Keep those roles distinct:
    
    - `PktRxBufAllocator` defaults to the `"Zutcp.Pkt.Rx"` heap for received UDP
      datagrams and in-place QUIC packet protection removal. Configure it through
      `ZiMultiplex::allocator` registration and the UDP call's receive allocator;
      the endpoint receives the original `io.buf`.
    - `PktTxBufAllocator` defaults to the `"Zutcp.Pkt.Tx"` heap for transmit
      packetization and packet protection output. Each endpoint retains its own
      allocator; active output belongs to `ZiTxContext::buf` until kernel retirement.
    - `StreamTxBufAlloc` defaults to the `"Zutcp.Stream.TxBuf"` heap for
      application stream bytes that must be retained for ACK, loss,
      retransmission, reset, cancellation, or teardown handling.
    - `CryptoRxBufAlloc` defaults to the `"Zutcp.Crypto.RxBuf"` heap for retained
      CRYPTO receive fragments.
    - `CryptoTxBufAlloc` defaults to the `"Zutcp.Crypto.TxBuf"` heap for TLS
      output staged for QUIC CRYPTO frame packetization.
    
    Completed transmit datagrams use `Zutcp_::TxPkt`, an intrinsic `ZiTxBuf`
    node with destination address and ECN metadata. Rx and retained plaintext buffers
    remain separate metadata types. The mx factory selects TxUDP backing; no builtin
    backing assumption is permitted. Packet protection writes directly into the
    provider's writable span with its original headroom and tailroom.
    
    Each physical `EndpointCxn` owns its common `ZiTx` queue on mx Tx. Its 4096-packet
    capacity includes the installed active head. Reject full-queue submissions before
    counting submitted bytes, recording both backpressure and a local drop. Posted
    submissions may acknowledge posting before rejection; QUIC recovery still owns
    retained plaintext and packet records above this boundary. Priority admission
    inserts immediately after the active head, newest priority first among pending
    packets. Ordinary submissions remain FIFO. Address and ECN stay immutable while
    queued and are installed afresh for every selected head.
    
    Posted output snapshots only raw physical identity and generation. Compare that
    identity on Tx without dereferencing or retaining the old connection; obtain the
    current connection locally at admission. Existing endpoint owner-drain rules
    protect the raw endpoint callback. Do not add per-packet owner references.
    
    When a protocol ACK opens congestion credit, service the existing bounded retained
    retransmission batch before ordinary producers. Fresh bulk output must not spend
    all reopened credit before deferred recovery runs. Socket completion reports one
    local datagram and byte count, without ACK,
    recovery retirement or producer notification. EAGAIN retains the same protected
    packet. Bind posted output to its original physical connection; reject stale
    submissions after rebind rather than routing them through a replacement. Closing
    prevents admission; physical disconnect and Tx owner drain precede context and
    queue retirement. Backend-held backing remains the backend's responsibility until
    its retirement. ZiTx advances queued output in the common completion turn rather
    than posting the former per-packet scheduler continuation; pacing remains above
    this queue. Measure bounded-drain latency when changing the capacity.
    
    `BufSize` is `1472`.  It is packet-buffer capacity, not the active UDP payload
    limit.  The active path payload starts at the QUIC minimum and is raised only by
    PMTUD/DPLPMTUD success.
    
    Transmit packet protection is source-to-destination.  Retained plaintext
    stream/control byte ranges are gathered as read-only inputs and encrypted
    directly into the final Tx packet buffer.  Do not add an intermediate
    ciphertext staging buffer.
    
    Receive packet protection decrypts in place in the Rx packet buffer.  STREAM
    receive data is represented by retained slices of that decrypted packet buffer:
    `StreamRxData` carries both a `ZmRef<ZiIOBuf>` to the packet and the payload
    span.  Frame-processing APIs that accept STREAM payload must require the packet
    reference; do not add a frame-only STREAM copy fallback.
    
    CRYPTO receive is different from STREAM receive.  Fragmented or out-of-order
    CRYPTO data may be copied into retained `CryptoRxBufAlloc` buffers for
    reassembly.  In-order CRYPTO delivery and TLS output should use direct
    spans/origin-backed buffers when possible.
    
    Cross-shard STREAM sends transfer an owned range or construct directly in the
    stream writer's retained buffers. Do not stage bytes in an asynchronous byte
    array before copying them into stream storage. TLS output already has a
    `CryptoTxBufAlloc` owner: transfer it through the CRYPTO send callback and retain
    its ranges for retransmission until the existing epoch/reset teardown retires
    them. Packet protection reads those ranges directly into final UDP output.
    
    Hidden fallback copies below the public API boundary are forbidden.  Any new
    copy path must be documented in this section and covered by a test that explains
    why the copy is required.
    
    # Recovery and handshake confirmation
    
    PTO reclamation selects the oldest eligible retained packets. Newly emitted
    retransmissions must not indefinitely displace older STREAM or control work.
    Use the existing recovery references and ACK retirement for HANDSHAKE_DONE;
    do not add a separate completion timer or retry queue.
    
    A PTO services its selected packet-number space. When another space has data
    in flight and transmit keys, leave room for an acknowledgment-eliciting probe
    there within the two-datagram budget (RFC 9002 section 6.2.4). A successful
    Handshake retransmission must not suppress all outstanding 1-RTT probes. A
    failed primary send does not authorize an unrelated substitute. Application
    Data does not independently select PTO before handshake confirmation.
    Candidate path proof retains priority over ordinary recovery for both active
    client migration and passive server rebinding.
    
    Server confirmation occurs at TLS completion; client confirmation occurs on
    HANDSHAKE_DONE. Retire the actual Handshake secrets on Rx and the independent
    Tx protector/recovery state on Tx. Defer server Rx retirement until its current
    CRYPTO delivery callback unwinds. Late crypto and ACK snapshots must not
    repopulate a retired packet-number space. Initial-key storage has a separate
    existing cross-owner read and is not changed by the Handshake retirement repair.
    
    # qlog
    
    ## Contract
    
    `ZutcpLOG` is the source marker for qlog-only runtime instrumentation.  It must
    make qlog work obvious during review and erase qlog-only work from release
    builds.
    
    Use the same split as `ZiLog` / `ZiLOG`:
    
    - `ZutcpLOG(...)` is the macro used at call sites.
    - `ZutcpLog(...)` is the function called by the macro in debug builds.
    - `ZutcpLogger` owns the qlog writer thread, ring, diagnostics, JSON helpers,
      and file output.
    
    Do not add `Zutcp_LOG*`, `Zutcp_DEBUG_LOG*`, or additional `ZutcpLOG*` macros.
    
    `Zutcp_DEBUG` is the controlling conditional compile for qlog code.  Release
    build verification must use `z.config`, then top-level `make clean`, then
    top-level `make -j8`; do not validate release behavior with partial
    subdirectory rebuilds.
    
    Qlog file output should follow the `ZiLog` file-sink precedent: when a qlog
    path already exists, age it through the configured archive depth before opening
    the new log file.  Automated tests must place qlogs in a `ZiTestResidue`-owned
    directory family so successful runs remove them and failed runs retain them.
    
    ## Lifecycle and gating
    
    `ZutcpLogger` is a `ZmSingleton` process-wide singleton.  The owning app
    initializes it under main-thread control, early and once, from qlog parameters
    during application `init`; it finalizes the logger after protocol app machinery
    is drained and all activity has ceased during application `final`.
    
    After initialization, `ZutcpLogger::enabled()` is the single runtime
    availability check for qlog.  Call sites and helpers should not separately
    consult the owning app's qlog params.
    
    No qlog-only expression may be evaluated in release builds.  No qlog-only
    expression may be evaluated in debug builds when qlog is disabled by
    configuration.  `ZutcpLOG` must check the runtime enabled flag before
    evaluating its argument, just as `ZiLOG` filters severity before posting to the
    logger thread.
    
    ## Call-site shape
    
    All qlog-only work belongs inside the `ZutcpLOG` argument, usually in lambda
    capture initializers or in the lambda body.  This includes:
    
    - reading runtime counters only used for qlog;
    - reading congestion, recovery, path, CID, stream, TLS, or packet metadata only
      used for qlog;
    - converting enums or times into qlog strings/units;
    - building qlog event structs;
    - counting qlog frames or ACK ranges;
    - copying qlog-only strings, owned `ZeString` values, or arrays;
    - calling qlog JSON helper functions.
    
    Correct pattern:
    
    ```c++
    ZutcpLOG(([
      space,
      pn,
      bytes,
      bytesInFlight = m_congestion.bytesInFlight(),
      latestRTT = m_rtt.latest()
    ](auto &o, ZuTime time) mutable {
      PktEvent event{
        .packetSpace = space,
        .packetNumber = pn,
        .packetSize = bytes,
        .bytesInFlight = bytesInFlight,
        .latestRTTUS = uint64_t(latestRTT.microsecs())
      };
      o.logPktSent(event, time);
    }));
    ```
    
    Incorrect pattern:
    
    ```c++
    uint64_t bytesInFlight = m_congestion.bytesInFlight();
    PktEvent event;
    event.packetSpace = space;
    ZutcpLOG(([event, bytesInFlight](auto &o, ZuTime time) mutable {
      o.logPktSent(event, time);
    }));
    ```
    
    The incorrect form leaves qlog-only reads and event construction in the hot
    path even when qlog compiles out.
    
    Do not add qlog-specific branches outside `ZutcpLOG` unless they also affect
    normal protocol behavior.  If an event should be skipped because it is empty,
    put the skip inside the macro when the skip is qlog-only:
    
    ```c++
    ZutcpLOG(([
      ackedBytes = update.ackdBytes,
      ...
    ](auto &o, ZuTime time) {
      if (!ackedBytes) return;
      ...
    }));
    ```
    
    If the branch is protocol logic already needed without qlog, keep it outside:
    
    ```c++
    if (!update.ackdBytes) return;   // protocol/recovery path already needs this
    ZutcpLOG(([...](auto &o, ZuTime time) { ... }));
    ```
    
    ## Captures and threading
    
    Capture by value only.  The lambda is moved through the inter-thread ring and
    executes later on the qlog thread.
    
    Allowed captures:
    
    - scalar IDs, packet numbers, sizes, timestamps, enum values, flags, counters;
    - small fixed-size or bounded qlog snapshots;
    - Z value types whose copy cost and lifetime are explicitly acceptable;
    - qlog frame summaries after they have been reduced to bounded metadata;
    - `ZeString` values only for genuinely arbitrary string data that must cross
      the async boundary.
    
    Do not capture:
    
    - references;
    - raw packet or stream payload buffers;
    - mutable runtime state;
    - `this`, `impl()`, `app()`, stream objects, path objects, congestion objects,
      or crypto objects;
    - secrets, plaintext, key material, tokens, or unbounded application data.
    
    The hot-path thread should only:
    
    - evaluate capture initializers in debug builds after `ZutcpLOG` has confirmed
      qlog is enabled;
    - move the lambda by value into the qlog ring;
    - update qlog enqueue/drop diagnostics.
    
    The qlog thread should do as much as possible:
    
    - construct qlog-specific structs from captured values;
    - map enum names through `ZtEnumMap` and qlog field names through `ZfStruct`
      metadata;
    - use `ZfJSON` / `ZfStruct` mappings;
    - write JSON-SEQ records;
    - perform bounded formatting.
    
    Do not format JSON, allocate scratch JSON strings, or walk runtime-owned
    containers on Rx/Tx I/O threads.
    
    ## Data modeling and JSON
    
    Most qlog fields are not arbitrary strings.  QUIC protocol data is normally
    fixed-size scalar data, IP address/port data, protocol IDs, error codes,
    enumerations, or other closed vocabularies.  Short string literals used in the
    code for qlog reasons, triggers, actions, states, packet labels, or frame
    labels should be modeled as enum values, aligning with system error-code style
    classification.  Do not capture those literals as strings.
    
    If a value is an enumeration or closed vocabulary, keep it as an enum and use a
    `ZtEnumMap` with `ZfStruct` / `ZfJSON`.  The JSON string conversion belongs on
    the logger thread, during `ZfJSON` serialization:
    
    ```c++
    ZtEnum(TheEnum, int8_t, Value0, Value1);
    ZtEnumMap(TheEnum, JSON, "value_0", "value_1");
    ZfStruct(, (TheStruct, JSON),
      (enum_, (Ctor<...>, Enum<TheEnum::JSON>),    Int8));
    ```
    
    Do not translate enums to strings in helper functions just to feed those
    strings back into `ZfJSON`.
    
    Use existing Z framework printing and JSON facilities for Z network value
    types.  `ZiIP` already knows how to print itself, and qlog endpoint/address
    JSON should be expressed as `ZfJSON` / `ZfStruct` mappings over `ZiIP`,
    `ZiSockAddr`, ports, and enum/scalar fields.  Do not add qlog-local IP address
    formatters, byte shifting, `{data(), length()}` span reconstruction, or string
    parsing helpers for functionality the Z types already provide.
    
    Do not capture `ZuCSpan` for arbitrary string data unless it points at static
    storage that will outlive the logger thread.  If the data is genuinely
    arbitrary or detailed at run time, capture it as an owning `ZeString` and move
    it into the event on the qlog thread:
    
    ```c++
    ZutcpLOG(([
      foo = ZeString{fooSpan},
      bar = int64_t(value)
    ](auto &o, ZuTime time) mutable {
      QLogBaz event{
        .foo = ZuMv(foo),
        .bar = bar
      };
      o.logBaz(ZuMv(event), time);
    }));
    ```
    
    ## Event construction and schema
    
    Build qlog event structs inside the lambda body from captured values:
    
    ```c++
    ZutcpLOG(([
      action,
      reason,
      mtu = m_path.activeMaxUDP(),
      antiAmplification = m_path.antiAmplificationRemaining(),
      validated = pathValidated_()
    ](auto &o, ZuTime time) {
      PathEvent event{
        .action = action,
        .reason = reason,
        .mtu = mtu,
        .antiAmplification = antiAmplification,
        .validated = validated
      };
      o.logPathUpdated(event, time);
    }));
    ```
    
    Qlog event types should be plain data structs with fields that can be
    initialized directly from captured values.  Prefer aggregate/member
    initialization over default construction followed by assignment:
    
    ```c++
    PathEvent event{
      .action = action,
      .reason = reason,
      .mtu = mtu,
      .validated = validated
    };
    ```
    
    Avoid this pattern unless there is a real dependency between assignments:
    
    ```c++
    PathEvent event;
    event.action = action;
    event.reason = reason;
    event.mtu = mtu;
    event.validated = validated;
    ```
    
    Default construction can needlessly zero-initialize or default-construct fields
    that are immediately overwritten.  Keep the data structs simple enough that
    call sites and writer helpers can initialize only the emitted fields.
    
    Prefer typed event fields over string fields.  If a value is derived at run
    time, first model it as a scalar, fixed-size value, error code, or enum with
    `ZtEnumMap`.  Qlog event names are closed vocabulary values: model them as a
    `ZtEnumMap`-backed enum and serialize them through `ZfJSON`; do not pass qlog
    event names around as `ZuCSpan`, `ZeString`, or string literals outside the
    enum map.  Event string fields must own their data only when the string is
    genuinely arbitrary free-form text; in that rare case use `ZeString`, move it
    into the event with `ZuMv`, and let the logger thread serialize from owned
    data.  Use borrowed `ZuCSpan` only for static non-event literals with process
    lifetime.
    
    Event names and field shapes must track the current qlog draft schema for
    `quic:*` events.  When an event or field extends beyond that schema, align it
    with mainstream reference implementation precedent where one exists, such as
    mvfst's `quic:path_validated` extension event and its `success` / `vantage`
    payload shape.  Reference precedent covers both the event name and the data
    fields; do not add zutcp-specific detail fields to a reference-backed `quic:*`
    extension event unless the reference implementation does the same.  If no
    clear reference precedent exists, keep the event or field under the private
    zutcp schema instead of presenting it as standard QUIC qlog output.
    
    For packet/frame summaries, reduce payload data to bounded metadata only:
    
    - frame type;
    - stream id, offset, length, FIN;
    - ACK largest/ranges/counts/delay;
    - crypto offset and length;
    - close error code and redacted/length-limited reason metadata;
    - CID sequence/length/reset-token presence;
    - path challenge/response presence and length, not challenge bytes.
    
    Do not log payload bytes or key material.
    
    ## Helpers and exceptions
    
    Helpers are encouraged, but they must preserve the compile-out rule.
    
    Good helpers:
    
    - logger-thread helpers called from inside the `ZutcpLOG` lambda;
    - pure qlog conversion helpers used only inside `ZutcpLOG`;
    - bounded event writers that take already-captured scalar metadata;
    - JSON serialization helpers using `ZfJSON` / `ZfStruct`.
    
    Bad helpers:
    
    - hot-path wrappers such as `qlogFoo_()` that hide qlog work behind a normal
      function call;
    - helpers that read runtime state before entering `ZutcpLOG`;
    - helpers that build qlog event structs before entering `ZutcpLOG`;
    - helpers that use `ZutcpLogger::enabled()` to guard qlog work in normal code.
    
    `ZutcpLogger::enabled()` is acceptable for lifecycle checks and tests, but it
    is not the hot-path instrumentation pattern.  Hot-path instrumentation should
    use `ZutcpLOG`.
    
    Use `ZutcpLogger::enabled()` only for qlog state that must be accumulated
    synchronously on the protocol thread before a later `ZutcpLOG` writer-thread
    post.  The main case is packet receive frame summaries: frame metadata is only
    available while parsing frames, but the final packet event is posted after the
    packet is accepted.  `ZutcpLogger::enabled()` must be conditionally compiled:
    in `Zutcp_DEBUG` builds it performs the qlog runtime-enabled check, and in
    non-debug builds it is a `constexpr false` stub.  In this narrow case,
    construct the accumulator only inside the enabled branch, use
    `ZuUnion<void, T>` so disabled qlog does not default-construct qlog state and
    the union manages destruction, and keep the accumulated data bounded and
    payload-free.
    
    ## Review checklist
    
    For every qlog call site, verify:
    
    - the visible marker is `ZutcpLOG`;
    - qlog-only reads and temporaries are inside capture initializers;
    - qlog-only conversions and struct construction are inside the lambda body;
    - qlog event structs use direct aggregate/member initialization where possible;
    - captures are by value and bounded;
    - no references, runtime owner pointers, packet payloads, or secrets escape to
      the qlog thread;
    - JSON output uses `ZfJSON` / `ZfStruct`;
    - release builds erase the qlog-only code at preprocessing time;
    - the hot path does not do qlog formatting or JSON serialization.
    
    Short-header key trials preserve ciphertext in scratch until authentication
    succeeds, then copy authenticated plaintext back into the original packet. This
    copy permits old/next-key retry after a failed authentication; STREAM slices
    still retain the original packet backing.

    // Tx publishes monotonic frontiers; Rx reads without scheduling mirror updates.
    // Reset invalidates the epoch before publishing any replacement values.
    struct alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) TxReadView {
      ZmAtomic<uint64_t> gen{U64Null}, next{0}, ack{0}, sentAck{0}, synEnd{U64Null};
    
      void reset(uint64_t generation) {
        gen = U64Null;
        next = 0; ack = 0; sentAck = 0; synEnd = U64Null;
        gen = generation;
      }
      bool read(uint64_t generation, uint64_t &next_, uint64_t &ack_, uint64_t &sent_) const {
        if (uint64_t(gen) != generation) return false;
        ack_ = ack;
        next_ = next;
        sent_ = sentAck;
        return uint64_t(gen) == generation && ack_ <= next_;
      }
    };

      ZmAtomic<uint64_t> gen{U64Null}, version{0}, seqAck{0}, detail{0};
    
      void reset(uint64_t generation) {
        gen = U64Null;
        version = 0; seqAck = 0; detail = 0;
        gen = generation;
      }

## Assistant

**Yes, Zutcp could use a plain `bool send(...)`, but its receive-side validation would need to change.**

Currently the hook publishes the transmitted sequence frontier before packet submission. The concurrent Rx thread reads that frontier and rejects ACKs beyond it. See [publication](/home/count0/src/z/zutcp/src/ZutcpConnection.hh:4300) and [ACK validation](/home/count0/src/z/zutcp/src/ZutcpConnection.hh:4092).

Simply moving publication after `send()` returns true creates this race:

1. The device transmits.
2. Rx receives an immediate ACK.
3. Rx rejects it because Tx has not yet published the new frontier.

A possible redesign is to pass ACK information to the Tx owner and validate it there, after the current send finishes. Zutcp already completes much of its recovery bookkeeping after successful submission. Handshake validation and other Rx reads of transmitted state would also need examination.

Then the sequence becomes:

```cpp
if (!send(packet, length)) return false;
publishTxCommit(...);
finishRecoveryBookkeeping(...);
```

So the hook is required by **Zutcp’s current cross-thread publication scheme**, rather than inherently by packet I/O. Changing that scheme could simplify Zxdp and avoid adding a DPDK submission queue solely to support `commitFn`.

## User

`zutcp` does not need to reject ACKs beyond a frontier, it just needs to mark those bytes as acknowledged. we don't care about validating incoming ACKs in that way

## Assistant

I’ll update the brief to remove frontier-based ACK rejection as a requirement and replace the commit hook with a plain success/failure send contract. Zutcp can then record successful sends on its Tx owner before processing queued ACK work.

    ## Analysis
    
    The objective is to let callers use AF_XDP or DPDK through the same raw-packet
    boundary while preserving the merged AF_XDP behavior. This is a backend extension,
    not a transport stack. The baseline contract is [zxdp/INTERFACE.md](zxdp/INTERFACE.md):
    separate caller and submission leases, a borrowed synchronous commit hook,
    scheduler sender service, counted receive wakes, queue telemetry and retryable
    shutdown. Backend-specific mechanisms may differ; these ownership guarantees may not.
    
    ### Confirmed decisions
    
    The author selected the virtual `Instance` boundary with no base `m_data`, pure
    virtual backend operations, the exact `Backend` enum and `Params::backend`, the
    one-argument namespace factory, and the tagged `If` representation above. Caller
    `txPools` and singular `rxPool` determine packet storage and ring provisioning.
    Software DPDK tests remain in scope. These choices are not reopened by the reviews.
    
    ### Proposed resolutions from the reviews
    
    These are recommendations, not additional author approvals. Blockers below block
    implementation readiness, not further brainstorming.
    
    1. **Admission — blocker.** Reserve capacity in a bounded, preallocated DPDK
       submission queue and acquire every required metadata credit before invoking
       `commit`. False cancels that reservation without a submission lease; true
       publishes unconditionally. Reuse the scheduler sender slot to pass accepted
       entries to the poll-mode driver (PMD), retaining unsent entries after a short
       burst. Service immediately without an intentional batching delay. A later
       device failure follows instance failure/close handling; it cannot turn an
       accepted send into a rejected send. DPDK burst admission can be partial, so
       placing the hook immediately before the driver call is insufficient.
       [DPDK ethdev API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    
    2. **Driver release — blocker.** Evaluate preallocated per-slot mbuf and external
       buffer shared information with a private release callback mapped directly to
       the slot. The callback indicates final detachment of driver-visible mbufs;
       caller ownership remains a separate lease. Publish release identity through
       a bounded preallocated handoff to the caller's Tx owner before changing its
       pending/active lists. `pollTx()` drains that handoff and counts retired
       submissions; `writable()` follows retirement, never enqueue success. Final
       caller return may run on any thread. The external-buffer API supports such
       callbacks, but supported PMDs, cleanup progress with no further traffic,
       DMA registration and callback contexts still require proof.
       [DPDK mbuf API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__mbuf_8h.html).
    
    3. **Shared backing — major.** Factor the smallest backend-neutral arena/slot
       lifetime component beneath the existing `BufPool`. Today it retains `UMem`
       and directly accesses its layout and `TxSlot`; a virtual instance alone does
       not remove this coupling ([ZxdpAlloc.hh](zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.hh),
       [ZxdpAlloc.cc](zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.cc)). Keep direct slot lookup, the existing
       payload-overlay recycling list and allocation-free packet operations. Keep
       XSK registration and DPDK registration private to each backend. Pool-held
       backing must survive instance close until the last caller packet returns.
       This needs no general allocator framework or second unrelated pool API.
    
    4. **Capacity — major.** Derive descriptor requests, submission credits and
       mbuf/shared-info metadata from existing pool counts and sizes. Validate the
       adjusted device limits, alignment/headroom and minimum useful Rx capacity at
    
    * **In-Scope Goals:** Virtual Instance API; backend enum and namespace factory;
      tagged interface parameters; AF_XDP and DPDK implementations in zxdp; migration
      of affected callers; pool-driven provisioning; software DPDK tests; preservation
      of admission, ownership, service and shutdown contracts.
    * **Out-of-Scope Non-Goals:** A transport stack or application runtime; duplicate
      public ring sizing; compatibility shims; new sender threads; hot-path allocation,
      packet searches or payload staging; a general allocator or tracing framework;
      claims of physical NIC DMA, offload or wire-latency validation from software tests.
    
    ## Alternatives Weighed
    
    * **Rejected by author:** Separate ring configuration in `If_DPDK`; multiple
      `rxPools` (that spelling was a typo). Keep pool-driven provisioning and singular
      `rxPool`.
    * **Not recommended:** Hook immediately before `rte_eth_tx_burst()`; no reservation
      protects the no-refusal promise. A bounded internal admission queue adds metadata,
      one ownership phase and possible backpressure queueing, but preserves the contract
      without copying. Derive its capacity from pools.
    * **Not recommended:** Treat enqueue success, descriptor consumption, or a cleanup
      count as packet-specific retirement. The proposed direct-slot release callback
      avoids searches; costs include external-buffer metadata, registration constraints,
      a cross-owner handoff and a stronger teardown proof.
    * **Not recommended:** Duplicate the pool allocator or force DPDK through XDP page
      geometry. A narrow common storage/lease component preserves the existing invariant
      with less duplicated lifecycle logic.
    * **Receive alternatives still open:** PMD notification versus bounded polling.
      Notification needs driver support; polling trades idle CPU and arrival latency.
      The inventive lens found no false compromise requiring a different architecture.
    
    ## Key Decisions & Staging for Next Steps
    
    Confirmed decisions are listed above. All new resolutions remain proposals;
    Goldfish completion is not author approval or implementation readiness.
    
    1. **Contract and feasibility:** Specify the API matrix, factory diagnostic
       workflow, named-device/EAL ownership, capacity equations and per-PMD Rx wait
       strategy. Prove the direct-slot release mechanism and no-traffic cleanup for
       the initial supported PMDs. Record producer, sender, Rx and retirement owners.
    2. **AF_XDP first:** Introduce the virtual boundary, enum, tagged parameters,
       namespace factory and shared backing seam together with every affected caller.
       Preserve AF_XDP behavior before adding DPDK. Search all factory/interface users,
       including Zutcp, zxdp utility/unit/integration tests and Zutcp pool integration.
       Propagate the intentional API/ABI break without shims and rebuild dependents.
    3. **DPDK implementation:** Add the narrow selector and pool-derived resources,
       admission/service path, retirement handoff and retryable teardown. Add the
       dependency through repository configure/pkg-config conventions. Keep existing
       scheduler ownership and bounded service turns.
    4. **Shared contract validation:** Reuse admission, ownership and lifecycle cases
       across backends. Test rejected send and hook cancellation; caller return before
       and after driver release; retained packet mutation/retransmission after retirement;
       no-traffic completion; Rx exhaustion; preposted/continuous-traffic/wait-transition
       wakes; packet arrival after idle; failed setup with rollback pending; two instances;
       and repeated close/recreate with shared EAL. Build/test according to
       [docs/BUILD.md](docs/BUILD.md), keeping environment-dependent cases in `itest`.
    
    ### Software fixture boundary
    
    Use `net_ring` for controlled in-process mbuf transport/ownership and `net_pcap`
    for deterministic capture input/output. A normal ring loopback exchanges original
    mbuf pointers and ignores its configured Rx mempool; therefore Tx-origin backing
    cannot be returned through the dedicated `rxPool`. Prefer a controlled peer that
    consumes/releases Tx mbufs and separately injects Rx-origin packets, plus PCAP
    input for independent Rx-provisioning coverage. Any fixture copy is test machinery,
    not production payload staging. Explicitly drain queued mbufs before ring destruction;
    the v25.11 ring close path does not do this for the fixture.

    # Simplify Zxdp send and Zutcp ACK publication
    
    Implement this separately from the DPDK backend work.
    
    1. **Remove the send commit hook.**
       Change `Zxdp::Instance::send` to
       `bool send(uint8_t *packet, unsigned length)`. Delete `CommitFn`, the hook
       invocation and its propagation through `Stack::sendPacket`, endpoint sends,
       client/server adapters and test senders. True means accepted submission;
       false acquires no submission lease and leaves backing with the caller.
       Preserve the independent caller/submission leases and existing completion
       and close behavior. Update `zxdp/INTERFACE.md`, module guidance and comments
       that currently require the hook.
    
    2. **Remove peer-ACK frontier validation from Zutcp Rx.**
       In `ZutcpConnection.hh`, delete rejection of incoming ACKs based on the
       published transmitted frontier (`ack > next`), including the corresponding
       transmitted-frontier checks in handshake ACK qualification. Incoming ACKs
       mark bytes acknowledged through the existing ACK processing path; do not
       introduce a replacement frontier check or delayed-validation queue.
       Remove fields/helpers that become unused. Preserve generation/lifetime
       checks and the separate receive-sequence/window and RST policies.
       Delete tests whose requirement is future/excess ACK rejection or
       pre-submission frontier publication. For mixed tests, remove those assertions
       while retaining independent ownership, generation and recovery coverage.
       The principal affected tests are in `zutcp/test/ZutcpDataTest.cc`.
    
    3. **Publish the transmitted ACK after successful send.**
       In `sendTCP`, replace the borrowed commit context with a plain boolean send.
       After it returns true, publish the ACK carried by that packet from the Tx
       owner with a `ZmAtomic` write to the retained `sentAck` field. Keep its
       existing coordinate conversion and monotonic update; a refused send must
       leave the published ACK unchanged. Perform publication before subsequent
       Tx work that depends on it, preserving the existing generation checks.
       Update remaining Rx readers, including timestamp handling, to read that
       atomic ACK without requiring the deleted transmit-frontier validation.
       Finish successful-send recovery bookkeeping on the Tx owner before queued
       peer-ACK work runs. Remove or rename `publishTxCommit` as appropriate.
    
    4. **Verify the smaller contract.**
       Adapt hook-based test doubles and remove hook-only tests in
       `zxdp/itest/zxdppackettest.cc`. Verify accepted/refused send ownership,
       ACK publication only after successful return, immediate peer ACK handling,
       generation changes and retransmission. Search for remaining `CommitFn`
       references. Rebuild dependencies and affected modules according to
       `docs/BUILD.md`; run zxdp/Zutcp unit tests and affected integration tests.
       The updated zpicotls is already installed locally.

    # Zxdp AF_XDP and DPDK backends
    
    * **Author:** Huw Rogers
    * **Date:** 2026-11-16
    * **Status:** Working hypothesis; seven brainstorming lenses completed. Proposed resolutions below await design/readiness confirmation; no source implementation has begun.
    
    ## Overview
    
    Make `Zxdp::Instance` a virtual interface implemented by AF_XDP and DPDK.
    Remove the base class's `InstanceData *m_data`; make backend operations pure

    to `Params`. Add the namespace factory `ZmRef<Instance> instance(const Params
    &params)`, which switches on `backend` and creates the corresponding derived
    instance. Use the merged AF_XDP implementation as the behavioral reference.
    
    Represent interface configuration with:
    
    ```cpp
    struct If_AF_XDP { unsigned index = 0; };
    struct If_DPDK { /* DPDK device selection; exact fields to be designed */ };
    ZuDerive(If, (ZuUnion<void, If_AF_XDP, If_DPDK>));
    ```
