    `Params::interface` becomes `If interface = {}`. The caller supplies `txPools`
    and singular `rxPool`; these determine packet storage and ring provisioning.
    Do not duplicate that provisioning in `If_DPDK`.
    
    ## Analysis
    
    The objective is to let callers use AF_XDP or DPDK through the same raw-packet
    boundary while preserving the merged AF_XDP behavior. This is a backend extension,
    not a transport stack. The baseline contract is [zxdp/INTERFACE.md](zxdp/INTERFACE.md):
    separate caller and submission leases, scheduler sender service, counted receive
    wakes, queue telemetry and retryable shutdown. The author has superseded the
    commit-hook requirement: use plain `bool send(packet, length)` and remove
    frontier-based rejection of incoming ACKs from Zutcp. Preserve backing ownership
    while adapting send and ACK processing to this simpler contract.
    
    ### Confirmed decisions
    
    The author selected the virtual `Instance` boundary with no base `m_data`, pure
    virtual backend operations, the exact `Backend` enum and `Params::backend`, the
    one-argument namespace factory, and the tagged `If` representation above. Caller
    `txPools` and singular `rxPool` determine packet storage and ring provisioning.
    Software DPDK tests remain in scope. The author clarified after review that Zutcp
    need not reject ACKs beyond a published transmitted frontier; it needs to mark
    bytes acknowledged. Remove that validation and the send commit hook. These
    choices supersede review findings that assumed the hook had to be preserved.
    
    ### Proposed resolutions from the reviews
    
    These are recommendations, not additional author approvals. Blockers below block
    implementation readiness, not further brainstorming.
    
    1. **Admission — revised after author clarification.** Use plain
       `bool send(packet, length)`: true means the backend accepted the packet;
       false leaves caller ownership intact and acquires no submission lease.
       Remove `CommitFn` from Zxdp and its propagation through Zutcp. On successful
       return, Zutcp completes its Tx-owner send bookkeeping; incoming ACKs mark
       bytes acknowledged without rejection against the published Tx frontier.
       Serialize ACK effects that touch Tx-owned recovery state on the Tx owner,
       after the active send completes. Review the remaining frontier readers for
       their independent purposes rather than preserving the hook for ACK validation.
       DPDK can return whether its one-packet Tx burst accepted the packet; do not
       add an internal admission queue solely to preserve the removed hook.
       [DPDK ethdev API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    
    2. **Driver release — blocker.** Evaluate preallocated per-slot mbuf and external
       buffer shared information with a private release callback mapped directly to
       the slot. The callback indicates final detachment of driver-visible mbufs;
       caller ownership remains a separate lease. Publish release identity through
       a bounded preallocated handoff to the caller's Tx owner before changing its
       pending/active lists. `pollTx()` drains that handoff and counts retired
       submissions; `writable()` follows retirement, never enqueue success. Final
       caller return may run on any thread. The external-buffer API supports such
       callbacks, but supported PMDs, cleanup progress with no further traffic,
       DMA registration and callback contexts still require proof.
       [DPDK mbuf API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__mbuf_8h.html).
    
    3. **Shared backing — major.** Factor the smallest backend-neutral arena/slot
       lifetime component beneath the existing `BufPool`. Today it retains `UMem`
       and directly accesses its layout and `TxSlot`; a virtual instance alone does
       not remove this coupling ([ZxdpAlloc.hh](zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.hh),
       [ZxdpAlloc.cc](zxdp/src/ZxdpAlloc.cc)). Keep direct slot lookup, the existing
       payload-overlay recycling list and allocation-free packet operations. Keep
       XSK registration and DPDK registration private to each backend. Pool-held
       backing must survive instance close until the last caller packet returns.
       This needs no general allocator framework or second unrelated pool API.
    
    4. **Capacity — major.** Derive descriptor requests, submission credits and
       mbuf/shared-info metadata from existing pool counts and sizes. Validate the
       adjusted device limits, alignment/headroom and minimum useful Rx capacity at
       setup. Account for caller-held Rx packets and driver caches; distinguish
       descriptor capacity from packet credits. Reject unsatisfiable configurations
       with the selected device and offending pool constraint. Add no public ring
       sizing in `If_DPDK`.
    
    5. **Device/EAL lifecycle — major.** Prefer a named, already-created Ethernet
       device in `If_DPDK`. The application or test fixture initializes DPDK's
       process-wide Environment Abstraction Layer (EAL) and creates virtual devices;
       ordinary instance close must not tear down EAL or unrelated ports. Specify
       exclusive queue/port ownership during binding, release of resources configured
       by the instance, and reuse after close. Validate backend/tag mismatch, an unset
       interface and absent device once on the cold path. Keep arbitrary EAL arguments
       and PMD-specific tuning outside the selector.
    
    6. **Factory failure — major.** Preserve the exact one-argument factory. Retain
       the baseline distinction between null after completed rollback and a non-ready
       handle owning pending rollback. The owner retains that handle and schedules
       `close()` retries; it releases ownership only when retirement is complete.
       Recommend existing cold-path error logging for setup cause, backend/device,
       native operation and cleanup status, with runtime errors still surfaced by
       `close()`. The precise diagnostic convention and a minimal caller example must
       be settled before caller migration. Do not add a completion callback or silently
       discard a partially initialized instance ([current factory](zxdp/src/Zxdp.cc)).
    
    7. **Receive idle behavior — major, unresolved feasibility gate.** Preserve one
       Rx owner, counted preposted/concurrent wakes, prompt interruption under load,
       and return only for wake or device failure. PMD Rx interrupts are optional;
       indefinitely waiting on only the wake eventfd would miss subsequent packets.
       Prefer real packet-arrival notification where supported. For ring/pcap, select
       and validate an arrival mechanism or an explicitly described bounded polling
       fallback, including its idle CPU and latency cost and its relationship to the
       spin-then-block contract. Do not claim this resolved by a wake-only test.
       [DPDK Rx interrupt contract](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html).
    
    ### Common API meanings to settle in the design
    
    Keep existing operations pure virtual; document backend results so callers do not
    need backend switches. This proposed matrix identifies the minimum semantic work.
    
    | Operation | AF_XDP reference | Proposed DPDK treatment / remaining detail |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `ifindex()` | Linux interface index | Return unavailable sentinel (proposed `0`) for software-only ports; never substitute a DPDK port ID. |
    | `mtu()`, `mac()` | Queried Linux link values | Use configured device values where meaningful; define software-port values and unavailable results before coding. |
    | `zeroCopy()` | Negotiated XSK mode | Specify an equally precise DPDK meaning; no physical DMA claim from ring/pcap results. |
    | `netmask` | Destination selection compiled into XDP | Preserve configured packet selection; choose a shared parser/software predicate or reject unsupported masks at setup. Never silently ignore them. |
    | `allQueues()` | Identified Rx/fill/Tx/CQ ring views, retained after close | Enumerate actual backend queues with documented units/final views; no fabricated hardware CQ or unsupported zero-valued statistic. |
    | `pollTx()` | Tx-owner CQ retirement count | Tx-owner drain of actual release records; sender consumption is a separate event. |
    | `stopSender()`, `close()` | FIFO sender barrier, safe retirement, retryable close | Quiesce producer/sender, resolve queued and PMD/peer-owned mbufs, retain final caller backing; no timeout-based reclamation. |
    
    Use existing queue views and cold diagnostics first. Additional owner-local
    counters or close-phase views are optional only when necessary to diagnose a
    specific test failure; a new tracing/observability subsystem is outside scope.
    
    ## Goals vs. Non-Goals
    
    * **In-Scope Goals:** Virtual Instance API; backend enum and namespace factory;
      tagged interface parameters; AF_XDP and DPDK implementations in zxdp; migration
      of affected callers; pool-driven provisioning; software DPDK tests; preservation
      of admission, ownership, service and shutdown contracts.
    * **Out-of-Scope Non-Goals:** A transport stack or application runtime; duplicate
      public ring sizing; compatibility shims; new sender threads; hot-path allocation,
      packet searches or payload staging; a general allocator or tracing framework;
      claims of physical NIC DMA, offload or wire-latency validation from software tests.
    * **Not recommended:** Duplicate the pool allocator or force DPDK through XDP page
      geometry. A narrow common storage/lease component preserves the existing invariant
      with less duplicated lifecycle logic.
    * **Receive alternatives still open:** PMD notification versus bounded polling.
      Notification needs driver support; polling trades idle CPU and arrival latency.
      The inventive lens found no false compromise requiring a different architecture.
    
    ## Key Decisions & Staging for Next Steps
    
    Confirmed decisions are listed above. All new resolutions remain proposals;
    Goldfish completion is not author approval or implementation readiness.
    
    1. **Contract and feasibility:** Specify the API matrix, factory diagnostic
       workflow, named-device/EAL ownership, capacity equations and per-PMD Rx wait
       strategy. Prove the direct-slot release mechanism and no-traffic cleanup for
       the initial supported PMDs. Record producer, sender, Rx and retirement owners.
    2. **AF_XDP first:** Introduce the virtual boundary, enum, tagged parameters,
       namespace factory and shared backing seam together with every affected caller.
       Migrate Zutcp to boolean send, remove frontier-based ACK rejection and hook
       propagation, and preserve the other AF_XDP contracts before adding DPDK.
       Search all factory/interface users,
       including Zutcp, zxdp utility/unit/integration tests and Zutcp pool integration.
       Propagate the intentional API/ABI break without shims and rebuild dependents.
    3. **DPDK implementation:** Add the narrow selector and pool-derived resources,
       admission/service path, retirement handoff and retryable teardown. Add the
       dependency through repository configure/pkg-config conventions. Keep existing
       scheduler ownership and bounded service turns.
    4. **Shared contract validation:** Reuse admission, ownership and lifecycle cases
       across backends. Test rejected and accepted sends, immediate peer ACKs without
       frontier rejection, and Tx-owner ACK ordering; caller return before
       and after driver release; retained packet mutation/retransmission after retirement;
       no-traffic completion; Rx exhaustion; preposted/continuous-traffic/wait-transition
       wakes; packet arrival after idle; failed setup with rollback pending; two instances;
       and repeated close/recreate with shared EAL. Build/test according to
       [docs/BUILD.md](docs/BUILD.md), keeping environment-dependent cases in `itest`.
    
    ### Software fixture boundary
    
    Use `net_ring` for controlled in-process mbuf transport/ownership and `net_pcap`
    for deterministic capture input/output. A normal ring loopback exchanges original
    mbuf pointers and ignores its configured Rx mempool; therefore Tx-origin backing
    cannot be returned through the dedicated `rxPool`. Prefer a controlled peer that
    consumes/releases Tx mbufs and separately injects Rx-origin packets, plus PCAP
    input for independent Rx-provisioning coverage. Any fixture copy is test machinery,
    not production payload staging. Explicitly drain queued mbufs before ring destruction;
    the v25.11 ring close path does not do this for the fixture.
    [Official ring source](https://github.com/DPDK/dpdk/blob/v25.11/drivers/net/ring/rte_eth_ring.c).
    
    Distinguish accepted, peer-dequeued and peer-released states; packet equality alone
    does not prove retirement. Record tested DPDK version/PMDs. Physical hardware
    validation remains separate. [Ring guide](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/nics/ring.html),
    [PCAP guide](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.03/nics/pcap_ring.html),
    [EAL parameters](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/linux_gsg/linux_eal_parameters.html),
    [local testing context](dpdk_loopback.md).

## User

doesn't `AF_XDP` have analogous implementation to 1? it also deals with packet release asynchronously

## Assistant

Yes. AF_XDP already provides the model:

- Accepted send acquires a submission lease.
- `pollTx()` consumes completion entries, identifies each slot and releases that lease.
- Pool return independently releases the caller lease.
- Recycling waits for both leases to end.

DPDK should reuse that slot bookkeeping and lifetime model. The backend-specific part is obtaining the release notification: AF_XDP supplies a completion queue containing buffer addresses; DPDK needs an equivalent per-buffer signal from mbuf release.

So issue 1 is **implementing the DPDK completion adapter**, rather than inventing asynchronous packet ownership. The remaining checks are where that notification executes and how reclamation progresses without further sends. I overstated it as a broad feasibility issue.

## Assistant

They normally use **DPDK’s mbuf ownership and reference counting**, letting the driver reclaim transmitted buffers.

Three relevant patterns:

1. **Transfer ownership to the driver.** After `rte_eth_tx_burst()`, accepted mbufs belong to the driver; unaccepted ones remain with the application for retry or freeing. DPDK’s basic forwarding example uses this directly. [Example](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.03/sample_app_ug/skeleton.html)

2. **Retain a reference when backing must survive transmission.** The application keeps its reference while the driver holds another. Driver reclamation drops its reference. DPDK explicitly documents retaining a packet and requesting `rte_eth_tx_done_cleanup()` until its reference count decreases before modifying and retransmitting it. Cleanup support depends on the driver. [Driver guide](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-24.11/prog_guide/ethdev/ethdev.html#free-tx-mbuf-on-demand)

3. **Attach application-owned backing to an mbuf.** `rte_pktmbuf_attach_extbuf()` supplies a callback invoked when the last attached mbuf releases that backing. This lets an application connect DPDK release to its own allocator. [External-buffer API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__mbuf_8h.html#rte_pktmbuf_attach_extbuf)

As a concrete application example, F-Stack’s ordinary transmit path copies its BSD packet into DPDK mbufs, submits those, and frees unaccepted mbufs. That separates its transport storage from driver storage. [F-Stack implementation](https://github.com/F-Stack/f-stack/blob/dev/lib/ff_dpdk_if.c)

For **Zxdp’s existing caller-owned, zero-copy backing**, pattern 3 looks like the closest fit: the internal release callback drops the submission lease; explicit pool return drops the caller lease. This is standard DPDK machinery—the work is connecting it to Zxdp’s existing slot accounting and service ownership.

## Assistant

Yes. The DPDK `Zi::IOBufPlugin` supplies mbuf-backed storage from allocation onward. Zutcp constructs the packet there, and Zxdp submits that existing mbuf directly.

That removes the external-buffer attachment and callback adapter I proposed. The remaining work is connecting native mbuf reclamation to `pollTx()` and `writable()`, while preserving any caller-held reference.

Updated the [brief](/home/count0/src/z/concepts_brief.md) to reflect this ownership model.

## User

recap the remaining issues

## Assistant

The remaining issues are:

1. **Mbuf reclamation:** Map native DPDK ownership/reference counts to `pollTx()`, `writable()` and safe close, including reclamation when sends stop.
2. **Pool integration:** Implement mbuf-backed `Zi::IOBufPlugin` provisioning and remove AF_XDP-specific assumptions from the shared pool boundary.
3. **Provisioning:** Derive queues, descriptors and metadata from `txPools` and `rxPool`, within driver constraints.
4. **Device lifecycle:** Define `If_DPDK`, EAL initialization ownership, port ownership and cleanup.
5. **Factory errors:** Preserve diagnostics and pending rollback ownership with `instance(const Params &)`.
6. **Receive waiting:** Define idle packet detection and counted `wake()` behavior for each supported PMD.
7. **API meanings:** Specify DPDK behavior for interface identity, MTU/MAC, `zeroCopy()`, filtering and queue telemetry.
8. **Software tests:** Define ring/pcap fixtures, receive-pool ownership and teardown of queued mbufs.

The commit-hook issue is resolved under the assumed `zutcp_fix.md` implementation. External-buffer adapters are unnecessary.

## User

on 1, `AF_XDP` already does this for `UMEM`, why can't DPDK do that for `mbuf`s

## Assistant

It can. AF_XDP’s UMEM handling is the reference: retain backing while either the caller or backend owns it, and recycle after both release it. DPDK implements the same rule using native mbuf ownership and reference counts.

The backend-specific reclamation code belongs in the DPDK implementation. It does not need a separate architectural decision or feasibility investigation.

I’ve been overstating routine implementation work as an unresolved issue. Item 1 should be folded into implementing the DPDK backend.

4. **Backend API semantics:** Define DPDK behavior for `ifindex()`, `zeroCopy()`, netmask filtering and queue telemetry.

I’ll check DPDK’s terminology and relate EAL and ports to the proposed `If_DPDK`.

## Activity

    Opened https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/prog_guide/env_abstraction_layer.html

## Assistant

**EAL—the Environment Abstraction Layer—is DPDK’s process-wide initialization layer.** `rte_eal_init()` sets up memory, device discovery, CPU configuration and other runtime facilities. Its options can select physical devices or create software devices such as `net_ring0`. `rte_eal_cleanup()` releases EAL resources at application shutdown. [EAL documentation](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/prog_guide/env_abstraction_layer.html)

A **port** is a DPDK Ethernet endpoint, identified internally by a `uint16_t port_id`. It can represent a physical NIC port or a software endpoint. It has Rx/Tx queues and device properties such as MAC address and MTU. It is unrelated to a TCP/UDP port number, and its ID is not a Linux interface index. [Ethernet device API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html)

For this design, the proposed lifecycle is:

1. The application initializes EAL, making the desired devices available.
2. `If_DPDK` selects a device.
3. `Zxdp::instance()` configures its queues using `txPools` and `rxPool`, then starts it.
4. Instance close retires that instance’s resources.
5. The application cleans up EAL after all DPDK users finish.

The remaining decision is whether Zxdp owns that process-wide initialization or expects the application to do it. My proposal was application-owned EAL, with `If_DPDK` selecting an already available device.

    ZmExtern void ZmGlobal_atexit()
    {
      lock();
      ZmGlobal_atexit_ = 0;
      unsigned n = 0;
      for (unsigned i = 0; i < ZmCleanup::N; i++)

## Assistant

`rte_eal_init(argc, argv)` takes DPDK startup arguments. Most have defaults; the relevant configuration is:

| Setting | Purpose |
|---|---|
| CPU/lcore selection | Controls DPDK core assignment. We should keep this consistent with `ZmScheduler` ownership. |
| Memory mode | Hugepage-backed memory for hardware use, or `--no-huge` for software tests. |
| Device discovery | PCI probing, optionally restricted with `--allow`, or disabled with `--no-pci`. |
| Software devices | `--vdev=net_ring0`, or PCAP device arguments naming input/output files. |
| Process isolation | `--file-prefix` separates independent DPDK processes; `--no-shconf` disables shared configuration. |

These are EAL options documented by DPDK. They do **not** specify our pool counts or queue sizes. [EAL parameters](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/linux_gsg/linux_eal_parameters.html)

For the software ring tests, the relevant arguments would resemble:

```text
--no-pci --no-huge --no-shconf --vdev=net_ring0
```

Then `If_DPDK::name = "net_ring0"` selects that device, while `txPools` and `rxPool` determine provisioning.

For hardware, the manager instead needs the memory/core policy and any device restrictions. The configuration question is how to supply those process-wide arguments to `InstanceMgr` before its first successful `init()`.

## User

does DPDK spawn threads internally? why does it need core assignment

## Assistant

I’ll check which threads EAL creates and how that relates to using `ZmScheduler` threads for packet I/O.

## Activity

    Searched the web for site.doc.dpdk.org guides EAL initialization worker threads main lcore control threads rte_thread_register, site.doc.dpdk.org guides --lcores EAL pthread_create worker threads interrupt thread

## Activity

    Searched for 'Control Thread' in https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/prog_guide/env_abstraction_layer.html

## Assistant

**Yes. DPDK can create both worker threads and internal support threads.**

- **Worker threads:** EAL normally creates a thread for each configured worker “lcore.” Applications can dispatch packet-processing functions onto them. Core assignment controls affinity to reduce scheduling overhead and preserve cache locality.
- **Support threads:** DPDK also uses threads for facilities such as interrupt handling and multiprocess coordination. [EAL documentation](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/prog_guide/env_abstraction_layer.html)

**Zxdp can keep packet processing on `ZmScheduler` threads.** DPDK supports application-created pthreads; `rte_thread_register()` gives such a thread a DPDK lcore identity, including access to per-lcore facilities such as mempool caches. Registration does not create a thread. [Thread API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__lcore_8h.html#rte_thread_register)

For our integration, the approach would be to configure EAL without additional worker lcores, use the existing scheduler’s Rx/Tx owners, and register those threads as needed. EAL still has a main-lcore configuration and may create internal support threads.

My earlier wording made core assignment sound like DPDK must own our packet-processing threads. It does not.

## User

## Assistant

I’ll check whether EAL automatically supplies a Tx service thread, and how that differs from running Tx work on a configured EAL worker.

## Activity

    Opened https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__launch_8h.html

## Assistant

**Only if we explicitly configure an EAL worker and launch our Tx service on it.** EAL does not automatically create a per-port thread that drains application submissions. Its workers initially wait for a function dispatched with `rte_eal_remote_launch()`. [EAL launch API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__launch_8h.html)

There is also a difference from AF_XDP: `rte_eth_tx_burst()` runs the driver’s submission code on the calling thread, filling device descriptors and reclaiming completed mbufs. For a hardware PMD, the NIC then consumes those descriptors asynchronously. There is no intervening kernel Tx-processing step. [Tx API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html#rte_eth_tx_burst)

If we want that driver work on a separate core, the arrangement is:

```text
Zutcp Tx owner → software submission ring → Zxdp Tx service → DPDK/NIC
```

That service can run on the existing `ZmScheduler` sender slot, registered with DPDK, or on an explicitly launched EAL worker. **Using the existing scheduler slot would preserve the current thread-ownership model.** The software ring would then serve the deliberate core separation, independently of the removed commit hook.

Then both hardware and software tests use the same path:

The selected PMD determines the destination:

## User

what other configuration does EAL init need?

## Assistant

With direct submission and singleton ownership settled, EAL configuration is mainly:

- **Memory mode:** hugepages for hardware deployments; `--no-huge` for software tests. Memory limits and hugepage directory can use defaults unless deployment requires overrides.
- **Device discovery:** normal PCI probing, an optional PCI allowlist, or `--no-pci` for software-only tests.
- **Software-device creation:** for example, `--vdev=net_ring0` or PCAP arguments specifying capture files.
- **Main lcore:** configure one EAL main lcore, with no EAL workers. Initialization’s effect on the calling thread’s affinity needs handling.
- **Process isolation:** a file prefix or shared-memory policy so independent processes do not conflict.
- **Driver loading:** paths only if required PMDs are not already linked or discoverable.

These are documented [EAL parameters](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-25.11/linux_gsg/linux_eal_parameters.html).

Pool counts, buffer sizes, Rx/Tx queue provisioning and `ZmScheduler` thread affinity remain outside EAL configuration.

We do not need a public field for every EAL option. The manager can establish defaults; the main configurable differences are hardware versus software operation and software-device arguments.

    # Code layout and naming
    
    Part of the repository guidance mapped in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
    
    ## Code style
    ### Header layout
    - Library headers must follow this skeleton (`[header]`: `ZuString`, `ZhttpQPack`; `[component]`: `Zu`, `Zhttp`):
      ```
      //  -*- mode:c++; indent-tabs-mode:t; tab-width:8; c-basic-offset:2; -*-
      //  vi: noet ts=8 sw=2 cino=+0,(s,l1,m1,g0,N-s,j1,U1,W2,i2
    
      // (c) Copyright [year] [author]
      // This code is licensed by the MIT license (see LICENSE for details)
    
      // [title and brief description of header]
    
      #ifndef [header]_HH
      #define [header]_HH
    
      #ifndef [component]Lib_HH
      #include <zlib/[component]Lib.hh>
      #endif
    
      [lowest-level includes, e.g. system library includes]
    
      [next-lowest-level includes, e.g. Zu includes]
    
      [next-lowest-level includes, e.g. Zt includes]
    
      [same-level component includes]
    
      [body of header]
      ```
    - Headers must include all direct dependencies.
    - Headers must not include indirect dependencies unless they use related code/definitions.
    
    ### Indentation
    - Match prevailing style in `{zu,zm,zt,ze,zi}/src/*.{hh,cc}`; when these rules, editor `cino`, and local precedent disagree, code precedent wins.
    - Use hard tabs for indentation (`noet`, `ts=8`) and a 2-column logical C++ indent (`sw=2`); do not replace leading tabs with spaces.
    - Indent class/struct/function bodies, control-flow bodies, and lambda bodies one logical level.
    - Namespaces:
      - Large namespace bodies (>20 lines):
        - not indented
        - closing braces are commented with `// [namespace]`
      - Small namespace bodies (<= 20 lines):
        - indented
        - closing braces are uncommented
    - Keep `public:`, `protected:`, and `private:` flush with the class declaration body; indent following members one logical level.
    - Keep `friend` declarations flush with the class declaration body, at the top in the default private section.
    - Follow local switch style for `case`/`default`; indent statements one logical level from the label.
    - For a braced `case`/`default` body, place its terminating `break` after the closing brace on the same line (`} break;`), not inside the braces on a separate line.
    
    ### Multiline layout
    - Wrap source code at 98 columns, counting hard tabs at tab stops of 8.
    - Prefer existing visual alignment over mechanical fixed-width continuation indents.
    - Split long template parameter lists, inheritance lists, base constructor calls, and function argument lists after natural delimiters.
    - Continue nested template/base/member-initializer expressions one logical level deeper than their containing line.
    - Align continuation lines with the open construct when nearby code does.
    - Function multiline style, with `{` on its own line:
      ```
      template <typename Client>
      int run(
        ZiMultiplex &mx, const Options &options, URL url,
        RequestResult *result = nullptr)
      {
        Client client;
      ```
    - Constructor multiline style, with `:` and `{` on their own lines:
      ```
      StoreTbl(
        Store *store, IDString id, unsigned nShards,
        ZfVFieldArray fields, ZfVKeyFieldArray keyFields,
        const reflection::Schema *schema, IOBufAllocFn bufAllocFn)
      :
        m_store{store}, m_id{ZuMv(id)},
        m_fields{ZuMv(fields)}, m_keyFields{ZuMv(keyFields)},
        m_bufAllocFn{ZuMv(bufAllocFn)}
      {
        // introspect fields and flatbuffers reflection data, building
      ```
    - Do not deeply indent lambdas; large multiline captures/parameters use this shape:
      ```
      auto lambda = [
        ... /* multiline captures */
      ](
        ... /* multiline parameters */)
      {
        ... /* body */
      };
      ```
    
    ### Compact layout and alignment
    - Keep short, simple functions and statements on one line when surrounding code does; split only when line length or expression shape makes it clearer.
    - Preserve tabular alignment for data members, macro bodies, and compact tables already using tabs to align names, initializers, or comments.
    - Vertically align `ZfStruct` field typecodes with hard tabs;
      wrap long properties at natural delimiters to keep declarations within 98 columns.
    - Vertically align data member names with hard tabs.
    - Do not let a verbose member type defeat tabular alignment. Give a complex or long member type a short local `using` alias when that keeps the member declaration aligned; place that alias immediately before the data declarations that use it.
    - `*` and `&` go with the member, not the type: `void<TAB>*m_`, not `void *<TAB>m_`.
    
    ### Class and struct shape
    - `struct`s are all-public data: members are not prefixed with `m_` and appear at the top, before constructors and other function members; required local `using` declarations may precede them.
    - Put directly shared, unprefixed data at the top of its composite type before member functions; required local `using` declarations may precede it.
    - `class`es have all-private data: members are prefixed with `m_` and appear in a trailing `private:` section at the bottom before closing `};`.
    - Do not create hybrid `class` or `struct` types with mixed public/private data members.
    - `m_` marks state owned and encapsulated by its class. Only the owning class's implementation accesses it directly; friendship does not relax this rule. Direct base/derived implementation access is the narrow exception.
    - Model state shared at field granularity as an unprefixed member of a `struct`, not as a friend's view into a class's `m_` state. If a type needs both shared data and encapsulated state, put the former in a `...Data` struct or expose the latter through member functions.
    
    ## Naming
    ### Length and abbreviations
    - Names must be concise; 28 bytes is the hard upper limit.
    - Use industry standard in-code abbreviations for long names:
      - `receive` -> `rx`
      - `transmit` -> `tx`
      - `reserve` -> `res`
      - `recovery` -> `rec`
      - `request` -> `req`
      - `receive` -> `recv`
      - `event` -> `evt`
      - `client` -> `cli`
      - `server` -> `srv`
      - `connection` -> `cxn`
      - `packet` -> `pkt`
      - `protection` -> `prot`
      - `security` -> `sec`
      - `generation` -> `gen`
      - `version` -> `ver`
      - `original` -> `orig`
      - `previous` -> `prev`
      - `parameter` -> `param`
      - `interface` -> `if`
      - `implementation` -> `impl`
      - ... and so on (this is not an exhaustive list)
    - Example: `packet` is fine; `reservePacketProtection` is too long; use `resPktProt`.
    - use "ack" and "ackd", not "acked"; example: `packetAckd`
    - use "nak and "nakd", not "nack", "nackd" or "nacked"; example: `packetNakd`
    - do not prefix or namespace file-scoped `static` functions in `.cc` files:
      - use short meaningful names, e.g. in `ZiIP.cc`: `pton4` not `ZiIP_pton4`
    - do not use ambiguous or obfuscated abbreviations:
      - bad: `bytesInFlight` -> `bif`: `if` is typically read as `interface`
      - bad: `congestionBytes` -> `congBytes`: `cong` is a non-standard and counter-intuitive abbreviation
    - elide redundant words in names:
      - `runtimeDiag` -> `diag`: "runtime" is implied, delete it
      - `Engine::stopEngine` -> `stop`: "engine" is implied - this is a member function of `Engine`
    
    ### Casing and member prefixes
    - Names are generally camel-case, not snake-case, but there are numerous exceptions.
    - Repository-owned library/component basenames in `src` and unit-test
      code/data basenames in `test` are CamelCase and use the module prefix, e.g.
      `ZmLib`, `ZmTest`, and `ZhttpParserTest`.
    - Programs built in `src` have succinct lowercase command-line names. Their
      program-specific source and resource basenames are also lowercase, e.g.
      `zcmd`, `zdash`, `ztotp`, and `zwsd`.
    - C compatibility-layer headers and implementations intended for direct use by
      C applications retain their snake-case C API names, e.g. `zu_bitmap.h` and
      `zu_bitmap.cc`.
    - Repository-owned code/data basenames in `util`, `itest`, `example`, `bench`,
      and `interop` are lowercase.
    - Flabuffers schema files are snake-case.
    - Conventional control filenames such as `Makefile.am`, `README.md`,
      `Dockerfile.*`, and `.gitignore` retain their conventional casing.
    - Native names mandated by an external tool or protocol retain their spelling;
      this includes PostgreSQL extension/control/SQL names, generated files,
      imported fixtures, and FlatBuffers schema filenames and contract fields.
      FlatBuffers schemas use their established lowercase/underscore basenames;
      keep the corresponding generation rules and generated-header names aligned.
      Do not apply this exception to ordinary repository-owned C++ files.
    - `m_` is reserved for encapsulated private data members of classes; see the class-shape ownership rule above.
    
    ### Accessors
    - Use overloads for getters/setters; do not invent separate names.
    - Example: `int x() const` and `void x(int)`.
    - `decltype(auto) x(this &&self) { ... }` is acceptable to preserve move context.
    - `int &x()` as a setter is an amber flag; use it only when thread-safety is guaranteed by the calling context. If direct mutation is intended, `int x` should probably be a public data member.
    - When an outer fluent parameter type contains or extends another fluent
      parameter type, preserve inline configuration with the
      `ZiMxParams::scheduler()` pattern: provide accessors for the inner/base
      parameters and a same-named lambda overload that applies the lambda and
      returns the outer type as an rvalue. Do not forward every inner/base setter,
      and do not permit an inherited setter's narrower return type to decay an
      inline expression to the base type.
    
    ### Trailing underscores
    - Use trailing underscores only to distinguish related wrapper, implementation and reserved names:
      - generically for wrapped functions and macros; wrapper chains may add one underscore per layer: `x` wraps `x_`, which wraps `x__`.
      - to distinguish internal-only functions/types from external functions, that are primarily wrappers of the internal function.
      - to distinguish thread-dedicated functions/types from those that are callable from any thread, that are primarily wrappers of the thread-dedicated function.
      - to avoid collisions with reserved words (`namespace_`, etc.)
    - Example: `send` may `txInvoke` a `send_` call on the Tx thread; `send_` can assume the correct thread and elide the check/context switch.
    - Example: `template <typename T> struct Foo : public Foo_ { ... };` where `Foo` is the API and `Foo_` is a `T`-independent common base.
    - Use numbered suffixes `_0`, `_1`, ... for multi-step functions and variable-argument macros, e.g. `stop_0`, `stop_1`, ...; do not use repeated trailing underscores to label steps or argument counts.
    - When repairing names, remove unjustified trailing underscores and update all affected declarations and uses; do not introduce a wrapper merely to justify an underscore.
    
    ### Vocabulary
    - Prefer precise project vocabulary: "utilities" not "helpers", "duplex" not "bidi", etc.
    - Do not choose imprecise or primitive English for accessibility to non-native, non-technical, or non-veteran readers; accessible naming is a hard non-goal.
    
    ### Standard function name vocabulary
    - `push()` - appends a value at tail
    - `unshift()` - prepends a value at head
    - `pop()` - removes a value from tail
    - `shift()` - removes a value from head
    - `add()` - inserts a value
    - `del()` - deletes a value
    - `find()` - finds a value
    - `iter()` - returns an iterator (`citer()` for const)
    - `riter()` - returns a reverse iterator (`criter()` for const)
    - `clear()`/`clr()` - clears to a default initial state
      - containers: clears certain contained values
    - `clean()` - removes and frees **all** contained data
    - `reset()` - both `clear` and `clean`
    - `null()` (as a mutable member function) - same as `reset` for objects with a semantic "null" value, with the postcondition that the object's value is "null"
    - `init()` - initializes an object post-constructor
    - `final()` - finalizes an object pre-destructor
    - `start()` - start running (should be idempotent)
    - `stop()` - stop running (should be idempotent)
    - `operator *()` - test for "null" sentinel (used with non-pointer types)

    };

    template <bool Secret_, typename NTP = ZtArray_Defaults>
    struct ZtArraySecret : public NTP {

## Assistant

Proposed [`Zxdp::DPDKParams` in the brief](/home/count0/src/z/concepts_brief.md), following the aggregate style of `Zxdp::Params` and `Zutcp::StackParams`.

It contains named fields for CPU mapping, device discovery, virtual devices, memory/NUMA settings, process isolation and diagnostics. Strings and arrays own their storage; optional numeric values use `ZuUnion<void, unsigned>` to distinguish unspecified from zero.

Example:

```cpp
dpdk->init(Zxdp::DPDKParams{
  .noPCI = true,
  .vdev = {"net_ring0"},
  .noHuge = true,
  .noShconf = true
});
```

An `args` array accepts additional EAL argument tokens, covering platform-specific and future options without requiring new fields. Supplying the same setting through both a named field and `args` would be rejected.

`init()` translates the structure into private writable `argv` storage for `rte_eal_init()`. Pool provisioning and scheduler configuration remain in their existing APIs.

## Assistant

Issue 1 is **what `rx()` does when no packets are available**.

AF_XDP currently:

1. Polls for `Params::spin` rounds.
2. Blocks in epoll on packet readiness and the internal wake eventfd.
3. Resumes receiving when packets arrive, or returns when `wake()` is called.

DPDK’s `rte_eth_rx_burst()` returns immediately when its queue is empty. Some PMDs support receive interrupts; others, including software paths, need polling. Waiting indefinitely on only the wake eventfd would miss incoming packets. [DPDK API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__ethdev_8h.html)

The decision is the idle policy:

- **Continuous polling:** lowest arrival latency, consumes a core while idle; check wake state between bounded batches.
- **Interrupt-based waiting:** where supported, arm notification, recheck the queue, then wait for packets or wake.
- **Timed polling:** sleep briefly between probes; saves CPU but adds arrival latency.

No extra Rx thread is implied—the caller’s Rx owner runs this loop.

Testing is now recorded as mirroring existing AF_XDP coverage in the [brief](/home/count0/src/z/concepts_brief.md).

## Assistant

**It supports a related mechanism: memory-monitor wakeup, rather than a synthesized Rx interrupt.**

The ring PMD implements `get_monitor_addr`, exposing its producer-head address. A DPDK power-monitor wait can sleep until an enqueue changes that memory location. The driver has no Rx interrupt enable/disable operations. [Ring PMD source](https://github.com/DPDK/dpdk/blob/v25.11/drivers/net/ring/rte_eth_ring.c#L295-L336)

DPDK also provides `rte_power_monitor_wakeup()` to interrupt a monitored wait, which is a candidate for implementing `wake()`. These facilities require runtime CPU-support checks. [Power-monitor API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api/rte__power__intrinsics_8h.html)

I missed this when describing the options. Ring loopback does not necessarily require continuous polling or a custom eventfd notification. Updated the [brief](/home/count0/src/z/concepts_brief.md).

## Assistant

I suggest **brief spinning followed by bounded idle waits**:

1. **While packets arrive:** call `rte_eth_rx_burst()` again immediately. Check `wake()` state between bounded batches. No sleeps or wait syscalls.
2. **After an empty burst:** spin for `Params::spin` rounds. Any packet resets that budget.
3. **After sustained emptiness:** park on the internal wake eventfd with a short timeout, backing off to a small cap—initially perhaps 1–50 µs, subject to measurement. Probe Rx after each timeout; any packet immediately restores active processing.

This preserves sustained receive performance and avoids indefinitely occupying a core. Without packet-arrival notification, the compromise is extra latency for the **first packet after extended idle**.

The ring’s memory-monitor support can improve the short-idle phase on supported CPUs. However, it enters a CPU power-saving state rather than descheduling the thread; it does not necessarily reduce reported CPU usage or make the core available to other work. [DPDK API](https://doc.dpdk.org/api-25.11/rte__power__intrinsics_8h.html)

Use native packet-arrival notification where available. A synthetic notification from the loopback fixture is optional; I would not make it a prerequisite.

Recorded as a proposal in the [brief](/home/count0/src/z/concepts_brief.md).

        unsigned headRoom = 0, unsigned tailRoom = 0,
        unsigned align = ZiIOBuf_DefltAlign) = 0;
      // Initialize once. Retain the handle after failure and close it to finish
      // rollback. Configuration may expire on return; pool references are retained.
      virtual ZuUnion<void, ZeException> init(const Params &) = 0;
    
      virtual bool ready() const = 0;
      virtual unsigned mtu() const = 0;
      virtual bool zeroCopy() const = 0;
      virtual ZuBSpan mac() const = 0;
    
      // False acquires no kernel lease. After true, keep bytes immutable until
      // kernel retirement. One descriptor may be outstanding for each slot.
      virtual bool send(uint8_t *packet, unsigned length) = 0;
      virtual void rx() = 0; // Rx owner, until wake() or device failure
      virtual void wake() = 0;
      virtual unsigned pollTx() = 0;
      virtual bool stopTx() = 0;
      // Quiesce Rx, Tx and wake callers first. True means closed, false means
      // retirement is pending; an error never authorizes releasing kernel backing.
      virtual ZuUnion<bool, ZeException> close() = 0;
    
      virtual unsigned allQueues(Ztc::QueueMgr::AllFn) const = 0;
    
    protected:
      Instance() = default;
    };
    
    ZxdpExtern ZmRef<Instance> instance(Type::T);
    
    } // namespace Zxdp
    #endif /* Zxdp_HH */
    # Zxdp implementation rules
    
    Follow the repository guidance in ../AGENTS.md and the caller-supplied
    [interface contract](INTERFACE.md). The contract supersedes earlier plans.
    
    * Select a cold backend with `instance(Type::Xdp)`, then call virtual
      `init(const Params &)` with backend `Xdp::Params` constructed in place using
      `Params::New<Params::Index<Xdp::Params>{}>{}`. Configuration: interface index,
      optional destination network mask,
      owning intrusive `Zi::IOBufPoolList` Tx list with count, size and alignment,
      one dedicated unlinked `ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool>` Rx pool, receive callback.
      Create pool objects with the selected instance's virtual `bufPool`.
      Init retains one reference per pool through close, while node membership
      remains in the caller configuration list. A node belongs to one
      list at a time; retain pool references for packets that outlive the instance.
      The concrete arena pool is internal. No transmit-completion callback. Without a mask all traffic is selected.
    * Keep allocation and kernel leases distinct in preallocated slot bookkeeping.
      Explicit pool return may run before or after CQ. Recycle only after both leases
      end; safe close releases kernel leases while caller-held backing stays valid.
      One descriptor may be outstanding for a slot. Rejected send acquires no lease.
      The Tx-owner writable query requires a caller-held allocation and reads only
      existing direct-slot lease state. It authorizes header changes after kernel
      retirement, with no new callback, tracking allocation or packet search.
    * Application and transport adaptation belongs to the caller. This library owns
      arena provisioning, raw packet allocation/return and kernel ring service.
    * Preallocate arenas and all packet bookkeeping at setup. Recycle each pool with
      the non-sharded ZmHeap payload-overlay slist. Exhaustion returns null.
    * Packet lookup and completion use direct slot identity, with constant-time
      updates. No packet/buffer searches or hot-path heap allocations.
    * Query kernel ring mapping offsets and preserve SWSR ownership. The caller
      provides one Rx service owner and one Tx service owner; final pool return may
      run on any thread. Keep thread-exclusive mutable state on separate cache lines.
    * The application assigns a sender `txSid` in its `ZmScheduler` and configures
      that slot with `Xdp::Params::txThread` (`ZmSchedTParams`, isolated by default).
      The scheduler owns thread startup, waiting and teardown. Zxdp owns no sender
      thread or semaphore. Publish initialized descriptors immediately: increment
      the pending-descriptor counter before commit and use scheduler `run()` after
      commit only on a zero-to-one transition. The dedicated sender calls nonblocking
      `sendto()`, observes the kernel consumer delta, spins for `Params_::spin` when
      pending work is exhausted, then atomically subtracts that delta. Use the
      returned pending count to continue or return without losing racing publication.
      Keep a persistent consumer cursor; never count the same consumption twice.
      Tx service has no custom wake function, epoll/eventfd or wait timeout. Rx keeps
      its epoll/eventfd wake protocol. The caller remains the sole descriptor
      producer and CQ owner; consumption accounting does not release kernel leases.
      Check exit during service and idle spin, then drain sender callbacks with a
      FIFO continuation before socket retirement.
    * Construct payload directly in registered backing. No payload staging or copy.
    * Quiesce service before close. Retire kernel access before returning submitted
      backing. A caller-owned pool retains its arena through the last packet return.
    * Queue configuration and mask compilation are cold-path operations.
    * Own the required `rx()`/`wake()` pair: spin for a configurable count before
      blocking with the most efficient suitable kernel mechanism; receive packets
      until explicitly woken, then return. With epoll, post wakeups through an
      internal `eventfd` when Rx has published a wait attempt, following
      ZiEventLoop/ZiMultiplex, with no per-wakeup allocation. Active and preposted
      wake pulses remain in userspace. Own these descriptors and their lifecycle. Wake
      must interrupt spinning and blocking promptly, including under continuous
      traffic and at the transition into the wait. Internal batches do not cause
      `rx()` to return on their own. The caller owns scheduling and lifecycle retries.

    // Keep pool objects alive through instance close and final packet return.
    // Freeze the list/count/size while bound. Exhaustion never allocates backing.
    class BufPool final : public ZmNHeap<BufPool>, public Zi::IOBufPool {
    friend inline ZuStringT<"Zxdp.Pool"> ZmNHeapID(BufPool *);
    friend class UMem;
    friend class Instance;
    
    public:
      using ZmNHeap<BufPool>::operator new;
      using ZmNHeap<BufPool>::operator delete;
      BufPool(unsigned count = 0, unsigned size = 0);
      ~BufPool() override;
      BufPool(const BufPool &) = delete;
      BufPool &operator =(const BufPool &) = delete;
    
      uint8_t *alloc() override;
      void free(uint8_t *packet) override;
      unsigned used() const override { return unsigned(m_used); }
      bool ready() const override { return unsigned(m_active); }
      bool owns(const void *) const override;
      unsigned slot(const void *) const override;
      uint8_t *backing(unsigned slot) const override;
      // Tx owner, with the caller allocation lease held. True only after all
      // kernel use retires; permits header changes before a subsequent send.
      bool writable(const void *) const override;
    
    private:
      void init(ZmRef<UMem>, uint64_t offset, unsigned stride, unsigned prefix, unsigned first);
      void retire() { m_active = 0; }
      unsigned first() const { return m_first; }
      unsigned stride() const { return unsigned(1)<<m_shift; }
    
      using Head = ZmAtomic<uintptr_t>;
      using Count = ZmAtomic<unsigned>;
      ZmRef<UMem>    m_arena;
      uint64_t    m_offset = 0;
      unsigned    m_shift = 0, m_prefix = 0, m_first = 0;
      bool        m_tx = false;
      alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) Head m_head{0};
      Count        m_used{0}, m_active{0};
    };

    #include <zlib/ZmAssert.hh>
    
    #include <zlib/ZxdpPool.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZxdpUMem.hh>
    
    namespace Zxdp::Xdp {
    
    BufPool::BufPool(unsigned n, unsigned bytes) {
      count = n;
      size = bytes;
    }
    BufPool::~BufPool() { ZmAssert_(!unsigned(m_used)); }
    
    void BufPool::init(
      ZmRef<UMem> arena, uint64_t offset, unsigned stride, unsigned prefix, unsigned first)
    {
      ZmAssert_(!unsigned(m_used));
      m_active = 0;
      m_arena = ZuMv(arena);
      m_offset = offset;
      m_shift = __builtin_ctz(stride);
      m_prefix = prefix;
      m_first = first;
      m_tx = offset >= m_arena->layout().rxLength;
      m_head = 0;
      // Same non-sharded payload-overlay slist initialization as ZmHeap arenas.
      for (unsigned i = count; i; --i) {
        auto p = backing(i - 1);
        reinterpret_cast<ZmAtomic<uintptr_t> *>(p)->store_(m_head.load_());
        m_head.store_(uintptr_t(p));
      }
      m_active = 1;
    }
    
    uint8_t *BufPool::alloc()
    {
      if (ZuUnlikely(!unsigned(m_active))) return nullptr;
      uintptr_t p;
    loop:
      p = m_head.load_();
      if (ZuUnlikely(!p)) return nullptr;
      if (ZuUnlikely(p & 1)) { ZmAtomic_acquire(); goto loop; }
      if (ZuUnlikely(m_head.cmpXch(p | 1, p) != p)) goto loop;
      ++m_used;
      m_head = reinterpret_cast<ZmAtomic<uintptr_t> *>(p)->load_();
      if (m_tx) m_arena->txSlot(*this, slot(reinterpret_cast<void *>(p))).refs = 1;
      return reinterpret_cast<uint8_t *>(p);
    }
    
    void BufPool::free(uint8_t *packet)
    {
      auto id = slot(packet);
      ZmAssert_(id != NoSlot);
      if (m_tx && --m_arena->txSlot(*this, id).refs) return;
      auto p = backing(id);
      uintptr_t next;
    loop:
      next = m_head.load_();
      if (next & 1) { ZmAtomic_acquire(); goto loop; }
      reinterpret_cast<ZmAtomic<uintptr_t> *>(p)->store_(next);
      if (m_head.cmpXch(uintptr_t(p), next) != next) goto loop;
      // Final accounting follows publication; no mapping access follows it.
      ZmAssert_(m_used--);
    }
    
    unsigned BufPool::slot(const void *packet) const
    {
      if (!m_arena) return NoSlot;
      auto begin = uintptr_t(m_arena->data()) + m_offset + m_prefix;
      auto address = uintptr_t(packet);
      if (address < begin) return NoSlot;
      auto offset = address - begin;
      auto id = offset>>m_shift;
      auto within = offset & (stride() - 1);
      return id < count && within < size ? unsigned(id) : NoSlot;
    }
    bool BufPool::owns(const void *packet) const { return slot(packet) != NoSlot; }
    bool BufPool::writable(const void *packet) const
    {
      auto id = slot(packet);
      return m_tx && id != NoSlot && unsigned(m_arena->txSlot(*this, id).refs) == 1;
    }
    uint8_t *BufPool::backing(unsigned id) const {
      ZmAssert_(m_arena && id < count);
      return m_arena->data() + m_offset + (uint64_t(id)<<m_shift) + m_prefix;
    }

    class Instance final : public ZmNHeap<Instance>, public Zxdp::Instance {
    friend inline ZuStringT<"Zxdp.Instance"> ZmNHeapID(Instance *);

        return queue && queue->socket.zeroCopy();

      ZuUnion<void, ZeException> init(const Zxdp::Params &params) override {
        if (m_state != Cold)
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "AF_XDP instance has already been initialized");
        m_state = Closing;
        if (!params.is<Params>())
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "AF_XDP instance requires XDP parameters");
        const auto &config = params.p<Params>();
        m_ifindex = config.ifindex;
        m_rxPool = dynamic_cast<BufPool *>(config.rxPool.ptr());
        m_receive = config.rx;
        m_txStopped = config.txStopped;
        m_spin = config.spin;
        m_scheduler = config.scheduler;
        m_txSid = config.txSid;
        m_txPools.length(config.txPools.count_());
        {
          auto pools = config.txPools.citer();
          unsigned i = 0;
          while (auto pool = pools()) m_txPools[i++] = static_cast<Zi::IOBufPool *>(pool);
        }
        if (!m_ifindex || !m_rxPool || !m_receive) {
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "interface, Rx pool and receive callback are required");
        }
        if (!m_scheduler || !m_txSid || m_txSid > m_scheduler->params().nThreads()) {
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "AF_XDP requires a scheduler and assigned Tx slot");
        }
        auto parsed = parseFilter(config.netmask);
        if (parsed.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(parsed).p<ZeException>();
        auto filter = ZuMv(parsed).p<Filter>();
        auto queried = queryLink(m_ifindex);
        if (queried.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(queried).p<ZeException>();
        m_link = ZuMv(queried).p<LinkState>();
        if (m_link.occupied())
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "interface has an unrelated XDP program");
        if (!m_link.rxQueues || m_rxPool->count < m_link.rxQueues) {
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "Rx pool must provision every interface queue");
        }
        auto created = UMem::create(config.txPools, m_rxPool.ptr(), m_link.mtu);
        if (created.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(created).p<ZeException>();
        m_arena = ZuMv(created).p<ZmRef<UMem>>();
        const auto &layout = m_arena->layout();
        auto round = [](unsigned n) -> unsigned {
          if (n > (unsigned(1)<<31)) return 0;
          if (n < 2) return 2;
          return unsigned(1)<<(32 - __builtin_clz(n - 1));
        };
        auto r = round(layout.rxCount/m_link.rxQueues + !!(layout.rxCount%m_link.rxQueues));
        auto t = round(layout.txCount);
        if (!r || !t) { return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "AF_XDP ring capacity overflow"); }
        m_rxSlots.length(m_rxPool->count);
        m_rxActive.length(m_rxPool->count);
        m_txActive.length(layout.txCount);

        if (m_events < 0) { return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", ([error = ZeLastError](auto &out) {
        out << "AF_XDP epoll creation failed: " << error;
          })); }
        m_wakeFD = eventfd(0, EFD_NONBLOCK | EFD_CLOEXEC);
        if (m_wakeFD < 0) { return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", ([error = ZeLastError](auto &out) {
        out << "AF_XDP wake eventfd creation failed: " << error;
          })); }
        epoll_event wakeEvent{};
        wakeEvent.events = EPOLLIN;
        wakeEvent.data.u32 = End;
        if (epoll_ctl(m_events, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, m_wakeFD, &wakeEvent)) {
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", ([error = ZeLastError](auto &out) {
        out << "AF_XDP wake registration failed: " << error;
          }));
        }
        auto loaded = m_program.load(m_link.rxQueues, filter);
        if (loaded.is<ZeException>()) return loaded;
        auto attached = m_attachment.attach(m_ifindex, m_program);
        if (attached.is<ZeException>()) return attached;
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < m_link.rxQueues; ++i) {
          auto queue = m_queues[i] = new Queue;
          queue->quota = layout.rxCount/m_link.rxQueues + (i < layout.rxCount%m_link.rxQueues);
          auto opened = queue->socket.open(m_arena, m_ifindex, i, r, i ? 2 : t,
        i ? m_queues[0]->socket.fd() : -1);
          if (opened.is<ZeException>()) return opened;
          auto id = ZuID{} << "xdp." << ZuBoxed(m_ifindex) << '.' << ZuBoxed(i) << '.';
          auto owner = ZuID{m_scheduler->id()};
          queue->socket.rx().identify(owner, ZuID{id} << "rx", Ztc::QueueType::Rx,
        queue->socket.fd());
          queue->socket.fill().identify(owner, ZuID{id} << "fill", Ztc::QueueType::Tx);
          queue->socket.tx().identify(owner, ZuID{id} << "tx", Ztc::QueueType::Tx);
          queue->socket.comp().identify(owner, ZuID{id} << "cq", Ztc::QueueType::Rx);
          auto published = m_program.publish(i, queue->socket.fd());
          if (published.is<ZeException>()) return published;
          epoll_event event{};
          event.events = EPOLLIN;
          event.data.u32 = i;
          if (epoll_ctl(m_events, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, queue->socket.fd(), &event)) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", ([error = ZeLastError](auto &out) {
        out << "AF_XDP readiness registration failed: " << error;
          }));
          }
        }
        m_txConsumed = m_queues[0]->socket.tx().consumed();
        m_state = Active;
        m_txExit = m_txExited = 0;
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < m_link.rxQueues; ++i)
          replenish(*m_queues[i], m_queues[i]->quota);
        return {};
      }
      ZuUnion<bool, ZeException> close() override {
        if (m_state == Closed) return true;
        m_state = Closing;
        if (!stopTx()) return false;
        if (m_arena && m_rxPool->ready()) {
          m_rxPool->retire();
          for (const auto &pool : m_txPools) static_cast<BufPool *>(pool.ptr())->retire();
        }
        // Retire one queue per call. No packet backing returns before every queue
        // has independently proved the end of kernel access.
        if (m_closeQueue < m_queues.length()) {
          ZmGuard guard(m_queueLock);
          auto queue = m_queues[m_closeQueue];
          if (queue) {
        if (m_program.fd() >= 0) {
          auto quiesced = m_program.quiesce(m_closeQueue);
          if (quiesced.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(quiesced).p<ZeException>();
        }
        if (queue->published) {
          auto &retirement = queue->retirement;
          ZuUnion<int, ZeException> result = retirement.done() ?
            ZuUnion<int, ZeException>{int(KernelRetirement::Done)} :
            retirement.waiting() ? retirement.retry() : retirement.begin(queue->socket);
          if (result.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(result).p<ZeException>();
          if (result.p<int>() != KernelRetirement::Done) return false;
          retirement.reset();
        } else queue->socket.close();
          }
          if (++m_closeQueue < m_queues.length()) return false;
        }
        if (m_events >= 0) { ::close(m_events); m_events = -1; }
        if (m_wakeFD >= 0) { ::close(m_wakeFD); m_wakeFD = -1; }
        unsigned budget = Quantum;
        while (m_rxHeld && budget--) {
          auto id = m_rxActive[--m_rxHeld];
          m_rxSlots[id] = End;
          m_rxPool->BufPool::free(m_rxPool->backing(id));
        }
        if (m_rxHeld) return false;
        budget = Quantum;
        while (m_txHeld && budget--) {
          auto p = m_txActive[--m_txHeld];
          auto pool = m_arena->pool(p);
          auto &slot = m_arena->txSlot(*pool, pool->slot(p));
          slot.pending = false;
          slot.active = End;
          pool->BufPool::free(p);
        }
        if (m_txHeld) return false;
        auto detached = m_attachment.detach();
        if (m_attachment.ifindex()) {
          if (detached.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(detached).p<ZeException>();
          return false;
        }
        m_program.reset();
        m_state = Closed;
        if (m_ioError) {
          return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", ([error = ZeError{int(m_ioError)}](auto &out) {
        out << "AF_XDP I/O failed: " << error;
          }));
        }
        if (detached.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(detached).p<ZeException>();
        return true;
      }
    
      bool stopTx() override {
        if (unsigned(m_txExited)) return true;
        if (m_scheduler->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped) {
          m_txPending = 0;
          m_txExit = m_txExited = 1;
          return true;
        }
        // The Tx producer is quiescent. This FIFO barrier drains queued sends;
        // callbacks never enqueue successors, so none can overtake the barrier.
        if (!m_txExit.xch(1)) {
          m_scheduler->run([this, stopped = m_txStopped] {
        // Descriptor accounting ends here; CQ or safe socket retirement still
        // owns every submitted backing lease.
        m_txPending = 0;
        m_txExited = 1;
        if (stopped) stopped();
          }, m_txSid);
          return false;
        }
        return unsigned(m_txExited);
      }
    
    private:
    
      void replenish(Queue &queue, unsigned budget) {
        auto &socket = queue.socket;
        const auto &layout = m_arena->layout();
        auto available = socket.fill().available();
        if (budget > available) budget = available;
        auto room = queue.quota - queue.rxHeld;
        if (budget > room) budget = room;
        while (budget--) {
          auto p = m_rxPool->BufPool::alloc();
          if (!p) break;
          auto id = m_rxPool->slot(p);
          ZmAssert_(m_rxSlots[id] == End && socket.fill().reserve(1) == 1);
          m_rxSlots[id] = m_rxHeld;
          m_rxActive[m_rxHeld++] = id;
          socket.fill().entry(0) = uint64_t(id) * layout.chunk;
          socket.fill().commit();
          ++queue.rxHeld;
          queue.published = true;
        }
      }
    
      void serveTx() {
        if (unsigned(m_txExit) || unsigned(m_state) != Active) return;
        auto &socket = m_queues[0]->socket;
        auto &ring = socket.tx();
        while (!unsigned(m_txExit)) {
          if (sendto(socket.fd(), nullptr, 0, MSG_DONTWAIT, nullptr, 0) < 0 &&
          errno != EINTR && errno != EAGAIN && errno != EBUSY && errno != ENOBUFS) {
        m_ioError = errno;
        m_state = Closing;
        notify();
        return;
          }
          auto consumed = ring.consumed();
          unsigned n = uint32_t(consumed - m_txConsumed);
          // Keep ownership during a short idle spin. The producer counts each
          // descriptor before publishing it, including work not yet consumed.
          for (unsigned i = 0; i < m_spin && m_txPending.load_() <= n; ++i)
        if (unsigned(m_txExit)) return;
          if (unsigned(m_txExit)) return;
          if (!n) continue;
          m_txConsumed = consumed;
          // The RMW closes the last-drain race: an earlier increment keeps this
          // invocation active; a later zero-to-one increment queues its successor.
          if (!(m_txPending -= n)) return;
        }
      }
    
      void notify() {
        if (m_wakeFD < 0) return;
        // Count every scheduler pulse, but interrupt the kernel only when Rx has
        // published a wait attempt. The ordered increment pairs with parking.xch
        // and the receiver's final pulse check; neither side can miss the other.
        ++m_wakes;
        if (!unsigned(m_parking)) return;
        uint64_t one = 1;
        while (::write(m_wakeFD, &one, sizeof(one)) < 0) {
          if (errno == EINTR) continue;
          ZmAssert_(errno == EAGAIN); // already readable on eventfd saturation
          break;
        }
      }
    
      void drainWake() {
        uint64_t value;
        while (::read(m_wakeFD, &value, sizeof(value)) < 0) {
          if (errno == EINTR) continue;
          ZmAssert_(errno == EAGAIN);
          break;
        }
      }
    
      bool woken() {
        if (!uint64_t(m_wakes)) return false;
        --m_wakes; // only the single Rx owner consumes pulses
        return true;
      }
    
      unsigned receiveQueue(unsigned q);
    
    
      enum { Quantum = 64, End = unsigned(-1) };
      enum { Cold, Active, Closing, Closed };
      using Indices = ZtArray<unsigned, ZtArrayHeapID<"Zxdp.RxSlots">>;
      using Packets = ZtArray<uint8_t *, ZtArrayHeapID<"Zxdp.TxActive">>;
      using Queues = ZtArray<Queue *, ZtArrayHeapID<"Zxdp.Queues">>;
      using Pools = ZtArray<ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool>, ZtArrayHeapID<"Zxdp.Pools">>;
      Pools        m_txPools;
      using RxPool = ZmRef<BufPool>;
      RxPool    m_rxPool;
      RecvFn    m_receive;
      StopFn    m_txStopped;
      LinkState    m_link;
      unsigned    m_ifindex = 0, m_spin = 1000;
      ZmScheduler    *m_scheduler = nullptr;
      unsigned    m_txSid = 0;
      ZmRef<UMem>    m_arena;
      BPFProgram    m_program;
      BPFAttach    m_attachment;
      Queues    m_queues;
      mutable ZmLock m_queueLock; // cold enumeration versus mapping retirement only
      int        m_events = -1, m_wakeFD = -1;
      ZmAtomic<unsigned> m_state{Cold}, m_txExit{1}, m_txExited{1};
      ZmAtomic<int> m_ioError{0};
      unsigned    m_closeQueue = 0;
      alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) ZmAtomic<unsigned> m_txPending{0};
      alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) ZmAtomic<uint64_t> m_wakes{0};
      ZmAtomic<unsigned> m_parking{0};
      alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) Indices m_rxSlots;
      Indices    m_rxActive;
      unsigned    m_rxHeld = 0, m_nextQueue = 0;
      alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) Packets m_txActive;
      unsigned    m_txHeld = 0;
      // Sender-only accounting must not invalidate shared immutable packet views.
      alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) uint32_t m_txConsumed = 0;
    };
    
    ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool> Instance::bufPool(
      unsigned count, unsigned size, unsigned headRoom, unsigned tailRoom, unsigned align)
    {
      ZmRef<BufPool> pool = new BufPool{count, size};
      pool->headRoom = headRoom;
      pool->tailRoom = tailRoom;
      pool->align = align;
      return pool;
    }
    
    unsigned Instance::allQueues(Ztc::QueueMgr::AllFn fn) const
    {
      ZmGuard guard(m_queueLock);
      unsigned count = 0;
      for (auto queue : m_queues) {
        if (!queue) continue;
        auto &socket = queue->socket;
        fn(&socket.rx()); fn(&socket.fill()); fn(&socket.tx()); fn(&socket.comp());
        count += 4;
      }
      return count;
    }
    bool Instance::send(uint8_t *packet, unsigned length)
    {
      if (!ready() || !packet || !length) return false;
      auto pool = m_arena->pool(packet);
      if (!pool || pool == m_rxPool.ptr()) return false;
      auto id = pool->slot(packet);
      if (id == BufPool::NoSlot) return false;
      auto canonical = pool->backing(id);
      auto wire = unsigned(packet - canonical);
      if (length > pool->size - wire) return false;
      auto &slot = m_arena->txSlot(*pool, id);
      if (slot.pending) return false;
      auto &ring = m_queues[0]->socket.tx();
      if (m_txHeld == ring.count() || !ring.reserve(1)) return false;
      slot.wire = wire;
      slot.active = m_txHeld;
      m_txActive[m_txHeld++] = canonical;
      slot.pending = true;
      ++slot.refs;
      auto address = uint64_t(packet - m_arena->data());
      ring.entry(0) = {address, length, 0};
      bool idle = !m_txPending++;
      ring.commit();
      if (idle) m_scheduler->run([this] { serveTx(); }, m_txSid);
      return true;
    }
    
    void Instance::rx()
    {
      unsigned idle = 0, empty = 0;
      auto queueCount = m_queues.length(); // frozen until the caller quiesces Rx for close
      while (ready()) {
        if (woken()) return;
        auto q = m_nextQueue++;
        if (m_nextQueue == queueCount) m_nextQueue = 0;
        if (receiveQueue(q)) { idle = empty = 0; continue; }
        // Check/replenish each hardware queue before parking. This visits queues,
        // never searches packets or buffers, and is independent of arena capacity.
        if (++empty < queueCount) continue;
        empty = 0;
        if (idle < m_spin) { ++idle; continue; }
        // Publish before rechecking pulses. A producer either sees this wait and
        // writes eventfd, or its already-published pulse prevents the wait entirely.
        m_parking.xch(1);
        if (uint64_t(m_wakes)) { m_parking = 0; continue; }
        epoll_event event;
        auto n = epoll_wait(m_events, &event, 1, -1);
        m_parking = 0;
        if (n < 0) {
          if (errno == EINTR) continue;
          m_ioError = errno;
          m_state = Closing;
          return;
        }
        // A delayed writer can leave stale readiness after its pulse was consumed.
        // Draining readiness never creates a pulse; only woken() permits a return.
        if (event.data.u32 == End) drainWake();
        else m_nextQueue = event.data.u32;
        idle = 0;
      }
    }
    
    unsigned Instance::receiveQueue(unsigned q)
    {
      auto &queue = *m_queues[q];
      auto &socket = queue.socket;
      auto &ring = socket.rx();
      // Empty probes need no service work unless FILL can accept returned backing
      // or the driver requests a wake. Keep both checks live even during long spins.
      if (!ring.available() && !socket.fill().needWakeup() &&
          (queue.rxHeld == queue.quota || m_rxPool->used() >= m_rxPool->count)) return 0;
      replenish(queue, Quantum);
      if (socket.fill().needWakeup()) {
        pollfd wake{socket.fd(), POLLIN, 0};
        poll(&wake, 1, 0);
      }
      const auto &layout = m_arena->layout();
      unsigned n = 0;
      while (n < Quantum && !m_wakes.load_() && ring.reserve(1)) {
        auto desc = ring.entry(0);
        ring.commit();
        ++n;
        if (desc.addr >= layout.rxLength) continue;
        auto id = unsigned(desc.addr/layout.chunk);
        if (id >= m_rxPool->count) continue;
        auto &index = m_rxSlots[id];
        if (index == End) continue;
        --queue.rxHeld;
        auto last = --m_rxHeld;
        if (index != last) {
          auto moved = m_rxActive[last];
          m_rxActive[index] = moved;
          m_rxSlots[moved] = index;
        }
        index = End;
        auto p = m_arena->data() + desc.addr;
        auto slot = m_rxPool->slot(p);
        auto origin = m_rxPool->backing(id);
        if (slot != id || !desc.len || desc.options ||
        desc.len > m_rxPool->size ||
        desc.len > layout.chunk - unsigned(desc.addr & (layout.chunk - 1))) {
          m_rxPool->BufPool::free(origin);
          continue;
        }
        m_receive(p, desc.len);
      }
      if (n) replenish(queue, Quantum);
      return n;
    }
    
    unsigned Instance::pollTx()
    {
      if (!ready()) return 0;
      unsigned count = 0;
      auto &ring = m_queues[0]->socket.comp();
      auto n = ring.reserve(Quantum);
      const auto &layout = m_arena->layout();
      for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        auto address = ring.entry(i);
        if (address < layout.rxLength || address >= layout.length) continue;
        auto p = m_arena->data() + address;
        auto pool = m_arena->pool(p);
        if (!pool) continue;
        auto id = pool->slot(p);
        if (id == BufPool::NoSlot) continue;
        auto canonical = pool->backing(id);
        auto &slot = m_arena->txSlot(*pool, id);
        // Generic Linux Tx tags the skb destructor address in bit zero and CQ
        // clears that bit. A slot has only one outstanding descriptor; compare
        // its offset excluding that tag, without a search or extra bookkeeping.
        if (!slot.pending || ((slot.wire ^ unsigned(p - canonical)) & ~1U)) continue;
        slot.pending = false;
        auto last = --m_txHeld;
        if (slot.active != last) {
          auto moved = m_txActive[last];
          m_txActive[slot.active] = moved;
          auto owner = m_arena->pool(moved);
          m_arena->txSlot(*owner, owner->slot(moved)).active = slot.active;
        }
        slot.active = End;
        pool->BufPool::free(canonical);
        ++count;
      }
      ring.commit();
      return count;
    }
    
    } // namespace Xdp
    
    ZmRef<Instance> instance(Type::T type)
    {
      switch (type) {
        case Type::Xdp: return new Xdp::Instance;
        default: return nullptr;
      }
    }
    
    } // namespace Zxdp
