    ## Analysis and adopted design
    
    ### Backend selection and instance parameters
    
    Extend the existing declarations in `Zxdp.hh` using its current enum macro form:
    
    ```cpp
    namespace Zxdp {
    
    ZtEnumNS(ZxdpAPI, Type, uint8_t, Xdp, Dpdk);
    
    // Existing Params_ retains its owning Tx list, Rx reference, callback,
    // spin, scheduler and txStopped fields.
    namespace Dpdk {
      struct Params : public Params_ {
        ZtString<> name;            // DPDK Ethernet device name
        unsigned rxInterval = 50;   // maximum idle wait, microseconds; zero polls
      };
    }
    ZuDerive(Params, (ZuUnion<Xdp::Params, Dpdk::Params>));
    
    } // namespace Zxdp
    ```
    
    Use `instance(Type::Dpdk)` to obtain `Dpdk::Instance`, then allocate pools,
    populate backend parameters in place, and call `init(config)`. For example:
    
    ```cpp
    auto backend = Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Dpdk);
    auto tx = backend->bufPool(txCount, packetSize);
    auto rx = backend->bufPool(rxCount, packetSize);
    Zxdp::Params config(
      Zxdp::Params::New<Zxdp::Params::Index<Zxdp::Dpdk::Params>{}>{});
    auto &params = config.p<Zxdp::Dpdk::Params>();
    params.name = "net_ring0";
    params.txPools.pushNode(tx.ptr());
    params.rxPool = rx;
    params.rx = receive;
    params.spin = 1000;
    params.rxInterval = 50;
    auto result = backend->init(config);
    ```
    
    EAL must already have been explicitly initialized before selecting a DPDK
    backend. Pool objects retain their independent factory/instance lifetime as in
    the current interface. Copy required configuration into the instance during init;
    the parameter union may expire after init. Retain pool references for packets
    that outlive the instance, and freeze geometry while bound.
    
    `Xdp::Params` keeps `ifindex`, `netmask`, `txSid` and `txThread`.
    Do not put AF_XDP sender settings into `Dpdk::Params`. Resolve the DPDK Ethernet
    name once with `rte_eth_dev_get_port_by_name()` and store its `uint16_t port_id`
    privately. Do not add the obsolete `Backend`, `If_AF_XDP`, `If_DPDK`, `If`,
    `Params::backend`, `Params::interface`, or `instance(const Params &)` APIs.
    
    ### Adopted consumer integration scope
    
    Include DPDK selection and pool provisioning through Zutcp, for initial startup
    and restart. Update `zutcp/src/ZutcpMx.hh` and `zutcp/src/ZutcpMx.cc`; do not
    limit this work to standalone Zxdp service.
    
    Zdb's table replication allocator must request `Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP` through
    `ZiMultiplex::allocator()`. Change the network-multiplexer-backed
    `tableBufAllocFn<T>()` in `zdb/src/ZdbBuf.hh` from `App` to `TxTCP`, retaining
    the table's configured size, alignment, heap identity and count policy. This
    routes allocation through the selected transport plugin and its native pool.
    The table's configured size remains the requested size; Zutcp constrains the
    transport allocation to MTU/payload capacity and supplies protocol headroom.
    Do not replace every application pool request with a fixed MTU-sized request.
    
    The current `ZiMultiplex::allocator()` already delegates TxTCP allocation to its
    plugin. The earlier observed App-type bypass is corrected at the Zdb caller,
    rather than by changing generic App allocation dispatch. Scope the associated
    Zdb allocation/replication test updates to this transport-type change.
    
    ### Explicit EAL ownership
    
    Move the previously adopted DPDK-only configuration and lifecycle under
    `Zxdp::Dpdk`: call the process-wide wrapper `Dpdk::EAL` and its configuration
    `Dpdk::EALParams`. This avoids colliding with per-instance `Dpdk::Params`.
    These names replace the earlier `Zxdp::DPDK` and `Zxdp::DPDKParams` spellings;
    the adopted fields and explicit initialization policy are unchanged.
    
    Use `ZmSingleton<Dpdk::EAL, ZmSingletonCleanup<ZmCleanup::Platform>>`.
    The application explicitly calls `init(const EALParams &)` and checks its
    structured result before selecting an instance. Singleton discovery/construction
    must not initialize EAL behind the scenes. DPDK selection/init requires prior
    successful initialization; AF_XDP is independent of this wrapper. EAL persists
    across individual instance close/recreate, and its destructor finalizes EAL after
    successful initialization.
    
    `Platform` cleanup follows Application/Library and precedes heap/thread cleanup.
    Retire instances, pools and held mbufs before final EAL cleanup; do not depend on
    ordering within a cleanup level. Use normal structured `ZeException` results and
    `ZiLOG(Fatal, ([...](auto &s) { s << ...; }));` where appropriate.
    
    ### Native pool backing and direct send
    
    Implement internal `Dpdk::BufPool : Zi::IOBufPool`, constructed by
    `Dpdk::Instance::bufPool(...)`. Keep `Xdp::BufPool` internal and unchanged in
    purpose. Both implementations honor the common pool geometry/identity and
    allocation/return/writable interface using their own backing.
    
    The DPDK pool supplies native mbuf backing from allocation onward. A packet
    received by DPDK send already identifies its mbuf; submit it directly without
    payload copies or external-buffer attachment. True means accepted submission;
    false acquires no submission lease and preserves caller ownership. Use native
    mbuf ownership/reference counting for asynchronous driver reclamation and any
    caller-retained backing, just as Xdp implements the same lifetime contract for
    UMEM. Reclamation accounting for `pollTx()` and `writable()` is ordinary backend
    implementation work, not another architectural feasibility gate.
    
    Derive queue/descriptor and preallocated bookkeeping capacity from `txPools` and
    `rxPool`, honoring driver constraints. Do not add duplicate public sizing knobs.
    Keep direct packet identity and allocation-free packet service. Backend-native
    pool implementations supersede the earlier shared-arena proposal.
    
    ### Service, shutdown and queries
    
    * Submit to DPDK on the existing Tx owner. Keep one owner for each Rx/Tx queue
      and serialize PMD submission/reclamation accordingly. Do not require the
      AF_XDP `txSid`/`txThread` service in DPDK.
    * Implement the current `stopTx()` contract for direct Tx: quiesce submission
      and honor the existing `txStopped` continuation semantics without inventing
      a sender thread. Keep that notification distinct from complete device/buffer
      retirement. `close()` retains the explicit true/pending/error result and
      caller-driven retry contract, including failed-init rollback.
    * `zeroCopy()` reports the instance's actual running mode, not backend selection
      or device capability alone. `mtu()` and `mac()` report device values.
    * Add the previously adopted pure virtual `void status()` and implement it in
      both backends with `ZiLOG(Info, ([...](auto &s) { s << ...; }));`, capturing
      state safely. Include useful backend/device/lifecycle and operating-mode
      details. Keep interface-specific numeric identity private.
    * `allQueues()` reports normalized telemetry for actual queues/rings using
      available DPDK APIs or reads through the current telemetry framework.
    
    ### Receive idle policy
    
    The adopted priority order is sustained receive latency, avoiding extended full
    CPU consumption, then packet-triggered wake from extended idle.
    
    1. While packets arrive, immediately retrieve the next burst. Check counted wake
       state between bounded batches. No sleep or wait syscall on sustained input.
    2. After empty input, spin for `Params_::spin` rounds; any packet resets the
       budget. Preserve brief spinning across short gaps.
    3. Use native packet-arrival waiting where available. Ring producer-head memory
       monitoring can improve a bounded short-idle phase on supported CPUs, but
       does not itself mean kernel descheduling or a free core.
    4. For extended idle without packet-arrival notification, wait on the internal
      an extra DPDK sender; a transport runtime; wider test or observability projects;
      claims of hardware DMA/offload validation from software PMDs.
    
    ## Alternatives Weighed
    
    * The original Backend enum, tagged If and configuration-taking namespace factory
      are superseded by the current Type selector and two-stage select/pool/init API.
    * Implicit EAL initialization in an InstanceMgr was rejected in favor of explicit
      configuration through the DPDK-only singleton wrapper.
    * A submission queue for CommitFn is unnecessary after the completed boolean-send
      change. An extra Tx core is not part of the selected direct DPDK path.
    * A shared arena and external-buffer attachment are superseded by native backend
      implementations of `Zi::IOBufPool`.
    * Separate public ring sizing duplicates the accepted pool-driven provisioning.
    * Continuous polling during extended idle is optional (`rxInterval == 0`);
      the default uses brief spinning and bounded timed waits to reduce idle CPU.
    
    ## Key Decisions & Staging for Next Steps
    
    1. Extend `Type` with Dpdk and `Params` with `Dpdk::Params`. Keep `Xdp::Params`
       and internals in their existing namespace. Add the adopted status operation.
    2. Add the public Dpdk EAL configuration/wrapper and private backend/pool
       implementations, with repository-prefixed source/header names (for example
       `ZxdpDpdk.hh/.cc` and `ZxdpDpdkPool.hh/.cc`). Export only caller-required
       EAL configuration/API declarations; keep concrete mbuf internals private.
    3. Add the DPDK dependency through configure/pkg-config conventions and extend
       `zxdp/src/Makefile.am`, preserving its existing Zi dependency and installed
       versus private header boundary. Do not repeat the completed Zi pool migration.
    4. Implement pool-derived queue setup, direct Tx, native reclamation, receive,
       counted wakes, stopTx and structured retryable close. Add DPDK selection and
       initial/restart provisioning in `zutcp/src/ZutcpMx.hh/.cc`. Change the
       replication `tableBufAllocFn<T>()` in `zdb/src/ZdbBuf.hh` to request TxTCP
       buffers, preserving table-requested geometry and plugin MTU constraints.
       Use the current union initialization and owning pool APIs without shims.
    5. Mirror existing AF_XDP unit/integration coverage using ring/pcap fixtures
       through the same DPDK path. Keep peer progress, Rx-pool provenance and queued
       mbuf draining in fixture implementation; do not expand the validation scope.
       Follow `docs/BUILD.md` for dependency builds and relevant tests.

      ZmRef<IOBuf> grantBuf(
        uint8_t *data, void *owner, uint32_t length, uint32_t mps)
      {
        uint32_t ps = capacity();
        if (ps > mps) ps = mps;
        ZmRef<IOBuf> buf = new IOBufStub<Buf, HeapID>(
          data, ps + headRoom + tailRoom, this, owner, length, false, true);
        buf->skip = headRoom;

      ZmRef<IOBuf> allocBuf(
        void *owner = nullptr, uint32_t length = 0, uint32_t mps = ~uint32_t(0)) override
      {
        if constexpr (
        Type == IOBufType::TxUDP ||
        Type == IOBufType::TxTCP) {
          // registered tx buffer
          uint32_t ps = capacity();
          if (ps > mps) ps = mps;
          if (length > ps) return nullptr;
          auto data = pool->alloc();
          if (ZuUnlikely(!data)) return nullptr;
          return grantBuf(data, owner, length, mps);
        } else {
          // registered rx buffer - stub only
          if (length) return nullptr;
          ZmRef<IOBuf> buf = new IOBufStub<Buf, HeapID>(
        nullptr, 0, this, owner, 0, false, true);
          buf->skip = headRoom;
          return buf;
        }
      }
    
      uint8_t *alloc(uint32_t size) const override {
        return static_cast<uint8_t *>(VHeap::alloc(size));
      }
      void free(uint8_t *ptr, uint32_t size, bool registered) const override {
        if (registered)
          return pool->free(ptr);
        else
          VHeap::free(ptr, size);
      }
    };

    struct Params_ {
      Zi::IOBufPoolList txPools;
      ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool> rxPool;
      RecvFn rx;
      unsigned spin = 1000; // idle probes before Rx blocks or Tx service returns
      ZmScheduler *scheduler = nullptr; // caller-owned scheduler
      StopFn txStopped; // optional owner continuation after sender callbacks drain
    };
    
    namespace Xdp {
      struct Params : public Params_ {
        unsigned ifindex = 0; // network-interface index in the current network namespace
        ZuCSpan netmask; // optional destination CIDR; empty takes all traffic
        unsigned txSid = 0; // application-assigned sender slot
        ZmSchedTParams txThread = ZmSchedTParams().isolated(true);
      };
    }
    ZuDerive(Params, (ZuUnion<Xdp::Params>));
    
    // The caller drives Rx/Tx on their respective single owners. Allocation/free
    // may run on other threads. Allocation holds backing until explicit pool return;
    // an accepted send also holds it until kernel completion or safe close.
    class ZxdpAPI Instance : public ZmPolymorph {
    public:
      ~Instance() override = default;
      Instance(const Instance &) = delete;
      Instance &operator =(const Instance &) = delete;
    
      // Pools are independent of the factory instance and can precede init().
      virtual ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool> bufPool(unsigned count, unsigned size,
        unsigned headRoom = 0, unsigned tailRoom = 0,
        unsigned align = ZiIOBuf_DefltAlign) = 0;
      // Initialize once. Retain the handle after failure and close it to finish
      // rollback. Configuration may expire on return; pool references are retained.
      virtual ZuUnion<void, ZeException> init(const Params &) = 0;
    
      virtual bool ready() const = 0;
      virtual unsigned mtu() const = 0;
      virtual bool zeroCopy() const = 0;
      virtual ZuBSpan mac() const = 0;
    
      // False acquires no kernel lease. After true, keep bytes immutable until
      // kernel retirement. One descriptor may be outstanding for each slot.
      virtual bool send(uint8_t *packet, unsigned length) = 0;
      virtual void rx() = 0; // Rx owner, until wake() or device failure
      virtual void wake() = 0;
      virtual unsigned pollTx() = 0;
      virtual bool stopTx() = 0;
      // Quiesce Rx, Tx and wake callers first. True means closed, false means
      // retirement is pending; an error never authorizes releasing kernel backing.
      virtual ZuUnion<bool, ZeException> close() = 0;
    
      virtual unsigned allQueues(Ztc::QueueMgr::AllFn) const = 0;
    
    protected:
      Instance() = default;
    };
    
    ZxdpExtern ZmRef<Instance> instance(Type::T);
    
    } // namespace Zxdp
    #endif /* Zxdp_HH */

    template <typename L> void Stack::Connections::visit(ZiConnection *mx, L &&fn)
    {
      if (!mx->plugin()) return;
      switch (mx->info().type) {
        case ZiCxnType::TCPOut:
          fn(static_cast<Cli::State *>(mx->plugin())->impl());
          break;
        case ZiCxnType::TCPIn:
          fn(static_cast<Srv::State *>(mx->plugin())->impl());
          break;
      }
    }
    
    static unsigned requireMTU(ZiMultiplex *mx, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (!mx) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "packet interface requires a multiplexer");
      auto result = interfaceMTU(interface);
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) throw ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      return result.p<unsigned>();
    }
    
    static unsigned ingressCount(ZiMultiplex *mx, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (mx->rxBufSize()) return mx->rxBufSize();
      auto result = Zxdp::Xdp::queryLink(interface);
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) throw ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      // Idle queues retain their FILL allocations. Each active queue needs room
      // beyond one connection's default retained list before its oldest can return.
      uint64_t count = uint64_t(result.p<Zxdp::Xdp::LinkState>().rxQueues) *
        (uint64_t(DefaultRxRetainPerCxn) + mx->rxQuantum());
      if (count > UINT_MAX) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "Rx pool count overflow");
      return count > ZiIOBuf_DefltCount ? unsigned(count) : ZiIOBuf_DefltCount;
    }
    
    static unsigned requirePackets(unsigned count)
    {
      if (!count) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "empty native packet pool");
      return count;
    }
    
    static unsigned requireTCPSecrets(ISN &isn, TFOKey &tfo, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (!isn.init(interface))
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "secure TCP sequence initialization failed");
      if (!tfo.init())
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "secure Fast Open cookie initialization failed");
      return interface;
    }

    void Stack::addProvider(Allocator *p)
    {
      ZmREF(p);
      m_txCapacity += p->pool->count;
      p->nextProvider = m_providers;

    }
    
    Zi::IOBufPool *Stack::allocator(
      Zi::IOBufType::T type, unsigned size, unsigned align, unsigned count)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped);
      // Providers reserve complete output framing before Zi copies their geometry.
      enum { Ethernet = 14, IPv6 = 40, TCP = 60 };
      unsigned head;
      switch (type) {
        case Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP:
        case Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP: head = Ethernet + IPv6 + TCP; break;
        default: throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported network allocator role");
      }
      if (head >= m_mtu + Ethernet || !align || (align & (align - 1)) ||
          align > unsigned(sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)))
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported packet allocator geometry");
      if (type == Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP)
        return new RxAllocator{m_ingress, head, count, align};
      uint64_t bytes = uint64_t(size) + head;
      if (bytes > m_mtu + Ethernet) bytes = m_mtu + Ethernet;
      auto p = new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(count, unsigned(bytes), head, 0, align)};
      addProvider(p);
      return p;
    }

    namespace Zxdp::Xdp {
    
    class UMem;
    class BufPool;
    class Instance;
    
    // Keep pool objects alive through instance close and final packet return.
    // Freeze the list/count/size while bound. Exhaustion never allocates backing.
    class BufPool final : public ZmNHeap<BufPool>, public Zi::IOBufPool {
    friend inline ZuStringT<"Zxdp.Pool"> ZmNHeapID(BufPool *);
    friend class UMem;
    friend class Instance;
    
    public:
      using ZmNHeap<BufPool>::operator new;
      using ZmNHeap<BufPool>::operator delete;
      BufPool(unsigned count = 0, unsigned size = 0);
      ~BufPool() override;
      BufPool(const BufPool &) = delete;
      BufPool &operator =(const BufPool &) = delete;
    
      uint8_t *alloc() override;
      void free(uint8_t *packet) override;
    private:
      enum { NoSlot = unsigned(-1) };
    
      unsigned used() const { return unsigned(m_used); }
      bool ready() const { return unsigned(m_active); }
      unsigned slot(const void *) const;
      uint8_t *backing(unsigned slot) const;
    
      void init(ZmRef<UMem>, uint64_t offset, unsigned stride, unsigned prefix, unsigned first);
      void retire() { m_active = 0; }
      unsigned first() const { return m_first; }
      unsigned stride() const { return unsigned(1)<<m_shift; }
    
      using Head = ZmAtomic<uintptr_t>;
      using Count = ZmAtomic<unsigned>;
      ZmRef<UMem>    m_arena;
      uint64_t    m_offset = 0;
      unsigned    m_shift = 0, m_prefix = 0, m_first = 0;
      bool        m_tx = false;
      alignas(Zm::CacheLineSize) Head m_head{0};
      Count        m_used{0}, m_active{0};
    };
    
    } // namespace Zxdp::Xdp
    #endif /* ZxdpPool_HH */

## User

explain this; `zxdp` does not tx oversized or chained packets; is this about rx?

## Assistant

Yes, this is specifically about **Rx**.

DPDK may return a packet spanning multiple mbufs when receive scatter is enabled. Zxdp’s receive callback accepts one contiguous pointer and length, so it cannot represent such a chain directly.

The proposed policy is:

- Configure Rx for single-segment packets, with buffers large enough for the configured MTU.
- Leave receive scatter disabled.
- If an unexpected chained packet arrives, release it without passing it to the callback or copying it.

This adds no Tx segmentation or chaining behavior.

    {
        struct pmd_internals *internals = NULL;
        struct ring_queue *r = NULL;
        uint16_t i;
        int ret;
    
        if (rte_eal_process_type() != RTE_PROC_PRIMARY)

        ret = eth_dev_stop(dev);
    
        internals = dev->data->dev_private;

             */
            for (i = 0; i < dev->data->nb_rx_queues; i++) {
                r = dev->data->rx_queues[i];
                rte_ring_free(r->rng);
            }

    ### Cross-Shard Handoffs
    Small fixed-size information may be snapshotted and captured by value when
    posting to another shard. Examples include scalar counters, packet numbers, or
    bounded ACK ranges.
    
    Large or variable-size information should not be captured directly by lambda.
    Write it into a buffer or queue owned by the destination shard, then capture
    only the handle and fixed metadata needed to consume it. For Tx work, this
    usually means writing into a Tx buffer on the Tx side.
    
    Do not use `ZmLock` to make non-owner access acceptable. A lock can protect
    memory, but it does not preserve the sharding model and tends to hide work
    running on the wrong I/O thread.
    
    ### Lifetime
    I/O buffers and dependent structures should use raw back-pointers to owning
    link/session/connection/... objects where that is the local pattern.
    The owner is responsible for draining or cancelling dependent structures during
    shutdown before destruction. Do not keep links alive by adding buffer-level reference
    churn unless the ownership model explicitly requires it.
    
    ### Teardown
    Sharded I/O teardown requires a 3-phase asynchronous process:
    1. prevent further ingress, timer and I/O work (e.g. `m_up = false`), and post a teardown continuation on the rx thread to drain rx activity
    2. (in the rx thread continuation) post a teardown continuation on the tx thread to drain tx activity
    3. (in the tx thread continuation) complete the teardown and release object ownership
    - do NOT block except in the main thread, this is async continuation code
    - I/O buffers, queued lambdas etc. are populous short-lived objects owned by fewer longer-lived objects such as connections/links/sessions/streams
      - populous short-lived objects should not hold reference counts back to their owners, this anti-pattern:
        - causes reference-count churn in the owner
        - risks ownership cycles
      - such back-pointers should be raw pointers (example: `ZiIOBuf::owner`)
      - owners are responsible for draining all activity using orderly teardown as described above, ensuring that objects with stale backpointers cannot outlive their owners
    
    ### Slow Receivers
    If a slow receiver causes backpressure on a sender that sustains faster sending, the sender's tx buffer capacity will eventually be exceeded. With the kernel TCP stack, the limit is the usual socket buffer size. With `zutcp`, the limit is the tx buffer pool size. In either case, exceeding tx buffer capacity should close the connection. Do NOT implement blocking/waiting/propagating backpressure onwards - a slow receiver should NOT disrupt tx to other receivers.
    No additional oversized/chained receive policy or copying path is requested.
    Do not expand testing merely to satisfy this withdrawn design question.
    
    ## Author clarification: pool sizes
    
    Rx pool buffers are always MTU-sized. Configured Tx sizes may be below or
    above MTU. Clamp during buffer allocation so the application never sees a
    buffer exceeding MTU; do not clamp the configuration itself. Queue provisioning
    must not assume uniform sizes, infer MTU from a Tx configuration or force all
    Tx requests to MTU. The receive-segment question stays closed.
    
    ## A4 proposed resolution: reusable ports
    
    * `Dpdk::EAL` owns the configured device registrations for its lifetime.
    * An instance acquires exclusive use of one named port; concurrent binding of
      another instance to that port fails with a structured error.
    * Instance close quiesces Rx/Tx/wake callers, stops the port, and retires its
      queue-held mbuf references. It returns pending/error until safe retirement
      is established, then releases exclusive use. Caller-held buffer references
      remain valid independently.
    * Ordinary instance close does not call destructive `rte_eth_dev_close()`,
      remove the named device, or finalize EAL. A later instance can configure/start
      the same port with its supplied pools. Retain backing needed by any retained
      device queue state until that state is reconfigured or finalized.
    * Failed initialization unwinds only the instance's acquired resources; it does
      not remove the configured device. It preserves its handle for pending rollback.
    * Final EAL teardown closes its stopped ports before `rte_eal_cleanup()`.
    * Software fixtures stop producers/peers and drain queued mbufs before releasing
      their rings; ring stop alone does not perform that drain.
    
    Status: proposed; awaiting author adoption. This records port ownership/reuse,
    not a change to the public pool interface or backing-based receive accounting.
    `ZiLOG(Fatal, ([...](auto &s) { s << ...; }));` where appropriate.
    
    ### Native pool backing and direct send
    
    Implement internal `Dpdk::BufPool : Zi::IOBufPool`, constructed by
    `Dpdk::Instance::bufPool(...)`. Keep `Xdp::BufPool` internal and unchanged in
    purpose. Both implementations expose the common pool geometry and only
    `alloc()`/`free()` over their own backing. Storage identity and backend lease
    bookkeeping remain private implementation details.
    
    The DPDK pool supplies native mbuf backing from allocation onward. A packet
    received by DPDK send already identifies its mbuf; submit it directly without
    payload copies or external-buffer attachment. True means accepted submission;
    false acquires no submission lease and preserves caller ownership. Use native
    mbuf ownership/reference counting for asynchronous driver reclamation and any
    caller-retained backing, just as Xdp implements the same lifetime contract for
    UMEM. Reclamation accounting for `pollTx()` is private backend implementation
    work. There is no public writable-permission API or replacement permission state.
    
    Derive queue/descriptor and preallocated bookkeeping capacity from `txPools` and
    `rxPool`, honoring driver constraints. Do not add duplicate public sizing knobs.
    Keep backend-private direct packet identity and allocation-free packet service. Backend-native
    pool implementations supersede the earlier shared-arena proposal.
    
    ### Corrected pool and receive-buffer boundary
    
    The current implementation has removed the unwanted additions to
    `Zi::IOBufPool`. Its public interface is geometry plus `alloc()` and `free()`.

    Receive retention belongs to each connection's counted intrusive `Zi::IOQueue`
    of `Zi::IOBuf` nodes. New retained buffers are pushed at the head; entries above
    the configured per-connection maximum are popped from the tail. Preserve separate

    RxAccount identity, backing-return charge protocol or generic pool query is needed.
    The backend still retains actual references needed for kernel/device lifetime;
    that private ownership mechanism is distinct from transport receive accounting.
    
    The source repair is already present and is not part of implementing DPDK.
    Use the existing null-allocation/backpressure handling; do not add waiters or
    new pool-notification machinery. Tests must exercise buffer-node retention rather
    than the deleted backing-charge model.
    
    Rx pool buffers are always MTU-sized. Configured Tx buffer sizes may be

    the application never receives a buffer exceeding MTU. Preserve configured
    requests; do not substitute pool-configuration-time clamping or force every
    Tx pool to the Rx size. Do not infer device MTU from a Tx pool configuration. Receive setup follows the existing contiguous-
    packet contract: provide the backend representation of the MTU-sized Rx buffer

    # Zxdp implementation rules
    
    Follow the repository guidance in ../AGENTS.md and the caller-supplied

      `Params::New<Params::Index<Xdp::Params>{}>{}`. Configuration: interface index,

      Init retains one reference per pool through close, while node membership
      remains in the caller configuration list. A node belongs to one
      list at a time; retain pool references for packets that outlive the instance.
      The concrete arena pool is internal. No transmit-completion callback. Without a mask all traffic is selected.
    * Keep allocation and kernel leases distinct in preallocated slot bookkeeping.
      Explicit pool return may run before or after CQ. Recycle only after both leases
      end; safe close releases kernel leases while caller-held backing stays valid.
      One descriptor may be outstanding for a slot. Rejected send acquires no lease.

      arena provisioning, raw packet allocation/return and kernel ring service.
    * Preallocate arenas and all packet bookkeeping at setup. Recycle each pool with
      the non-sharded ZmHeap payload-overlay slist. Exhaustion returns null.
    * Packet lookup and completion use direct slot identity, with constant-time
      updates. No packet/buffer searches or hot-path heap allocations.
    * Query kernel ring mapping offsets and preserve SWSR ownership. The caller
      provides one Rx service owner and one Tx service owner; final pool return may
      run on any thread. Keep thread-exclusive mutable state on separate cache lines.
    * The application assigns a sender `txSid` in its `ZmScheduler` and configures
      that slot with `Xdp::Params::txThread` (`ZmSchedTParams`, isolated by default).
      The scheduler owns thread startup, waiting and teardown. Zxdp owns no sender
      thread or semaphore. Publish initialized descriptors immediately: increment
      the pending-descriptor counter before commit and use scheduler `run()` after
      commit only on a zero-to-one transition. The dedicated sender calls nonblocking
      `sendto()`, observes the kernel consumer delta, spins for `Params_::spin` when
      pending work is exhausted, then atomically subtracts that delta. Use the
      returned pending count to continue or return without losing racing publication.
      Keep a persistent consumer cursor; never count the same consumption twice.
      Tx service has no custom wake function, epoll/eventfd or wait timeout. Rx keeps
      its epoll/eventfd wake protocol. The caller remains the sole descriptor
      producer and CQ owner; consumption accounting does not release kernel leases.
      Check exit during service and idle spin, then drain sender callbacks with a
      FIFO continuation before socket retirement.
    * Construct payload directly in registered backing. No payload staging or copy.
    * Quiesce service before close. Retire kernel access before returning submitted
      backing. A caller-owned pool retains its arena through the last packet return.
    * Queue configuration and mask compilation are cold-path operations.
    * Own the required `rx()`/`wake()` pair: spin for a configurable count before
      blocking with the most efficient suitable kernel mechanism; receive packets
      until explicitly woken, then return. With epoll, post wakeups through an
      internal `eventfd` when Rx has published a wait attempt, following
      ZiEventLoop/ZiMultiplex, with no per-wakeup allocation. Active and preposted
      wake pulses remain in userspace. Own these descriptors and their lifecycle. Wake
      must interrupt spinning and blocking promptly, including under continuous
      traffic and at the transition into the wait. Internal batches do not cause
      `rx()` to return on their own. The caller owns scheduling and lifecycle retries.
        - `ZtString` and `ZtArray` can be tagged with a compile-time `ZmNHeapID`
        - certain types with specific heap IDs are re-used throughout the framework:
          - `ZeString`: `ZtString` with heap ID for error messages, logs and diagnostics
    
    ### Errors and events
    
    - At `ze` and above, errors must be represented by low-level OS `ZeError`
      values or structured `ZeEvent`-derived events, including typed events and
      the type-erased `ZeException`.
    - Higher-level functions that can fail normally return
      `ZuUnion<T, ZeException>`, where `T` is the normal result type. Use
      `ZuUnion<void, ZeException>` when successful completion has no value.
      Low-level OS wrappers may instead report a `ZeError` through an output
      parameter.
    - Never return, store, or propagate an error as a plain string. This includes
      returning strings by value, writing errors through mutable string references
      or pointers, retaining error-string members, and passing strings as the error
      result of a callback. Changing the string type or assigning it a named heap
      does not make such an error contract valid.
    - Preserve OS error identity in `ZeError` and retain structured events through
      propagation. Do not stringify an error for transport and reconstruct an
      event at the receiving end.
    - `ZeString` is appropriate for capturing owned message text in an event or
      logging lambda, for example
      `ZeLOG(..., ([text = ZeString(message)](auto &s) { s << text; }));`.
      The captured text will eventually form part of a logged error message;
      `ZeString` itself is not an error representation. Formatting a structured
      error at its final logging or presentation boundary is permitted.

    using namespace ZuTestUtil;
    
    static unsigned action(int fd, const void *bytes, unsigned length)
    {
      bpf_attr attr{};
      attr.test.prog_fd = fd;
      attr.test.data_in = uintptr_t(bytes);
      attr.test.data_size_in = length;
      attr.test.repeat = 1;
      return syscall(__NR_bpf, BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN, &attr, sizeof(attr)) < 0 ?
        unsigned(-1) : attr.test.retval;
    }
    
    static void testKernelMasks()
    {
      ZuTestScopeRT(testKernelMasks);
      ZeException error;
      // Empty XSK map returns DROP for a selected packet and PASS for unmatched
      // traffic. Real socket redirection is exercised separately by packet tests.
      struct Case { const char *mask, *match, *other; unsigned family; } cases[] = {
        {"192.0.2.7/24", "192.0.2.99", "192.0.3.99", 4},
        {"2001:db8:1234::7/48", "2001:db8:1234::99", "2001:db8:1235::99", 6},
        {"128.0.0.1/1", "192.0.2.1", "127.0.0.1", 4}
      };
      for (auto test : cases) {
        auto parsed = Zxdp::Xdp::parseFilter(test.mask);
        Zxdp::Xdp::BPFProgram program;
        bool loaded = false;
        if (parsed.is<ZeException>()) error = parsed.p<ZeException>();
        else {
          auto result = program.load(2, parsed.p<Zxdp::Xdp::Filter>());
          loaded = result.is<void>();
          if (!loaded) error = result.p<ZeException>();
        }
        ZuCheckRT(loaded, log_("kernel verifier accepts network mask ", test.mask, ": ", error));
        if (!loaded) continue;
        uint8_t bytes[96]{}; // Ethernet plus either IP header, including two VLAN tags
        for (unsigned tags = 0; tags <= 2; ++tags) {
          auto ip = 14 + 4 * tags;
          for (unsigned i = 0; i < tags; ++i) {
            bytes[12 + 4 * i] = 0x81;
            bytes[13 + 4 * i] = 0x00;
          }
          bytes[ip - 2] = test.family == 4 ? 0x08 : 0x86;
          bytes[ip - 1] = test.family == 4 ? 0x00 : 0xdd;
          bytes[ip] = test.family == 4 ? 0x45 : 0x60;
          auto dest = bytes + ip + (test.family == 4 ? 16 : 24);
          inet_pton(test.family == 4 ? AF_INET : AF_INET6, test.match, dest);
          bool matched = action(program.fd(), bytes, sizeof(bytes)) == XDP_DROP;
          inet_pton(test.family == 4 ? AF_INET : AF_INET6, test.other, dest);
          ZuCheckRT(matched && action(program.fd(), bytes, sizeof(bytes)) == XDP_PASS &&
              action(program.fd(), bytes, ip + (test.family == 4 ? 19 : 39)) == XDP_PASS,
            log_("kernel mask distinguishes destination and bounds with VLAN depth ", tags));
        }
      }
      Zxdp::Xdp::BPFProgram program;
      auto unmasked = program.load(2, {});
      if (unmasked.is<ZeException>()) error = unmasked.p<ZeException>();
      ZuCheckRT(unmasked.is<void>(), log_("kernel accepts unmasked classifier: ", error));
      uint8_t frame[64]{};
      frame[12] = 0x88;
      frame[13] = 0xb5;
      ZuCheckRT(action(program.fd(), frame, sizeof(frame)) == XDP_DROP,
        log_("absent mask selects non-IP traffic as well"));
    }
    
    static void testForeign()
    {
      ZuTestScopeRT(testForeign);
      auto ifindex = unsigned(strtoul(getenv("ZXDP_TEST_IFINDEX"), nullptr, 10));
      Zxdp::Xdp::BPFProgram foreign;
      Zxdp::Xdp::BPFAttach attachment;
      ZeException error;
      auto attachedResult = foreign.load(2, {});
      if (attachedResult.is<void>()) attachedResult = attachment.attach(ifindex, foreign);
      bool attached = attachedResult.is<void>();
      if (!attached) error = attachedResult.p<ZeException>();
      ZuCheckRT(attached, log_("fixture attaches an independent owner: ", error));
      if (!attached) return;
      auto instance = Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Xdp);
      auto rx = instance->bufPool(8, 1514);
      Zxdp::Params config(
        Zxdp::Params::New<Zxdp::Params::Index<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>{}>{});
      auto &params = config.p<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>();
      params.ifindex = ifindex;
      params.rxPool = rx;
      params.rx = [](uint8_t *, unsigned) { };
      ZmScheduler scheduler{ZmSchedParams{}.nThreads(1).thread(1,
        [&params](auto &thread) { thread = params.txThread; })};
      params.scheduler = &scheduler;
      params.txSid = 1;
      bool started = scheduler.start();
      ZuCheckRT(started);
      if (!started) { attachment.detach(); return; }
      auto initialized = instance->init(config);
      if (initialized.is<ZeException>()) error = initialized.p<ZeException>();
      auto link = Zxdp::Xdp::queryLink(ifindex);
      if (link.is<ZeException>()) error = link.p<ZeException>();
      ZuCheckRT(initialized.is<ZeException>() && !instance->ready() &&
          link.is<Zxdp::Xdp::LinkState>() &&
          (link.p<Zxdp::Xdp::LinkState>().drvID == foreign.id() ||
        link.p<Zxdp::Xdp::LinkState>().skbID == foreign.id()),
        log_("creation refuses an occupied interface and preserves its program"));
      if (instance) {
        for (;;) {
          auto result = instance->close();
          if (result.is<bool>() && result.p<bool>()) break;
        }
        instance = nullptr;
      }
      ZuCheckRT(scheduler.stop());
      auto detached = attachment.detach();
      if (detached.is<ZeException>()) error = detached.p<ZeException>();
      ZuCheckRT(detached.is<void>(), log_("foreign owner retires its own attachment: ", error));
    }
    
    int main(int argc, char **argv)
    {
      parse(argc, argv);
      if (geteuid() || !getenv("ZXDP_TEST_IFINDEX")) {
        std::cout << "1..0 # SKIP requires privileged fixture-owned interface\n";
        return 0;
      }
      ZuTestMain();
      ZuTestCall(testKernelMasks);
      ZuTestCall(testForeign);
    }

    bool Stack::recoverClosed(const Datagram &d)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (!d.buf || d.buf->skip < 14) return false;
      IPView ip{.local = d.local.ip(), .remote = d.addr.ip()};
      TCPView tcp{.header = d.tcp, .payload = d.buf->cspan()};
      return closedPacket(d.buf->data_(), ip, tcp);
    }
    
    void Stack::resetUnmatched(const Datagram &d)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (!d.buf || d.buf->skip < 14 || (d.tcp.flags & 0x04)) return;
      IPPath path{.local = d.local.ip(), .remote = d.addr.ip(), .mtu = m_mtu};
      memcpy(path.localMAC, d.buf->data_(), 6);
      memcpy(path.remoteMAC, d.buf->data_() + 6, 6);
      resetReply(d.tcp, d.buf->length, path);
    }
    
    void Stack::resetReply(const TCPHeader &incoming, unsigned payload, IPPath path)
    {
      TCPHeader tcp{.srcPort = incoming.dstPort, .dstPort = incoming.srcPort, .flags = 0x04};
      if (incoming.flags & 0x10) tcp.seq = incoming.ack;
      else {
        tcp.flags |= 0x10;
        tcp.ack = incoming.seq + payload + unsigned(bool(incoming.flags & 0x02)) +
          unsigned(bool(incoming.flags & 0x01));
      }
      mx()->txRun([this, tcp, path] { replyControl(tcp, path); });
    }
    
    void Stack::replyControl(TCPHeader tcp, IPPath path)
    {
      auto packet = allocPacket(this, path.local.type(), true);
      if (!packet) return;
      unsigned wire = writeTCP(packet->data_(), packet->size, path, tcp, 0);
      if (!wire) return;
      packet->skip = 0;
      packet->length = wire;
      sendPacket(packet);
    }
    
    bool Stack::closedPacket(const uint8_t *frame, const IPView &ip, const TCPView &tcp)
    {
      ClosedTuple record;
      ClosedTupleKey key{ZiSockAddr{ip.local, tcp.header.dstPort},
        ZiSockAddr{ip.remote, tcp.header.srcPort}};
      if (!m_closed.find(key, record) || (tcp.header.flags & 0x02)) return false;
      // This belongs to the retired incarnation. Never deliver it to a new owner.
      // A lost final ACK can leave older DATA ahead of FIN in peer recovery.
      // ACK that DATA too; pure ACKs and resets must never create ACK loops.
      if (tcp.header.flags & 0x04) return true;
      bool reply = record.fin && (tcp.payload.length() || (tcp.header.flags & 0x01)) &&
        int32_t(tcp.header.seq - record.rxNext) < 0;
      bool refreshed = false;
      if (record.timestamps) {
        if (!(tcp.header.options.flags & TCPOptions::TS)) return true;
        auto now = Zm::now();
        bool recent = *record.tsRecentTime && (now < record.tsRecentTime ||
          now - record.tsRecentTime <= ZuTime{24*24*60*60});
        uint32_t distance = tcp.header.options.tsval - record.tsRecent;
        if ((reply || tcp.header.seq == record.rxNext) &&
        (!recent || distance < uint32_t(0x80000000))) {
          record.tsRecent = tcp.header.options.tsval;
          record.tsRecentTime = now;
          refreshed = true;
        }
      }
      if (!reply) {
        if (refreshed) m_closed.update(record);
        return true;
      }
      auto response = record;
      if (refreshed) m_closed.update(record);
      IPPath path{.local = ip.local, .remote = ip.remote, .mtu = m_mtu};
      memcpy(path.localMAC, frame, 6);
      memcpy(path.remoteMAC, frame + 6, 6);
      mx()->txRun([this, response, path] { replyClosed(response, path); });
      return true;
    }
    
    void Stack::replyClosed(ClosedTuple record, IPPath path)
    {
      auto packet = allocPacket(this, path.local.type(), true);
      if (!packet) return;
      TCPHeader tcp{.srcPort = record.key.p<0>().port(), .dstPort = record.key.p<1>().port(),
        .seq = record.txNext, .ack = record.rxNext, .flags = 0x10};
      if (record.timestamps) {
        tcp.options.flags = TCPOptions::TS;
        tcp.options.tsecr = record.tsRecent;
        if (!tcpTimestamp(Zm::now(), tcp.options.tsval)) return;
        int options = tcp.options.encodedLength(false);
        if (options < 0 || unsigned(options) > packet->avail()) return;
        packet->skip += unsigned(options);
      }
      unsigned wire = writeTCP(packet->data_(), packet->size, path, tcp, 0);
      if (!wire) return;
      packet->skip = 0;
      packet->length = wire;
      if (sendPacket(packet) && record.timestamps)
        mx()->rxRun([this, key = record.key, id = record.id, sent = tcp.options.tsval] {
          ClosedTuple current;
          if (m_closed.find(key, current) && current.id == id) {
        current.lastSentTS = sent;
        m_closed.update(current);
          }
        });
    }

    void Stack::wake()
    {
      ++m_wakeUsers;
      Zxdp::Instance *p = m_current;
      if (p) p->wake();
      --m_wakeUsers;
    }
    
    void Stack::rx()
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (!ready()) return;
      m_rxPackets = 0;

    void Stack::received(uint8_t *p, unsigned n)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      IPView ip;
      TCPView tcp;
      EndpointBindings::Node *binding = nullptr;
      bool valid = readIP({p, n}, ip) && readTCP(ip, tcp);
      if (valid) {
        binding = m_endpoints->findPtr(ZiSockAddr{ip.local, tcp.header.dstPort});
        if (!binding) {
          ZiIP any;
          if (ip.local.v6()) any = in6addr_any;
          else any = in_addr{};
          binding = m_endpoints->findPtr(ZiSockAddr{any, tcp.header.dstPort});
        }
      }
      // A current owner qualifies input before consulting retired tuple history.
      // In particular, newer-TS reuse can choose a peer ISN below an old frontier.
      bool closed = valid && !binding && closedPacket(p, ip, tcp);
      if (closed) m_ingress->free(p);
      else if (binding || m_packet) {
        ZmRef<Zi::IOBuf> buf = new Zi::IOBufStub<Zi::IOBuf, ZiIOBuf_HeapID>{
          p, n, &m_rxAllocator, this, n, false, true};
        if (binding) {
          buf->skip = tcp.payload.data() - p;
          buf->length = tcp.payload.length();

    static void testContention()
    {
      ZuTestScope(testContention);
      auto backend = Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Xdp);
      enum { Slots = 64, Threads = 6, Turns = 30000 }; // bounded contention fixture
      auto rx = backend->bufPool(2, 1514);
      auto tx = backend->bufPool(Slots, 128);
      Zi::IOBufPoolList pools;
      pools.pushNode(tx.ptr());
      auto created = Zxdp::Xdp::UMem::create(pools, rx.ptr(), 1500);
      ZuCHECK(created.is<ZmRef<Zxdp::Xdp::UMem>>(), "contention fixture provisioned");
      if (created.is<ZeException>()) return;
      auto arena = ZuMv(created.p<ZmRef<Zxdp::Xdp::UMem>>());
      auto origin = tx->alloc();
      uintptr_t begin = uintptr_t(origin);
      tx->free(origin);
      ZmAtomic<unsigned> owners[Slots]{};
      ZmAtomic<unsigned> failures{0};
      ZmThread workers[Threads];
      for (unsigned t = 0; t < Threads; ++t) workers[t] = ZmThread{[
        &tx, &owners, &failures, begin, t
      ] {
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < Turns; ++i) {
          auto p = tx->alloc();
          if (!p) { ++failures; continue; }
          auto id = (uintptr_t(p) - begin)/128;
          if (id >= Slots) { ++failures; tx->free(p); continue; }
          if (owners[id].cmpXch(t + 1, 0)) { ++failures; continue; }
          memset(p, t + 1, tx->size);
          for (unsigned j = 0; j < tx->size; ++j)
            if (p[j] != t + 1) { ++failures; break; }
          owners[id] = 0;
          tx->free(p);
        }
      }};
      for (auto &worker : workers) worker.join();
      ZuCHECK(!unsigned(failures), "contended slist preserves ownership and payload");
      uint8_t *held[Slots];
      bool full = true;
      for (auto &p : held) full &= !!(p = tx->alloc());
      ZuCHECK(full && !tx->alloc(), "no frame lost during contended reuse");
      for (auto p : held) if (p) tx->free(p);
    }

## Assistant

The AF_XDP flow matches what you described: Zxdp obtains backing from the Rx pool, supplies it to the kernel, calls `RecvFn` with the received bytes, and Zutcp creates an `IOBuf` referring to those bytes.

A DPDK descriptor is a driver queue entry that refers to an mbuf; it is separate from the mbuf itself. The proposed half-pool split was an arbitrary policy, and I’m withdrawing it.

I also checked my earlier “Rx-only tests” claim: the filter case tests failed initialization, while the wake fixtures simply omit Tx pools. I’ll remove that empty-Tx setup while retaining their filter and wake assertions.

    # Audit flags and fixes
    
    Part of the repository guidance mapped in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
    
    ## Audit flags
    - Audit scope: unless a request explicitly narrows it, every audit against these
      flags covers all repository-owned C++ source directories in each in-scope
      module: `src`, `test`, `util`, `itest`, `example`, `bench`, and `interop`
      where present. Inspect both uses and declarations relevant to each flag; do
      not treat `src` as the whole module.
    
    ### Repair procedure
    - Audit scope is not edit scope. For each repair, identify the requirement or
      observed failure, violated invariant, and owning component. Report unproven
      concerns; do not edit merely to clear a flag.
    - Establish the contract before adding validation, references, locks,
      containers, retries, or APIs. Respect caller responsibilities and framework
      guarantees; validate untrusted input at its boundary without rechecking
      states guaranteed by types.
    - Make the smallest demonstrated fix. Judge storage by actual bounds and
      workload, and account for added allocations, copies, references, lookups,
      and hot-path work.
    - Preserve unrelated code, tests, diagnostics, standard streams, and
      platform-normalizing APIs. Test an agreed invariant or reproduced failure,
      not a speculative new contract.
    - Review every changed line for necessity, then verify the intended behavior
      on relevant platforms using the current build configuration. A green build
      does not justify scope expansion. When reverting, remove the named change
      and its direct dependents without disturbing other work.
    
    ### Error representation
    ### Storage and capacity
    - Red Flag: `operator new` overload outside `ZmNHeap`, except for objects
      managed by `ZmSingleton` or `ZmSpecific`
      Problem: fixed-size allocations outside `ZmSingleton` and `ZmSpecific`
      should be trackable with `ZmNHeap`
      Fix: replace other custom overloads with use of `ZmNHeap`
    - Red Flag: a module-local object allocator/base class which hides `ZmNHeap` or
      `ZmVHeap` behind inherited `operator new`.
      Problem: it erases the concrete allocation size and heap identity, permits a
      variable-size heap for fixed-size objects, and makes allocation audits miss
      dependents.
      Fix: each fixed-size concrete type inherits its own `ZmNHeap` specialization
      (first base), with the concrete type as its CRTP argument and a
      `friend inline ZuStringT<"..."> ZmNHeapID(Type *);` declaration. Do not declare
      `operator new`/`operator delete` merely to forward to a heap, and do not
      introduce generic `Object`, `ObjectAlloc`, or equivalent allocation bases.
    - Red Flag: hard-coded capacities such as `16`.
      Problem: unexplained limits may impair scaling when too low, bloat stack/heap when too high, or leave mostly unused capacity.
      Fix: use prominently located, named library-defined compile-time constants with a maintenance comment: RFC/standard mandate, mainstream alignment, or measured scaling/footprint trade-off.
    - Red Flag: scanning containers for objects to garbage collect
      Problem: garbage collection should be deterministic and immediate - zombie objects should not linger in containers - their memory should be made available to the recycling block allocator
      Fix: delete such scans and ensure that short-lived objects are deterministically removed from their owners when their state becomes final
    - Red Flag: intrusively reference-counted objects as values (including all Z hash tables)
      Problem: intrusively reference-counted objects should only be destroyed by a corresponding smart pointer to prevent multiple destruction / double-free
      Fix: store/pass by reference: replace the object value with the corresponding smart pointer
    - Red Flag: disorderly structs
      Problem: disordered members induce unnecessary padding due to alignment
      Fix: strike a balance between organizing members into logical groups and ordering by size from largest-to-smallest; immutable members should still come first, followed by mutable shared members, then groups of thread-exclusive members
    # Zxdp kernel integration
    
    Build the tree with `make -j8`. The TAP programs skip privileged cases unless
    explicitly supplied fixture interfaces. Never supply an interface carrying
    traffic you need to retain: an absent mask selects all its traffic.
    
    * `zxdppackettest` uses `ZXDP_TEST_IFINDEX` and `ZXDP_TEST_PEER_IFINDEX`, a
      fixture-owned two-queue veth pair. An independent raw packet socket verifies
      transmitted bytes and injects unmasked Ethernet reception. The test requires
      actual CQ completion, small Tx-pool transmission, kernel retirement during
      close, late Rx return and removal of the owned XDP program.
      Sender checks cover pending-descriptor accounting and publication ordering,
      including concurrent submission during kernel drain and shutdown while the sender
      callback is active. Tx uses scheduler `run()` and nonblocking `sendto()`; CQ completion remains
      distinct from descriptor consumption.
    * `zxdpfiltertest` uses `ZXDP_TEST_IFINDEX`. Kernel program test runs verify
      IPv4/IPv6 masks, high-bit addresses, truncated headers, zero/one/two VLAN tags
      and absent-mask behavior. A separate attachment checks foreign-owner protection.
    * `zxdpwaketest` uses the same pair. Real Rx epoll/eventfd observation verifies
      zero-spin blocking, queued/concurrent wake pulses, repeated check-to-wait races,
      packet processing without returning, and interruption during active processing
      with a large spin count. It can also run with a single-queue fixture pair.
    * `zxdplooptest` requires root and `ZXDP_RUN_FIXTURE=1`; it invokes the anonymous
      namespace fixture for independent client/server utility processes, full-MTU
      and smaller packets, three application wait policies and oversized input.
    
    ```
    sudo -n env ZXDP_RUN_FIXTURE=1 ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1 \
      ./zxdp/itest/zxdplooptest
    ```
    
    The tests drive the raw `rx()`/`wake()` pair and Tx completion service. Close retries
    observe deferred kernel retirement with an absolute deadline; expiry never
    permits backing release. Kernel ring tests use actual queues, not a synthetic
    completion as evidence of retirement. Veth establishes software-copy behavior;
    physical NIC DMA requires a hardware run.
    # Standalone packet utility
    
    `zxdppacket` runs a raw Ethernet/IPv4/UDP client or server using the public packet
    API. The main thread runs the library receive loop; a separate utility Tx owner
    drives completions and the application deadline. Packets are built directly in
    Tx backing; the independent peer
    checks headers, checksums, sequence and payload. Every accepted transmission must
    complete. The utility retains at most one unsent packet during local exhaustion.
    There is no network loss recovery; a dropped packet expires the deadline.
    
    Build with top-level `make -j8`, then run the scoped fixture:
    
    ```
    sudo -n bash zxdp/util/zxdpfixture.sh --count 32 --payload 1472 --mode wait
    sudo -n bash zxdp/util/zxdpfixture.sh --count 32 --payload 129 --mode spin
    sudo -n bash zxdp/util/zxdpfixture.sh --count 32 --payload 128 --mode ll
    ```
    
    The fixture creates an anonymous network namespace and its own veth pair. It
    retains configuration and logs in the printed directory and removes its owned
    network resources on namespace exit. Existing host network state is preserved.
    The modes configure the library's receive spin count before its internal
    epoll wait. `--spin` is passed through to `Params::spin`; `--timeout` controls
    only the utility Tx service backoff, not receive blocking. Veth uses software-copy operation.
    
    For caller-owned physical interfaces use `--physical --output NEW_DIR --` followed
    by utility arguments; the fixture then runs only the utility and records logs.
    Run the utility without arguments for its CLI. `--frames` must cover every Rx
    queue. Payload must fit MTU minus 28 bytes. The default absent mask takes over
    all traffic on the chosen interface. Provision peer addressing yourself.

      auto data = m_data;

    inlinestatic
    
    Retrieve a burst of input packets from a receive queue of an Ethernet device. The retrieved packets are stored in rte_mbuf structures whose pointers are supplied in the rx_pkts array.
    
    The rte_eth_rx_burst() function loops, parsing the Rx ring of the receive queue, up to nb_pkts packets, and for each completed Rx descriptor in the ring, it performs the following operations:
    
    Initialize the rte_mbuf data structure associated with the Rx descriptor according to the information provided by the NIC into that Rx descriptor.
    
    Store the rte_mbuf data structure into the next entry of the rx_pkts array.
    
    Replenish the Rx descriptor with a new rte_mbuf buffer allocated from the memory pool associated with the receive queue at initialization time.
    
    When retrieving an input packet that was scattered by the controller into multiple receive descriptors, the rte_eth_rx_burst() function appends the associated rte_mbuf buffers to the first buffer of the packet.
    
    The rte_eth_rx_burst() function returns the number of packets actually retrieved, which is the number of rte_mbuf data structures effectively supplied into the rx_pkts array. A return value equal to nb_pkts indicates that the Rx queue contained at least rx_pkts packets, and this is likely to signify that other received packets remain in the input queue. Applications implementing a "retrieve as much received packets as possible" policy can check this specific case and keep invoking the rte_eth_rx_burst() function until a value less than nb_pkts is returned.
    
    This receive method has the following advantages:
    
    It allows a run-to-completion network stack engine to retrieve and to immediately process received packets in a fast burst-oriented approach, avoiding the overhead of unnecessary intermediate packet queue/dequeue operations.
    
    Conversely, it also allows an asynchronous-oriented processing method to retrieve bursts of received packets and to immediately queue them for further parallel processing by another logical core, for instance. However, instead of having received packets being individually queued by the driver, this approach allows the caller of the rte_eth_rx_burst() function to queue a burst of retrieved packets at a time and therefore dramatically reduce the cost of enqueue/dequeue operations per packet.
    
    It allows the rte_eth_rx_burst() function of the driver to take advantage of burst-oriented hardware features (CPU cache, prefetch instructions, and so on) to minimize the number of CPU cycles per packet.
    
    To summarize, the proposed receive API enables many burst-oriented optimizations in both synchronous and asynchronous packet processing environments with no overhead in both cases.
    
    NoteSome drivers using vector instructions require that nb_pkts is divisible by 4 or 8, depending on the driver implementation.
    
    The rte_eth_rx_burst() function does not provide any error notification to avoid the corresponding overhead. As a hint, the upper-level application might check the status of the device link once being systematically returned a 0 value for a given number of tries.
    
    Parameters
    
    
    port_idThe port identifier of the Ethernet device.
    
    
    queue_idThe index of the receive queue from which to retrieve input packets. The value must be in the range [0, nb_rx_queue - 1] previously supplied to rte_eth_dev_configure().
    
    
    rx_pktsThe address of an array of pointers to rte_mbuf structures that must be large enough to store nb_pkts pointers in it.
    
    
    nb_pktsThe maximum number of packets to retrieve. The value must be divisible by 8 in order to work with any driver.
    
    
    
    ReturnsThe number of packets actually retrieved, which is the number of pointers to rte_mbuf structures effectively supplied to the rx_pkts array.

    Allocate and set up a receive queue for an Ethernet device.
    
    The function allocates a contiguous block of memory for nb_rx_desc receive descriptors from a memory zone associated with socket_id and initializes each receive descriptor with a network buffer allocated from the memory pool mb_pool.
    
    Parameters
    
    
    port_idThe port identifier of the Ethernet device.
    
    
    rx_queue_idThe index of the receive queue to set up. The value must be in the range [0, nb_rx_queue - 1] previously supplied to rte_eth_dev_configure().
    
    
    nb_rx_descThe number of receive descriptors to allocate for the receive ring.
    
    
    socket_idThe socket_id argument is the socket identifier in case of NUMA. The value can be SOCKET_ID_ANY if there is no NUMA constraint for the DMA memory allocated for the receive descriptors of the ring.
    
    
    rx_confThe pointer to the configuration data to be used for the receive queue. NULL value is allowed, in which case default Rx configuration will be used. The rx_conf structure contains an rx_thresh structure with the values of the Prefetch, Host, and Write-Back threshold registers of the receive ring. In addition it contains the hardware offloads features to activate using the RTE_ETH_RX_OFFLOAD_* flags. If an offloading set in rx_conf->offloads hasn't been set in the input argument eth_conf->rxmode.offloads to rte_eth_dev_configure(), it is a new added offloading, it must be per-queue type and it is enabled for the queue. No need to repeat any bit in rx_conf->offloads which has already been enabled in rte_eth_dev_configure() at port level. An offloading enabled at port level can't be disabled at queue level. The configuration structure also contains the pointer to the array of the receiving buffer segment descriptions, see rx_seg and rx_nseg fields, this extended configuration might be used by split offloads like RTE_ETH_RX_OFFLOAD_BUFFER_SPLIT. If mb_pool is not NULL, the extended configuration fields must be set to NULL and zero.
    
    
    mb_poolThe pointer to the memory pool from which to allocate rte_mbuf network memory buffers to populate each descriptor of the receive ring. There are two options to provide Rx buffer configuration:
    
    single pool: mb_pool is not NULL, rx_conf.rx_nseg is 0.
    
    multiple segments description: mb_pool is NULL, rx_conf.rx_seg is not NULL, rx_conf.rx_nseg is not 0. Taken only if flag RTE_ETH_RX_OFFLOAD_BUFFER_SPLIT is set in offloads.
    
    
    
    Returns
    
    0: Success, receive queue correctly set up.
    
    -EIO: if device is removed.
    
    -ENODEV: if port_id is invalid.
    
    -EINVAL: The memory pool pointer is null or the size of network buffers which can be allocated from this memory pool does not fit the various buffer sizes allowed by the device controller.
    
    -ENOMEM: Unable to allocate the receive ring descriptors or to allocate network memory buffers from the memory pool when initializing receive descriptors.

    class ZxdpAPI KernelRetirement {
    friend class Instance;
    
    public:
      enum { Pending = 0, Done = 1 };
      KernelRetirement() = default;
      ~KernelRetirement();
      KernelRetirement(const KernelRetirement &) = delete;
      KernelRetirement &operator =(const KernelRetirement &) = delete;
    
      // Tx only, after Rx work/publication is quiescent. Prepare the empty observer
      // before touching the original binding. Caller retains both objects and all
      // packet holds through Done; an error never authorizes their release.
      ZuUnion<int, ZeException> begin(Xsk &);
      // A caller continuation/timer retries Pending; this never spins or waits.
      ZuUnion<int, ZeException> retry();
      void reset(); // Tx only, after both queue owners released their retired holds
      bool waiting() const { return m_socket && m_ifindex; }
      bool done() const { return m_socket && !m_ifindex; }
    
    private:
      Xsk        *m_socket = nullptr;
      unsigned    m_ifindex = 0;
      unsigned    m_queue = 0;
      Xsk        m_probe;
    };

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # (c) Copyright 2026 Huw Rogers; MIT license (see LICENSE).
    set -euo pipefail
    
    script_dir=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
    utility="$script_dir/zxdppacket"
    output=
    count=32
    payload=128
    mode=wait
    physical=false
    
    usage() {
      echo 'usage: zxdpfixture.sh [--output NEW_DIR --utility PATH --count N --payload N]' >&2
      echo '  [--mode wait|spin|ll]' >&2
      echo '  --physical --output NEW_DIR -- [zxdppacket arguments]' >&2
      exit 2
    }
    while (($#)); do
      case "$1" in
        --output) (($# >= 2)) || usage; output=$2; shift 2;;
        --utility) (($# >= 2)) || usage; utility=$2; shift 2;;
        --count) (($# >= 2)) || usage; count=$2; shift 2;;
        --payload) (($# >= 2)) || usage; payload=$2; shift 2;;
        --mode) (($# >= 2)) || usage; mode=$2; shift 2;;
        --physical) physical=true; shift;;
        --) shift; break;;
        *) usage;;
      esac
    done
    [[ -x $utility ]] || { echo "packet utility unavailable: $utility" >&2; exit 1; }
    
    if $physical; then
      [[ -n $output && $# -gt 0 ]] || usage
      mkdir -m 700 -- "$output"
      printf 'backend=caller-owned-interface\nutility=%q\n' "$utility" > "$output/state.txt"
      printf 'argument=%q\n' "$@" >> "$output/state.txt"
      # All interface configuration is caller-owned. The utility protects existing
      # XDP users and only retires its own binding. Preserve logs on either result.
      set +e
      "$utility" "$@" > "$output/endpoint.log" 2>&1
      result=$?
      set -e
      printf 'exit=%s\n' "$result" >> "$output/state.txt"
      exit "$result"
    fi
    
    [[ $# == 0 && $count =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ && $payload =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || usage
    case "$mode" in wait|spin|ll) ;; *) usage;; esac
    [[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || { echo 'fixture requires network-namespace setup privileges' >&2; exit 1; }
    if [[ ${ZXDP_FIXTURE_INNER:-0} != 1 ]]; then
      if [[ -z $output ]]; then
        output=$(mktemp -d /tmp/zxdp-fixture-parent.XXXXXX)/run
      fi
      # The entire resource-owning shell runs inside this anonymous namespace.
      # No named namespace, host route, interface, neighbor or attachment is changed.
      exec unshare --net env ZXDP_FIXTURE_INNER=1 "$0" --output "$output" \
        --utility "$utility" --count "$count" --payload "$payload" --mode "$mode"
    fi
    
    [[ $(readlink /proc/self/ns/net) != $(readlink /proc/1/ns/net) ]] || {
      echo 'refusing fixture resource creation in the initial network namespace' >&2
      exit 1
    }
    mkdir -m 700 -- "$output"
    server_pid=
    cleanup() {
      result=$?
      trap - EXIT
      if [[ -n $server_pid ]]; then
        kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
      printf 'fixture_exit=%s\n' "$result" >> "$output/state.txt"
      echo "Zxdp fixture artifacts: $output"
      exit "$result"
    }
    trap cleanup EXIT
    trap 'exit 130' INT
    trap 'exit 143' TERM
    printf 'backend=veth\nnamespace=anonymous\nmode=%s\ncount=%s\npayload=%s\n' \
      "$mode" "$count" "$payload" > "$output/state.txt"
    printf 'owned_links=zxdpp0,zxdpp1\nreserved_endpoints=192.0.2.1:40000,192.0.2.2:40001/udp\n' \
      >> "$output/state.txt"
    ip link add zxdpp0 numrxqueues 1 numtxqueues 1 type veth \
      peer name zxdpp1 numrxqueues 1 numtxqueues 1
    ip addr add 192.0.2.1/32 dev zxdpp0
    ip addr add 192.0.2.2/32 dev zxdpp1
    ip link set zxdpp0 up
    ip link set zxdpp1 up
    client_mac=$(ip -o link show dev zxdpp0 | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)
      if($i=="link/ether") print $(i+1)}')
    server_mac=$(ip -o link show dev zxdpp1 | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)
      if($i=="link/ether") print $(i+1)}')
    ip neigh add 192.0.2.2 lladdr "$server_mac" nud permanent dev zxdpp0
    ip neigh add 192.0.2.1 lladdr "$client_mac" nud permanent dev zxdpp1
    ip -details link show > "$output/links.txt"
    ip addr show > "$output/addresses.txt"
    ip neigh show > "$output/neighbors.txt"
    wait_args=(--spin 0 --timeout 1)
    case "$mode" in
      spin) wait_args=(--spin 3 --timeout 2);;
      ll) wait_args=(--spin 1000 --timeout 0);;
    esac
    common=(--count "$count" --payload "$payload" --frames 2 --deadline 15 "${wait_args[@]}")
    timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=2s 25s "$utility" server \
      --interface zxdpp1 --peer-mac "$client_mac" \
      --local-ip 192.0.2.2 --peer-ip 192.0.2.1 --local-port 40001 --peer-port 40000 \
      --ready-file "$output/server.ready" "${common[@]}" > "$output/server.log" 2>&1 &
    server_pid=$!

    #include <zlib/ZuTestUtil.hh>
    
    #include <zlib/ZiPlatform.hh>
    
    #include "zxdplog.hh"
    
    using namespace ZuTestUtil;
    
    static bool contains(const char *path, const char *text)
    {
      // The fixture's result is a single bounded summary line.
      char bytes[4096];
      return ZxdpTest::readLog(path, bytes) && strstr(bytes, text);
    }
    
    static int fixture(const char *output, const char *mode, const char *payload,
      const char *count = "32")
    {
      auto pid = fork();
      if (pid < 0) return -1;
      if (!pid) {
        Zi::Path log;
        log << output << ".log";
        int fd = open(log, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
        if (fd < 0 || dup2(fd, STDOUT_FILENO) < 0 || dup2(fd, STDERR_FILENO) < 0) _exit(126);
        close(fd);
        execl("/bin/bash", "bash", ZXDP_FIXTURE, "--utility", ZXDP_PACKET,
          "--output", output, "--count", count, "--payload", payload, "--mode", mode,
          static_cast<char *>(nullptr));
        _exit(127);
      }
      int status;
      while (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) if (errno != EINTR) return -1;
      return WIFEXITED(status) ? WEXITSTATUS(status) : -1;
    }
    
    static void testProcesses()
    {
      ZuTestScopeRT(testProcesses);
      char directory[] = "/tmp/zxdp-loop.XXXXXX";
      auto parent = mkdtemp(directory);
      ZuCheckRT(!!parent, log_("private fixture artifact parent created"));
      if (!parent) return;
      auto beforeA = if_nametoindex("zxdpp0"), beforeB = if_nametoindex("zxdpp1");
      const char *modes[] = {"wait", "spin", "ll"};
      const char *payloads[] = {"1472", "129", "128"};
      for (unsigned i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        Zi::Path output;
        output << parent << '/' << modes[i];
        int result = fixture(output, modes[i], payloads[i]);
        ZuCheckRT(result == 0, log_(modes[i], " standalone pair exits successfully: ", output));
        Zi::Path client, server, state;
        client << output << "/client.log";
        server << output << "/server.log";
        state << output << "/state.txt";
        ZuCheckRT(contains(client, "PASS role=client packets=32 completions=32") &&
        contains(server, "PASS role=server packets=32 completions=32") &&
        contains(state, "fixture_exit=0"),
        log_(modes[i], " separate processes verify all payloads and kernel completions"));
        ZuCheckRT(if_nametoindex("zxdpp0") == beforeA && if_nametoindex("zxdpp1") == beforeB,
        log_(modes[i], " namespace cleanup preserves the caller's interfaces"));
      }
      Zi::Path output, server;
      output << parent << "/oversize";
      server << output << "/server.log";
      ZuCheckRT(fixture(output, "wait", "1473") != 0 &&
          contains(server, "invalid interface/payload geometry"),
        log_("oversized standalone payload fails before packet binding: ", output));
      log("Standalone packet artifacts retained: ", parent);
    }
    
    int main(int argc, char **argv)
    {
      parse(argc, argv);
      if (geteuid() || !getenv("ZXDP_RUN_FIXTURE")) {
        std::cout << "1..0 # SKIP requires root and ZXDP_RUN_FIXTURE=1 for scoped namespace setup\n";
        return 0;
      }
      ZuTestMain();
      ZuTestCall(testProcesses);
    }

## Assistant

AF_XDP now rejects initialization without a nonempty Tx pool. The filter and wake fixtures supply Tx pools, so they no longer rely on empty-Tx provisioning.

One sizing discrepancy remains in the current code: `Stack::allocator()` clamps before pool creation, while the Zi allocation path also applies a payload-size limit. The DPDK integration plan must implement your allocation-time clamping rule rather than claim it is already fully present. The build is running.

        text='''The verified receive flow is the existing AF_XDP flow, mirrored by DPDK:
        
        1. Application `mx->allocator(...)` requests route through the selected plugin
           to backend-native pool allocation. A DPDK physical pool contains its configured
           count of native mbufs; allocation applies the MTU constraint. Rx uses the
           shared physical ingress pool; logical Rx allocator requests provide metadata
           for that backing rather than independent physical packet pools.
        2. The backend makes Rx backing available to its driver/kernel. AF_XDP publishes
           UMEM addresses in FILL; a hardware DPDK PMD posts mbuf addresses through its
           internal Rx queue. A descriptor is that driver queue entry referring to a
           buffer, not another packet buffer or application pool allocation.
        3. On receive, the backend calls `RecvFn(packetBytes, length)` on the Rx owner.
        4. Zutcp creates a `Zi::IOBuf` stub referring to those same bytes and processes
           the packet. Metadata creation does not copy packet payload.
        5. Final metadata/backing release returns through the original Rx allocator to
           its ingress pool, making the backing available for subsequent reception.
        
        The arbitrary half-Rx-pool descriptor split is withdrawn. Do not silently
        partition an application-supplied pool into descriptor and retention halves or
        add physical-pool transport accounting. Driver queue setup and replacement use
        native DPDK mechanisms over the supplied mbuf pool. Driver constraints remain
        cold-path implementation details rather than new application sizing policy.
        
        '''

    extern "C" __attribute__((visibility("default")))
    ssize_t sendto(int fd, const void *data, size_t size, int flags,
        const sockaddr *address, socklen_t length)
    {
      bool xsk = !data && !size && !address && !length && (flags & MSG_DONTWAIT);
      if (xsk) {
        xdpSender = int(syscall(SYS_gettid));
        xdpSid = ZmSelf()->sid();
        ++xdpKicks;
        if (gateSender.xch(0)) {
          senderEntered.post();
          senderRelease.wait();
        }
        if (auto error = retryError.xch(0)) { errno = error; return -1; }
        if (auto budget = budgetOnce.xch(0))
          budgetResult = setsockopt(fd, SOL_XDP, XDP_MAX_TX_SKB_BUDGET, &budget, sizeof(budget));
      }
      auto n = syscall(SYS_sendto, fd, data, size, flags, address, length);
      int error = errno;
      if (xsk && (n >= 0 || error == EINTR || error == EAGAIN ||
          error == EBUSY || error == ENOBUFS) && gateAfter.xch(0)) {
        afterEntered.post();
        afterRelease.wait();
      }
      errno = error;
      return n;
    }
    
    static bool shutdown(ZmRef<Zxdp::Instance> &instance, ZeException &error)
    {
      if (!instance) return true;
      auto deadline = Zm::now() + ZuTime{10};
      do {
        auto result = instance->close();
        error = {};
        if (result.is<bool>() && result.p<bool>()) { instance = nullptr; return true; }
        if (result.is<ZeException>()) error = result.p<ZeException>();
        // Main-thread fixture loop; retry only deferred kernel retirement. No
        // concurrent application service remains, and no timeout authorizes free.
        poll(nullptr, 0, 1);
      } while (Zm::now() < deadline);
      return false;
    }

    struct ZuTestMgr::Section {
      ZuTest_Step    *begin;
      ZuTest_Step    *end;
      Section    *next;
    };
    
    ZuTestMgr::ZuTestMgr() { }
    
    ZuTestMgr::~ZuTestMgr()
    {
      Section *next;
      for (Section *section = m_head; section; section = next) {
        next = section->next;
        delete section;
      }
    }
    
    ZuTestMgr &ZuTestMgr::instance()
    {
      static ZuTestMgr _;
      return _;
    }
    
    void ZuTestMgr::addSection(ZuTest_Step *begin, ZuTest_Step *end)
    {
      if (!begin || !end || begin == end) return;
      for (Section *section = m_head; section; section = section->next)
        if (section->begin == begin && section->end == end) return;
    
      auto *section = new Section{begin, end, nullptr};
      if (m_tail)
        m_tail->next = section;
      else
        m_head = section;
      m_tail = section;
    }
    
    void ZuTestMgr::init()
    {
      if (m_finalized) return;
      // count steps
      unsigned n = 0;
      for (Section *section = m_head; section; section = section->next)
        n += static_cast<unsigned>(section->end - section->begin);
      // allocate temporary steps[] on stack, falling back to heap
      bool mallocd = false;
      auto steps = static_cast<ZuTest_Step **>(
        ZuAlloca(n * sizeof(ZuTest_Step *), alignof(ZuTest_Step *)));
      if (!steps) {
        mallocd = true;
        steps = static_cast<ZuTest_Step **>(
          ::malloc(n * sizeof(ZuTest_Step *)));
      }
      memset(steps, 0, n * sizeof(ZuTest_Step *));
      // fill steps[] with pointers to statically-allocated steps
      {
        unsigned i = 0;
        for (Section *section = m_head; section; section = section->next)
          for (auto step = section->begin; step < section->end; ++step)
        steps[i++] = step;
      }
      // sort steps and establish IDs
      ZuSort(steps, n, [](ZuTest_Step *&l, ZuTest_Step *&r) {
        // pointer comparison is fine here, just segregating files
        if (int cmp = ZuCompare(l->file, r->file)) return cmp;
        return ZuCompare(l->line, r->line);
      });
      for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        auto step = steps[i];
        auto scope = step->scope;
        step->id = ++scope->count;
      }
      if (mallocd) ::free(steps);
      m_finalized = true;
