    ## Work performed on resume
    
    Read the current Zi pool interface, Xdp pool internals, Zutcp retained-buffer
    queue and allocation/provider paths, Zdb table allocation, source history and
    prior review artifacts. Corrected the brief's obsolete writable/interface
    assumptions. No C++ source edits, builds or tests were performed.
    
    ## Adopted dependency resolution
    
    The author selected optional DPDK using the PostgreSQL precedent. The brief now
    specifies configure control, pkg-config, wrapper control/defaults, conditional
    source/test compilation and enabled/disabled validation. Existing AF_XDP-only
    builds remain possible. This resolves A8; source changes remain unimplemented.
    
    ## Receive-segment clarification
    
    The earlier A5 presentation overstated an implementation setup detail as a new
    design decision. With usable mbuf capacity fitting the configured MTU/frame
    overhead and scatter/coalescing disabled, normal Rx does not require chaining.
    No additional oversized/chained receive policy or copying path is requested.
    Do not expand testing merely to satisfy this withdrawn design question.
    
    ## Author clarification: pool sizes
    
    Rx pool buffers are always MTU-sized. Configured Tx sizes may be below or
    above MTU. Clamp during buffer allocation so the application never sees a
    buffer exceeding MTU; do not clamp the configuration itself. Queue provisioning
    must not assume uniform sizes, infer MTU from a Tx configuration or force all
    Tx requests to MTU. The receive-segment question stays closed.
    
    ## A4 adopted resolution: reusable ports
    
    * `Dpdk::EAL` owns the configured device registrations for its lifetime.
    * An instance acquires exclusive use of one named port; concurrent binding of
      another instance to that port fails with a structured error.
    * Instance teardown follows docs/IO.md: gate new ingress/timer/I/O work and
      post an Rx drain continuation; from Rx post a Tx drain continuation; drain
      queued Tx and accepted device work on Tx, then complete queue retirement,
      stop the port and release exclusive use. Keep completion progress alive while
      closing. Return pending/error until safe retirement; do not block I/O owners
      or discard accepted work in place of draining. Caller-held backing remains
      valid independently; raw owner back-pointers are protected by drain ordering.
    * Ordinary instance close does not call destructive `rte_eth_dev_close()`,
      remove the named device, or finalize EAL. A later instance can configure/start
      the same port with its supplied pools. Retain backing needed by any retained
      device queue state until that state is reconfigured or finalized.
    * Failed initialization unwinds only the instance's acquired resources; it does
      not remove the configured device. It preserves its handle for pending rollback.
    * Final EAL teardown closes its stopped ports before `rte_eal_cleanup()`.
    * Software fixtures stop producers/peers and drain queued mbufs before releasing
      their rings; ring stop alone does not perform that drain.
    
    Status: adopted with author-required asynchronous draining. This records port ownership/reuse,
    not a change to the public pool interface or backing-based receive accounting.
    
    ## A3 correction: mirror AF_XDP receive flow
    
    The half-pool descriptor proposal and Rx-only/zero-Tx-queue provision are
    withdrawn. Both backends require at least one nonempty Tx pool. The current
    filter/wake tests omitted Tx setup; they did not establish a separate public
    Rx-only mode. Preserve their independent assertions with valid Tx provisioning.
    
    DPDK pools provide native mbuf backing with configured count/size and allocation-
    time MTU constraints. Rx packets arrive into pool backing, RecvFn supplies its
    pointer/length, and Zutcp constructs IOBuf metadata referring to it. Final return
    uses the original allocator/pool. Mirror the existing AF_XDP ownership flow.
    A driver descriptor is a queue entry referencing backing, not a second pool.
    No arbitrary half-pool partition or backing-based transport accounting is adopted.
    
    Verified source: ZiMultiplex::allocator, Stack::allocator and ingress setup,
    Xdp::Instance::replenish/receiveQueue, Stack::received, IOBufPoolAllocator and
    RxAllocator::free. DPDK is not yet implemented; its documented Rx API supplies
    mbufs from the queue's configured mempool and replenishes from that same pool.
    The current Stack::allocator still clamps bytes before bufPool; the intended
    allocation-time-only clamping must be carried through DPDK/Zutcp integration
    rather than claimed as already verified in that implementation.
    
    ## Mandatory Tx provisioning and receive-flow verification
    
    Implemented the requested nonempty Tx requirement for AF_XDP instance and arena
    initialization. The DPDK plan carries the same requirement. Existing filter/wake
    fixtures now supply a Tx pool; there was no dedicated successful Rx-only feature
    test to retain or delete. Missing-Tx provisioning is now rejected in the pool
    unit suite. Independent filter and wake behavior coverage remains intact.
    
    The packet integration run exposed a repeatable asynchronous rebind race before
    its final lease subtest. Its main-thread setup now follows the wake fixture's
    existing bounded init/close/retry pattern; production teardown and packet service
    were not changed for that race. The initial temporary namespace harness also
    used host sysfs for interface indices; the corrected harness uses namespace
    netlink via ip. Those failed attempts are not counted as passing verification.
    
    Final checks:
    
    * Top-level `make -j8`: passed.
    * `make -C zxdp/test test`: passed, 4 programs / 14 top-level TAP tests.
    * Native packet/filter/wake tests under sudo in an anonymous two-queue-veth
      namespace: passed, 3 programs / 7 top-level TAP tests.
    * `git diff --check`: passed.
    
    Flow verified by source inspection: backend Rx pool backing is posted to the
    kernel/driver, completed reception calls RecvFn with the backing pointer/length,
    Zutcp constructs IOBuf metadata referencing those bytes, and final release

    ## Delegation
    
    A Goldfish runs in a fresh context with no conversation history. Spawn each
    subagent with your harness's subagent tool (Antigravity: `invoke_subagent`; Claude Code: `Agent`; Codex: `spawn_agent`). Each subagent is defined in `agents/<file>.md`, and its

    If your harness has no subagent tool, stop and tell the user: a review in the same context is not a Goldfish review.
    
    ## Execution Constraints (CRITICAL)
    
    1.  **Artifact-First Delivery (MANDATORY)**: You are **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN** from
        presenting large proposals, drafts, summaries, or plans directly in the chat
        pane. You **MUST** write them to the working directory (or your harness's
        artifact directory, if it has one) using your file-writing tool and then

    2.  **Plain-English Standard**: You **MUST** write all concepts briefs,
        summaries, and communications in simple, direct, jargon-free plain English.
        Explain technical mechanisms directly. Do not summarize away substance or
        rely on buzzwords. Do not use ungrounded promotional adjectives (e.g.,
        *seamless*, *robust*, *blazingly fast*) or decorative adverbs (e.g.,
        *seamlessly*, *effortlessly*, *literally*, *drastically*, *obviously*).
    3.  **Default to Stress-Testing**: Never agree by default. Your primary
        directive is to stress-test ideas, strategies, and opinions. Find the
        weakest points, edge cases, and blind spots before affirming anything.
    4.  **No Glazing**: Eliminate sycophancy. Do not call ideas "great,"
        "brilliant," or "smart." Compliments without substance are noise.
    5.  **Critique First**: Even when an idea is strong, lead with what is wrong,

    6.  **Reject Echo-Chamber Framing**: Never parrot framing back to the user. If a

    7.  **Generate Counter-Arguments**: For every strategy proposed, actively

    namespace Zxdp {
    
    using RecvFn = ZmFn<void(uint8_t *, unsigned), ZmFnHeapID<"Zxdp.Receive">>;
    using StopFn = ZmFn<void(), ZmFnHeapID<"Zxdp.TxStopped">>;
    
    ZtEnumNS(ZxdpAPI, Type, uint8_t, Xdp);
    
    struct Params_ {
      Zi::IOBufPoolList txPools; // at least one nonempty Tx pool is required
      ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool> rxPool;
      RecvFn rx;
      unsigned spin = 1000; // idle probes before Rx blocks or Tx service returns
      ZmScheduler *scheduler = nullptr; // caller-owned scheduler
      StopFn txStopped; // optional owner continuation after sender callbacks drain
    };
    
    namespace Xdp {
      struct Params : public Params_ {
        unsigned ifindex = 0; // network-interface index in the current network namespace
        ZuCSpan netmask; // optional destination CIDR; empty takes all traffic
        unsigned txSid = 0; // application-assigned sender slot
        ZmSchedTParams txThread = ZmSchedTParams().isolated(true);
      };
    }
    ZuDerive(Params, (ZuUnion<Xdp::Params>));
    
    // The caller drives Rx/Tx on their respective single owners. Allocation/free
    // may run on other threads. Allocation holds backing until explicit pool return;
    // an accepted send also holds it until kernel completion or safe close.
    class ZxdpAPI Instance : public ZmPolymorph {
    public:
      ~Instance() override = default;
      Instance(const Instance &) = delete;
      Instance &operator =(const Instance &) = delete;
    
      // Pools are independent of the factory instance and can precede init().
      virtual ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool> bufPool(unsigned count, unsigned size,
        unsigned headRoom = 0, unsigned tailRoom = 0,
        unsigned align = ZiIOBuf_DefltAlign) = 0;
      // Initialize once. Retain the handle after failure and close it to finish
      // rollback. Configuration may expire on return; pool references are retained.
      virtual ZuUnion<void, ZeException> init(const Params &) = 0;
    
      virtual bool ready() const = 0;
      virtual unsigned mtu() const = 0;
      virtual bool zeroCopy() const = 0;
      virtual ZuBSpan mac() const = 0;
    
      // False acquires no kernel lease. After true, keep bytes immutable until
      // kernel retirement. One descriptor may be outstanding for each slot.
      virtual bool send(uint8_t *packet, unsigned length) = 0;
      virtual void rx() = 0; // Rx owner, until wake() or device failure
      virtual void wake() = 0;
      virtual unsigned pollTx() = 0;
      virtual bool stopTx() = 0;
      // Quiesce Rx, Tx and wake callers first. True means closed, false means
      // retirement is pending; an error never authorizes releasing kernel backing.
      virtual ZuUnion<bool, ZeException> close() = 0;
    
      virtual unsigned allQueues(Ztc::QueueMgr::AllFn) const = 0;
    
    protected:
      Instance() = default;
    };
    
    ZxdpExtern ZmRef<Instance> instance(Type::T);
    
    } // namespace Zxdp

      if (!count) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "empty native packet pool");
      return count;

    static unsigned requireTCPSecrets(ISN &isn, TFOKey &tfo, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (!isn.init(interface))
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "secure TCP sequence initialization failed");
      if (!tfo.init())
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "secure Fast Open cookie initialization failed");
      return interface;
    }
    
    Instance::Instance(ZiMultiplex *mx, InstanceParams params)
    : ZiMxPlugin{mx}, m_interface{requireTCPSecrets(m_isn, m_tfoKey, params.interface)},
      m_mtu{requireMTU(mx, params.interface)},
      m_spin{params.spin},
      m_txSid{params.txSid},
      m_netmask{params.netmask}, m_packet{ZuMv(params.packet)},
      m_backend{Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Xdp)},
      m_ingress{new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(
        ingressCount(mx, m_interface), m_mtu + 14)}},
      m_rxAllocator{mx, m_ingress},
      m_packets{new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(
        requirePackets(params.packetCount), m_mtu + 14, 14 + 40 + 60)}},
      m_control{new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(
        DefaultControlBufCount, m_mtu + 14, 14 + 40 + 60)}},
      m_packetAllocator{mx, m_packets}, m_dataAllocator{mx, m_packets},
      m_controlAllocator{mx, m_control},
      m_endpoints{new EndpointBindings{ZmHashParams{}.bits(5).loadFactor(1).cBits(3)
        .init("Zutcp.Endpoints")}}
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped);
      // TCP controls use separate native backing and never borrow application slots.
      m_tfoCookies.queueOwner(mx->id());
      m_closed.queueOwner(mx->id());
      m_ingress->returned = [this] {
        if (!ready() || this->mx()->invoked(this->mx()->rxThread()) ||
        m_rxWakeQueued.xch(1)) return;
        // Replenish an empty FILL ring even when no packet can make it readable.
        // Queueing through mx supplies both scheduler re-entry and backend wake.
        this->mx()->rxRun([this] { m_rxWakeQueued = 0; });
      };
      addProvider(m_packets);
      addProvider(m_control);
    }
    
    Instance::~Instance()
    {
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped && !m_current && !unsigned(m_wakeUsers));
      ZmAssert_(!m_txServicing && !m_txPending);
      ZmAssert_(!m_routePending && !m_endpoints->count_());
      ZmAssert_(!m_observed && !m_observedCount);
      delete m_cxns;
      m_ingress->returned = {};
      m_backend = nullptr;
      while (m_providers) {
        auto p = m_providers;
        m_providers = p->nextProvider;
        p->nextProvider = nullptr;
        ZmDEREF(p); // stopped, long-lived configuration ownership
      }
    }
    
    void Instance::addProvider(Allocator *p)
    {
      ZmREF(p);
      m_txCapacity += p->pool->count;
      p->nextProvider = m_providers;
      m_providers = p;
    }
    
    Zi::IOBufPool *Instance::allocator(
      Zi::IOBufType::T type, unsigned size, unsigned align, unsigned count)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped);
      // Providers reserve complete output framing before Zi copies their geometry.
      enum { Ethernet = 14, IPv6 = 40, TCP = 60 };
      unsigned head;
      switch (type) {
        case Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP:
        case Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP: head = Ethernet + IPv6 + TCP; break;
        default: throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported network allocator role");
      }
      if (head >= m_mtu + Ethernet || !align || (align & (align - 1)) ||
          align > unsigned(sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)))
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported packet allocator geometry");
      if (type == Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP)
        return new RxAllocator{m_ingress, head, count, align};
      uint64_t bytes = uint64_t(size) + head;
      if (bytes > m_mtu + Ethernet) bytes = m_mtu + Ethernet;
      auto p = new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(count, unsigned(bytes), head, 0, align)};
      addProvider(p);
      return p;
    }
    
    ZuUnion<void, ZeException> Instance::configureControl(unsigned count, unsigned credits)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped && m_state == Stopped);
      uint64_t capacity = m_txCapacity - m_control->pool->count + count;
      if (!count || !credits || credits >= capacity || capacity > UINT_MAX ||
          m_txPending) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", ([count, credits, capacity](auto &out) {
          out << "invalid or busy control reserve count=" << count
        << " credits=" << credits << " Tx capacity=" << capacity;
        }));
      }
      m_control->count = m_control->pool->count = count;
      m_controlCredits = credits;
      m_txCapacity = capacity;
      return {};
    }
    
    TxAdmission Instance::txAdmission() const
    {
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped || mx()->invoked(mx()->txThread()));
      unsigned count = m_control->pool->count;
      return {.capacity = m_txCapacity, .dataStalls = m_dataStalls,
        .controlStalls = m_controlStalls, .reserved = m_controlCredits,
        .outstanding = m_txPending, .controlCount = count};
    }
    
    ZuUnion<void, ZeException> Instance::configure(const InstanceConfig &config)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped && m_state == Stopped);
      if (!positiveTimeout(config.connectTimeout)) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid connect timeout");
      }
      if (!positiveTimeout(config.closeDrainTimeout) || !positiveTimeout(config.finWaitTimeout)) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid close timeout");
      }

    ### Native pool backing and direct send
    
    Implement internal `Dpdk::BufPool : Zi::IOBufPool`, constructed by
    `Dpdk::Instance::bufPool(...)`. Keep `Xdp::BufPool` internal and unchanged in
    purpose. Both implementations expose the common pool geometry and only
    `alloc()`/`free()` over their own backing. Storage identity and backend lease
    bookkeeping remain private implementation details.
    
    The DPDK pool supplies native mbuf backing from allocation onward. A packet
    received by DPDK send already identifies its mbuf; submit it directly without
    payload copies or external-buffer attachment. True means accepted submission;
    false acquires no submission lease and preserves caller ownership. Use native
    mbuf ownership/reference counting for asynchronous driver reclamation and any
    caller-retained backing, just as Xdp implements the same lifetime contract for
    UMEM. Reclamation accounting for `pollTx()` is private backend implementation
    work. There is no public writable-permission API or replacement permission state.
    
    Derive queue/descriptor and preallocated bookkeeping capacity from `txPools` and
    `rxPool`, honoring driver constraints. Do not add duplicate public sizing knobs.
    Keep backend-private direct packet identity and allocation-free packet service. Backend-native
    pool implementations supersede the earlier shared-arena proposal.
    
    The verified receive flow is the existing AF_XDP flow, mirrored by DPDK:
    
    1. Application `mx->allocator(...)` requests route through the selected plugin
       to backend-native pool allocation. A DPDK physical pool contains its configured
       count of native mbufs; allocation applies the MTU constraint. Rx uses the
       shared physical ingress pool; logical Rx allocator requests provide metadata
       for that backing rather than independent physical packet pools.
    2. The backend makes Rx backing available to its driver/kernel. AF_XDP publishes
       UMEM addresses in FILL; a hardware DPDK PMD posts mbuf addresses through its
       internal Rx queue. A descriptor is that driver queue entry referring to a
       buffer, not another packet buffer or application pool allocation.
    3. On receive, the backend calls `RecvFn(packetBytes, length)` on the Rx owner.
    4. Zutcp creates a `Zi::IOBuf` stub referring to those same bytes and processes
       the packet. Metadata creation does not copy packet payload.
    5. Final metadata/backing release returns through the original Rx allocator to
       its ingress pool, making the backing available for subsequent reception.
    
    The arbitrary half-Rx-pool descriptor split is withdrawn. Do not silently
    partition an application-supplied pool into descriptor and retention halves or
    add physical-pool transport accounting. Driver queue setup and replacement use
    native DPDK mechanisms over the supplied mbuf pool. Driver constraints remain
    cold-path implementation details rather than new application sizing policy.
    
    ### Corrected pool and receive-buffer boundary
      implementations of `Zi::IOBufPool`.
    * Separate public ring sizing duplicates the accepted pool-driven provisioning.
    * Continuous polling during extended idle is optional (`rxInterval == 0`);
      the default uses brief spinning and bounded timed waits to reduce idle CPU.

    **For a simple TX → RX loopback, use `net_ring`.** It exposes an in-memory ring through the normal DPDK Ethernet APIs. DPDK documents this specifically for testing without Ethernet hardware. [Ring PMD documentation](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/nics/ring.html)
    
    Assuming `dpdk-testpmd` and the ring driver are installed:
    
    ```bash
    # Replace 0-1 with two CPUs available to your process.
    dpdk-testpmd -l 0-1 \
      --no-pci --no-huge --no-shconf -m 256 \
      --vdev=net_ring0 \
      -- -i --nb-cores=1 --total-num-mbufs=4096 \
      --rxq=1 --txq=1 --disable-rss \
      --port-topology=loop --forward-mode=io
    ```
    
    At its prompt:
    
    ```text
    start tx_first
    show port stats all
    stop
    quit
    ```
    
    Wait a few seconds before displaying statistics. `start tx_first` injects the initial packets; forwarding then circulates them through the ring. RX and TX counters should increase. Plain `start` has no initial traffic to circulate. [Testpmd commands](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/testpmd_app_ug/testpmd_funcs.html)
    
    Here, `--no-pci` disables PCI discovery and `--no-huge` uses ordinary memory, avoiding hugepage setup. This configuration does not support DPDK primary/secondary shared-memory operation. [EAL options](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/linux_gsg/linux_eal_parameters.html)
    
    **For testing your actual TCP/UDP application, choose the connection you need:**
    
    | Test arrangement | Suitable approach |
    |---|---|
    | One process, packet loopback | `net_ring` |
    | Two endpoints within one process | Two ports created with `rte_eth_from_rings()`, with RX/TX rings cross-connected |
    | Linux socket client ↔ DPDK protocol stack | `net_tap` |
    | Two independent DPDK processes | Linux `veth` pair, with `net_af_packet` attached to each end |
    | Repeatable packet input/output | `net_pcap` with input/output capture files |
    
    These are supported by the [ring](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/nics/ring.html), [TAP](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/nics/tap.html), [AF_PACKET](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides/nics/af_packet.html), and [PCAP](https://doc.dpdk.org/guides-24.11/nics/pcap_ring.html) drivers.
    
    For example, launch your protocol-stack application with these **EAL arguments**:
    
    ```bash
    sudo ./your-app -l 0-1 --no-pci --no-huge \
      --vdev=net_tap0,iface=dtap0 -- <application-options>
    ```
    
    Then configure the Linux side:
    
    ```bash
    sudo ip addr add 192.0.2.1/24 dev dtap0
    sudo ip link set dtap0 up
    ```
    
    Configure **192.0.2.2/24 inside your DPDK application’s stack**, and connect from Linux to that address. Do not assign `.2` to Linux as well: local routing would bypass your application. The application must implement the relevant ARP/IP/TCP/UDP handling; DPDK itself supplies packet I/O.
    
    Use these setups for functional testing and software-path measurements. They do not validate physical NIC DMA, hardware offloads, or wire latency.

    static unsigned power2(unsigned n)
    {
      if (n > (unsigned(1)<<31)) return 0;
      if (n < 2) return 2;
      return unsigned(1)<<(32 - __builtin_clz(n - 1));
    }
    
    static unsigned poolStride(const Zi::IOBufPool &pool)
    {
      unsigned size = pool.size;
      if (size < pool.align) size = pool.align;
      return power2(size < 64 ? 64 : size);
    }
    
    ZuUnion<ZmRef<UMem>, ZeException> UMem::create(
      const Zi::IOBufPoolList &txPools, Zi::IOBufPool *rxPool, unsigned mtu)
    {
      auto fail = [](const char *text) { return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", text); };
      // Linux copy-mode Rx adds NET_IP_ALIGN before the Ethernet header.
      enum { RxAlign = 2 };
      auto rx = dynamic_cast<BufPool *>(rxPool);
      auto page = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
      if (page < 2048 || uint64_t(page) > UINT32_MAX || (page & (page - 1)))
        return fail("unsupported AF_XDP page size");
      if (!rx || !rx->count || rx->ready() || rx->used())
        return fail("one unused, nonempty Rx pool is required");
      if (!rx->align || (rx->align & (rx->align - 1)) || rx->align > unsigned(page) ||
          rx->headRoom > rx->size || rx->tailRoom > rx->size - rx->headRoom)
        return fail("invalid Rx pool geometry");
      unsigned prefix = rx->align > XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM ? rx->align : XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM;
      if (!mtu || rx->size < mtu + 14 || uint64_t(rx->size) + prefix + RxAlign > unsigned(page))
        return fail("Rx packet size does not fit the interface and one AF_XDP chunk");
      ArenaLayout layout;
      layout.prefix = prefix;
      layout.chunk = power2(rx->size + layout.prefix + RxAlign);
      if (layout.chunk < 2048) layout.chunk = 2048;
      layout.rxCount = rx->count;
      uint64_t txBytes = 0;
      {
        auto pools = txPools.citer();
        while (auto node = pools()) {
          auto pool = dynamic_cast<BufPool *>(node);
          if (!pool || pool == rx || pool->ready() || pool->used() || !pool->size ||
        pool->size > unsigned(page) || pool->headRoom > pool->size ||
        pool->tailRoom > pool->size - pool->headRoom || !pool->align ||
        (pool->align & (pool->align - 1)) || pool->align > unsigned(page))
        return fail("invalid or busy Tx pool");
          if (pool->count > UINT32_MAX - layout.txCount) return fail("Tx count overflow");
          layout.txCount += pool->count;
          auto stride = poolStride(*pool);
          if (stride > layout.chunk) layout.chunk = stride;
          auto bytes = uint64_t(pool->count) * stride;
          auto length = (bytes + page - 1) & ~(uint64_t(page) - 1);
          if (length > SIZE_MAX - txBytes) return fail("Tx arena size overflow");
          txBytes += length;
        }
      }
      if (!layout.txCount) return fail("at least one nonempty Tx pool is required");
      if (layout.chunk > unsigned(page)) return fail("packet exceeds AF_XDP chunk size");
      auto rxBytes = uint64_t(rx->count) * layout.chunk;
      rxBytes = (rxBytes + page - 1) & ~(uint64_t(page) - 1);
      if (rxBytes > SIZE_MAX - txBytes) return fail("Rx arena size overflow");
      layout.rxLength = rxBytes;
      layout.txLength = txBytes;
      layout.length = rxBytes + txBytes;
      if (layout.length/layout.chunk > UINT32_MAX || layout.length/unsigned(page) > UINT32_MAX)
        return fail("AF_XDP arena exceeds kernel count limits");
      ZmRef<UMem> arena = new UMem;
      auto mem = mmap(nullptr, layout.length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
        MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
      if (mem == MAP_FAILED) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", ([error = ZeLastError](auto &out) {
          out << "AF_XDP arena mmap failed: " << error;
        }));
      }
      arena->m_data = static_cast<uint8_t *>(mem);
      arena->m_layout = layout;
      arena->m_pageShift = __builtin_ctz(unsigned(page));
      arena->m_pages.length(layout.length>>arena->m_pageShift);
      arena->m_tx.length(layout.txCount);
      rx->init(arena, 0, layout.chunk, layout.prefix, 0);
      for (size_t i = 0; i < layout.rxLength>>arena->m_pageShift; ++i) arena->m_pages[i] = rx;
      uint64_t offset = rxBytes;
      unsigned first = 0;
      auto pools = txPools.citer();
      while (auto node = pools()) {
        auto pool = static_cast<BufPool *>(node);
        auto stride = poolStride(*pool);
        auto bytes = (uint64_t(pool->count) * stride + page - 1) & ~(uint64_t(page) - 1);
        pool->init(arena, offset, stride, 0, first);
        for (auto i = offset>>arena->m_pageShift; i < (offset + bytes)>>arena->m_pageShift; ++i)
          arena->m_pages[i] = pool;
        first += pool->count;
        offset += bytes;
      }
      return arena;
    }
    
    BufPool *UMem::pool(const void *packet) const
    {
      auto address = uintptr_t(packet), begin = uintptr_t(m_data);
      if (address < begin || address - begin >= m_layout.length) return nullptr;
      return m_pages[(address - begin)>>m_pageShift];
    }
    TxSlot &UMem::txSlot(const BufPool &pool, unsigned slot)
    {
      return m_tx[pool.first() + slot];
    }
    void UMem::retire(const Zi::IOBufPoolList &txPools, BufPool *rx)
    {
      rx->retire();
      auto pools = txPools.citer();
      while (auto node = pools()) static_cast<BufPool *>(node)->retire();
    }
    UMem::~UMem() { if (m_data) munmap(m_data, m_layout.length); }

    {
      return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", ([operation, error = ZeLastError](auto &out) {
        out << operation << ": " << error;
      }));
    }
    
    template <typename R> ZuUnion<void, ZeException> Xsk::map(
      unsigned i, R &ring, const xdp_ring_offset &off, unsigned count, uint64_t offset)
    {
      size_t length;
      if (!R::mapLength(off, count, length))
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "invalid AF_XDP kernel ring offsets or mapping length");
      auto mem = mmap(nullptr, length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, m_fd, offset);
      if (mem == MAP_FAILED) return socketFailed("AF_XDP ring mmap");
      m_maps[i] = {mem, length};
      if (!ring.init(mem, length, off, count))
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zxdp", "invalid AF_XDP mapped ring state");
      return {};
    }

      ZmRef<UMem> arena, unsigned ifindex, unsigned queue, unsigned rxCount, unsigned txCount,

      if (prepared.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(prepared).p<ZeException>();
      auto bound = bind(ifindex, queue);
      if (bound.is<ZeException>()) { close(); return ZuMv(bound).p<ZeException>(); }
      return {};
    }

    # Zxdp AF_XDP and DPDK backends
    
    * **Author:** Huw Rogers
    * **Date:** 2026-11-16
    * **Updated:** 2026-11-17
    * **Status:** Decisions reconciled with the current `zxdp/src` refactor. Seven
      historical brainstorming reviews completed; this update is source reconciliation,
      not another review or an implementation/test run.
    
    ## Overview
    
    Add DPDK alongside the existing AF_XDP backend using the current polymorphic
    `Zxdp::Instance`. AF_XDP implementation types live in `Zxdp::Xdp`; DPDK types
    will live in `Zxdp::Dpdk`. Extend the existing `Type` selector and tagged
    `Params` union rather than recreating the earlier Backend/If design.
    
    The direct DPDK path is `Zutcp Tx owner → rte_eth_tx_burst() → DPDK/NIC`.
    Software ring/pcap PMDs exercise that same path without a NIC. No intermediate
    DPDK submission ring, EAL Tx worker or extra scheduler sender is required.
    AF_XDP retains its own scheduler sender for kernel Tx processing.
    
    ## Current source baseline
    
    Read `Zxdp.hh`, `Zxdp.cc`, `ZxdpPool.hh/.cc`, `ZxdpUMem.hh/.cc`,
    `ZxdpRetire.hh/.cc`, `ZxdpBPF.hh` and the BPF implementation changes,
    `ZxdpRing.hh` changes, `Makefile.am` and `src/EGM.md`. Also read the updated
    `zxdp/GUIDELINES.md` and `zxdp/INTERFACE.md`. The baseline includes commit
    `3892a86f` and the subsequent shared-buffer and pool-interface repairs.
    Preserve current source and unrelated working-tree edits.
    
    The refactor already supplies:
    
    * Cold `instance(Type::Xdp)` selection and a pure virtual base, without `m_data`.
    * `Params_` for common settings, `Xdp::Params` for AF_XDP settings, and a tagged
      `Zxdp::Params` union populated in place.
    * Virtual `bufPool(count, size, headRoom, tailRoom, align)` returning
      `ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool>`. Cold factory instances and pool nodes have independent
      lifetimes; pools can precede instance initialization.
    * `Params_::txPools` as an owning `Zi::IOBufPoolList`, and `rxPool` as an unlinked
      `ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool>`. Init retains pool references; intrusive membership
      stays in the caller's configuration list. One node belongs to one list.
    * `init(const Params &)` returning `ZuUnion<void, ZeException>`, with one init
      attempt per instance. Retain the handle after failure and close for rollback.
    * Plain `bool send(uint8_t *, unsigned)`, `stopTx()`, and
      `close()` returning `ZuUnion<bool, ZeException>`: true is closed, false is
      retirement pending, and the exception branch is an error. An error never
      authorizes freeing backing that remains in use.
    * Internal `Xdp::Instance`, `Xdp::BufPool`, `Xdp::UMem`, `Xdp::Xsk`, ring, BPF
      and retirement types. `ZxdpPool.hh` replaces the old `ZxdpAlloc.hh`.
    * A Zi dependency in `src/Makefile.am`; only `Zxdp.hh` and `ZxdpLib.hh` are
      currently installed, while pool/UMEM/ring/BPF/retirement headers are private.
    
    The send/ACK simplification from `zutcp_fix.md` is present in the baseline;
    it is no longer a pending prerequisite. This reconciliation does not certify
    its tests. Public `ifindex()` has also been removed in the working tree;
    the adopted `status()` operation still needs adding.
    
    ## Analysis and adopted design
    
    ### Backend selection and instance parameters
    
    Extend the existing declarations in `Zxdp.hh` using its current enum macro form:
    
    ```cpp
    namespace Zxdp {
    
    ZtEnumNS(ZxdpAPI, Type, uint8_t, Xdp, Dpdk);
    
    // Existing Params_ retains its owning Tx list, Rx reference, callback,
    // spin, scheduler and txStopped fields.
    namespace Dpdk {
      struct Params : public Params_ {
        ZtString<> name;            // DPDK Ethernet device name
        unsigned rxInterval = 50;   // maximum idle wait, microseconds; zero polls
      };
    }
    ZuDerive(Params, (ZuUnion<Xdp::Params, Dpdk::Params>));
    
    } // namespace Zxdp
    ```
    
    Use `instance(Type::Dpdk)` to obtain `Dpdk::Instance`, then allocate pools,
    populate backend parameters in place, and call `init(config)`. For example:
    
    ```cpp
    auto backend = Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Dpdk);
    auto tx = backend->bufPool(txCount, txSize); // configured size; clamp on allocation
    auto rx = backend->bufPool(rxCount, rxSize); // established for MTU-sized packets
    Zxdp::Params config(
      Zxdp::Params::New<Zxdp::Params::Index<Zxdp::Dpdk::Params>{}>{});
    auto &params = config.p<Zxdp::Dpdk::Params>();
    params.name = "net_ring0";
    params.txPools.pushNode(tx.ptr());
    params.rxPool = rx;
    params.rx = receive;
    params.spin = 1000;
    params.rxInterval = 50;
    auto result = backend->init(config);
    ```
    
    EAL must already have been explicitly initialized before selecting a DPDK
    backend. Pool objects retain their independent factory/instance lifetime as in
    the current interface. Copy required configuration into the instance during init;
    the parameter union may expire after init. Retain pool references for packets
    that outlive the instance, and freeze geometry while bound.
    
    `Xdp::Params` keeps `ifindex`, `netmask`, `txSid` and `txThread`.
    Do not put AF_XDP sender settings into `Dpdk::Params`. Resolve the DPDK Ethernet
    name once with `rte_eth_dev_get_port_by_name()` and store its `uint16_t port_id`
    privately. Do not add the obsolete `Backend`, `If_AF_XDP`, `If_DPDK`, `If`,
      implementations of `Zi::IOBufPool`.
    * Separate public ring sizing duplicates the accepted pool-driven provisioning.
    * Continuous polling during extended idle is optional (`rxInterval == 0`);
      the default uses brief spinning and bounded timed waits to reduce idle CPU.
    
    ## Key Decisions & Staging for Next Steps
    
    1. Extend `Type` with Dpdk and `Params` with `Dpdk::Params`. Keep `Xdp::Params`
       and internals in their existing namespace. Add the adopted status operation.
    2. Add the public Dpdk EAL configuration/wrapper and private backend/pool
       implementations, with repository-prefixed source/header names (for example
       `ZxdpDpdk.hh/.cc` and `ZxdpDpdkPool.hh/.cc`). Export only caller-required
       EAL configuration/API declarations; keep concrete mbuf internals private.
    3. Add the DPDK dependency through configure/pkg-config conventions and extend
       `zxdp/src/Makefile.am`, preserving its existing Zi dependency and installed
       versus private header boundary. Do not repeat the completed Zi pool migration.
    4. Implement pool-derived queue setup, direct Tx, native reclamation, receive,
       counted wakes, stopTx and structured retryable close. Add DPDK selection and
       initial/restart provisioning in `zutcp/src/ZutcpMx.hh/.cc`. Change the
       replication `tableBufAllocFn<T>()` in `zdb/src/ZdbBuf.hh` to request TxTCP
       buffers, preserving table-requested geometry and plugin MTU constraints.
       Use the current union initialization and owning pool APIs without shims.
    5. Mirror existing AF_XDP unit/integration coverage using ring/pcap fixtures
       through the same DPDK path. Keep peer progress, Rx-pool provenance and queued
       mbuf draining in fixture implementation; do not expand the validation scope.
       Follow `docs/BUILD.md` for dependency builds and relevant tests.

      void free(uint8_t *packet) override;

    The verified receive flow is the existing AF_XDP flow, mirrored by DPDK:
    
    1. Application `mx->allocator(...)` requests route through the selected plugin
       to backend-native pool allocation. A DPDK physical pool contains its configured
       count of native mbufs; allocation applies the MTU constraint. Rx uses the
       shared physical ingress pool; logical Rx allocator requests provide metadata
       for that backing rather than independent physical packet pools.
    2. The backend makes Rx backing available to its driver/kernel. AF_XDP publishes
       UMEM addresses in FILL; a hardware DPDK PMD posts mbuf addresses through its
       internal Rx queue. A descriptor is that driver queue entry referring to a
       buffer, not another packet buffer or application pool allocation.
    3. On receive, the backend calls `RecvFn(packetBytes, length)` on the Rx owner.
    4. Zutcp creates a `Zi::IOBuf` stub referring to those same bytes and processes
       the packet. Metadata creation does not copy packet payload.
    5. Final metadata/backing release returns through the original Rx allocator to
       its ingress pool, making the backing available for subsequent reception.

    cold-path implementation details rather than new application sizing policy.

    allocation-wait protocol. Instance readiness remains a separate valid operation.
    
    Receive retention belongs to each connection's counted intrusive `Zi::IOQueue`
    of `Zi::IOBuf` nodes. New retained buffers are pushed at the head; entries above
    the configured per-connection maximum are popped from the tail. Preserve separate
    intrusive memberships used by independent queues. No physical-slot charge table,
    RxAccount identity, backing-return charge protocol or generic pool query is needed.

    name: egm-resolve
    license: Apache-2.0
    disable-model-invocation: true
    description: >-
      The Elephant resolution skill. Ingests flat deficiency reports from
      concurrent Goldfish reviewers, applies automated fixes for PROPOSE FIX
      items via UI multiple-choice gates, and presents interactive
      negotiation/re-sync checkpoints.
    ---
    
    # Goldfish Review: Resolve
    
    When running in Codex or ChatGPT Work, first read [Codex integration](../../docs/codex.md).
    In Claude Code or Cowork, read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/claude.md` first.
    
    ## Overview
    
    This skill instructs the agent on how to operate within the primary Elephant
    context window to parse flat deficiency reports from concurrent Goldfish
    reviewers. It defends accurate design choices, applies automated textual
    repairs, and manages interactive negotiation checkpoints.
    
    ## Prerequisites & Context Strategy
    
    *   **Context Recommendation (Elephant Memory)**: This skill should be run in
        the persistent conversation session that generated the target document (the
        Elephant) to recall earlier reasoning and craft higher-quality fixes.
    
    ## Inputs
    
    The caller or orchestration driver provides exactly these parameters:
    
    *   **`TargetFile`**: Absolute or relative path to target document.
    *   **`LineRange`**: Exact line numbers (or `full file`).
    *   **`FindingsList`**: Aggregated flat list of findings from Goldfish
        reviewers.
    
    ## Execution Workflow
    
    ### Step 1: Intake Validation & Gather Context
    
    1.  **Hybrid Execution UX**: Detect if execution arguments are present:
    
        *   *Automated Mode*: If all parameters are provided, execute silently as a
            subprocess.
        *   *Standalone Human Mode*: If parameters are omitted, trigger a friendly
            onboarding flow. Prompt for one piece of input at a time, waiting for
            the user's response after each turn. Once all inputs are specified,
            display the final setup and verify the user is ready to continue.
    
    2.  Read `TargetFile` at `LineRange` by reading it and parse the `FindingsList`.
    
    ### Step 2: Evaluate & Categorize
    
    Give each finding exactly one category:
    
    *   **CONTEST**: The critique is inaccurate or relies on a misunderstanding of
        the codebase. Cite evidence that the reviewer could read: a file and
        symbol, or a decision recorded in the document.
    *   **ESCALATE**: The critique is inaccurate, but the evidence is outside every
        file the reviewer could read (for example, a team convention or a verbal
        decision). State that fact. Do not fix the finding. Give it to the user.
    *   **PROPOSE FIX**: The critique is valid. Define precise textual replacements
        or structural formatting adjustments to resolve the gap.
    *   **DECLINE**: The finding is a Nit. Record it. Do not fix it. You can use
        PROPOSE FIX for a Nit if the fix is worth it.
    
    Apply these rules:
    
    *   **A contest must be checkable.** "This was intentional" is not evidence.
        If you cannot cite evidence the reviewer could read, use ESCALATE or
        PROPOSE FIX.
    *   **Do not add context only to satisfy a reviewer.** Add context when a human
        reader of the document needs it. If only a zero-context subagent needs it,
        use ESCALATE.
    *   **Do not contest a comprehension gap.** If a fresh reader could not follow
        the document, the document is missing context.
    *   **Do not change a severity.** If you think a Blocker is a Nit, CONTEST it
        and state the reason.
    *   You wrote the document under review. A wish to contest is not evidence
        that the reviewer is wrong.
    
    ### Step 3: Report Fixes
    
    Construct the final report and save it named
    `goldfish_review_report.md` in the working directory (or your harness's artifact directory, if it has one)
    using your file-writing tool. Use this layout:
    
    ```markdown
    # Goldfish Annotated Review Report
    
    **Target:** `[TargetFile]` (`[LineRange]`)
    
    ## Prioritized Findings & AI Suggestions
    
    {{range findings, ordered by Severity}}
    ### [Issue 1] [`[ReviewerPersona]`] - Severity: [Blocker | Major | Nit]
    *   **Affected Scope:** [Lines Start-End]([RelativePath]#L[Start]-L[End]) ([Sub-header])
    *   **Discrepancy Description:** [copied from FindingsList]
    *   **Rationale:** [copied from FindingsList]
    *   ***AI Suggestion:*** [CONTEST | ESCALATE | PROPOSE FIX | DECLINE]
    *   ***Justification:*** [Detailed reason]
    *   ***Proposed Edit:***
        *   Location: [Line/Header]
        *   Change: [Precise replacement string or deletion note]
    {{end}}
    ```
    
    ### Step 4: Interactive Resolution Gate
    
    If any finding is `ESCALATE`, list those findings first in the chat message.
    They need the user's knowledge, not only approval.
    
    Before proceeding, output a visible chat message to the user: *"I have compiled
    the audit findings into `goldfish_review_report.md`. Please review the findings there and choose how you would like to
    proceed:
    
    -   **Comment directly on the file**: Review `goldfish_review_report.md` in
        chat or the file and leave comments/edits to approve, reject, or contest
        specific items.
    -   **Auto accept**: Reply "auto accept" to batch-apply all proposed fixes
        (skipping contested items).
    -   **Continue to next phase**: Reply "continue" or "no changes" to proceed
        without applying fixes.
    -   **Interactive breakdown**: Reply "interactive breakdown" for a guided,
        item-by-item walkthrough in chat with detailed explanations for each
        proposed edit or contested finding before making decisions.
    -   **Custom instruction / Wildcard request**: Reply with any custom
        instruction, question, or out-of-band request."*

## Activity

    Opened https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DPDK/dpdk/v25.11/drivers/net/intel/ixgbe/ixgbe_rxtx.c

## Assistant

An **Rx descriptor** is an entry in a NIC queue containing a buffer’s DMA address and reception status. An **mbuf** holds the packet storage and its software metadata. The PMD is the driver managing both.

For the contiguous packets we use, the usual lifecycle is:

1. **Setup:** the PMD allocates an mbuf from the supplied Rx mempool and puts its storage address into a descriptor.
2. **Arrival:** the NIC writes packet bytes into that storage and marks the descriptor complete.
3. **Reception:** the PMD reads the completed descriptor, replaces its buffer address with that of another mbuf allocated from the same pool, and returns the received mbuf to the application.
4. **Release:** when the application finishes with the received mbuf, it returns to the pool.

The descriptor stays in the ring; successive mbufs pass through it. Replacing the mbuf lets the NIC receive another packet while the application retains the previous one.

Allocation here means taking an existing mbuf from the fixed pool, without creating additional backing storage.

The ordering matters: ixgbe, for example, obtains the replacement **before handing the received mbuf to the application**. If allocation fails, it leaves that completed packet pending and stops processing the queue. [DPDK ixgbe source](https://github.com/DPDK/dpdk/blob/v25.11/drivers/net/intel/ixgbe/ixgbe_rxtx.c)

Thus, descriptors consume part of the supplied pool while armed. Other mbufs are free or held by the application. If every mbuf is posted initially, a replacement-first PMD has nothing available to perform that first handoff.

## User

so what is the problem?

## Assistant

Only the initial sizing: if the pool contains `N` mbufs and the PMD posts all `N` to Rx descriptors, a replacement-first PMD cannot deliver the first packet.

Configure fewer descriptors, leaving enough mbufs for the PMD’s refill operation. Later exhaustion from application retention is acceptable, as you specified.

This is routine queue setup, not an unresolved architectural issue. I overstated it.

## User

why would the PMD post all N to Rx descriptors?

## Assistant

It wouldn’t choose that automatically. `zxdp` supplies the descriptor count when configuring the Rx queue; the PMD populates those descriptors with mbufs.

Posting all `N` would result from `zxdp` choosing that count. Nothing requires that choice. My concern assumed a configuration we had never proposed, so it should not have been raised as an outstanding issue.

## User

what's the purpose of preventing the PMD from using descriptors/mbufs at startup

## Assistant

There is no purpose in preventing the PMD from using mbufs at startup.

The distinction is between **attaching an mbuf to a descriptor** and **leaving it available for the PMD to allocate as a replacement**. Both serve reception. Configuring fewer descriptors leaves the remaining mbufs available to the PMD; it does not reserve them for the application or prohibit their use.

My earlier wording made ordinary queue sizing sound like an additional restriction. No such restriction is needed.

## User

all of them should be available to the PMD - they're all rx mbufs

## Assistant

Yes. The entire Rx pool is available to the PMD. It allocates mbufs from that pool to populate descriptors and replenish them as received mbufs pass to the application.

Descriptor count configures the queue depth; it does not partition the pool or restrict which mbufs the PMD may use. No reserved subset is needed.

## User

right, so again, what is the question?

## Assistant

There is no outstanding question. The PMD uses the entire Rx pool, and `zxdp` derives queue sizing subject to driver requirements. Later pool exhaustion and packet loss are acceptable.

A3 should be closed as routine implementation detail.

## User

explain the loopback ownership question

## Assistant

With a NIC, reception uses a buffer from the receiver’s Rx pool. Zutcp wraps those bytes in an `IOBuf` and eventually returns the backing through its Rx allocator.

`net_ring` instead transfers the **sender’s mbuf pointer** directly to the receiver. It does not copy the packet into the receiver’s Rx pool. Directly connecting two instances therefore gives Zutcp backing from the sender’s Tx pool, while its receive path expects backing from its own Rx pool.

The proposed test-fixture solution is to simulate the wire: drain the sender’s outgoing mbuf, copy its bytes into an mbuf from the destination’s Rx pool, enqueue that mbuf for reception, and release the outgoing reference. Production DPDK remains unchanged; the copy exists only in the software peer fixture.

    // Interface geometry and direct IP carriage over Ethernet.
    
    #ifndef ZutcpIP_HH
    #define ZutcpIP_HH
    
    #ifndef ZutcpLib_HH
    #include <zlib/ZutcpLib.hh>
    #endif
    
    #include <stdint.h>
    
    #include <zlib/ZuSpan.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZuUnion.hh>
    
    #include <zlib/ZePlatform.hh>
    
    #include <zlib/ZiIP.hh>
    
    #include <zlib/ZutcpOptions.hh>
    
    namespace Zutcp {
    
    // Linux owns interface configuration. Query before creating Zi adapters so
    // their framing geometry is stable; validate again against the running backend.
    ZutcpAPI ZuUnion<unsigned, ZeException> interfaceMTU(unsigned interface);
    
    struct IPPath {
      ZiIP        local, remote;
      uint8_t    localMAC[6], remoteMAC[6];
      unsigned    mtu;
    };
    
    // Cold setup on the control caller: read the kernel's route constrained to this
    // interface and its static next-hop neighbor. Preserve an explicit local IP;
    // otherwise use the kernel-selected source. Publish only on success. No ARP/ND.
    ZutcpAPI ZuUnion<IPPath, ZeException> resolveIPPath(unsigned interface, IPPath);
    
    struct IPView {
      ZiIP        local, remote;
      ZuBSpan    payload;
      unsigned    protocol, ecn;
    };
    
    // The payload is already at frame + ipHead(type). Write only framing and
    // Ethernet padding, without moving payload or allocating backing. Return the
    // complete wire length, or zero without changing the frame on invalid geometry.
    inline unsigned ipHead(ZiIPType::T type) {
      switch (type) {
        case ZiIPType::V4: return 14 + 20;
        case ZiIPType::V6: return 14 + 40;
        default: return 0;
      }
    }
    ZutcpAPI unsigned writeIP(
      uint8_t *frame, unsigned capacity, const IPPath &, unsigned protocol,
      unsigned payload, unsigned ecn = 0);
    
    // This layer validates IP framing only; payload integrity belongs to the transport.
    // No UDP header, transport shim or payload checksum is added.
    // Output borrows the input packet. IPv4 options and common IPv6 extension
    // headers are traversed in place; fragmented datagrams need IP reassembly and
    // are not admitted as complete transport packets.
    ZutcpAPI bool readIP(ZuBSpan frame, IPView &);
    
    struct TCPHeader {
      uint16_t    srcPort = 0, dstPort = 0;
      uint32_t    seq = 0, ack = 0;
      uint16_t    window = 0, urgent = 0;
      uint8_t    flags = 0;
      TCPOptions    options = {};
    };
    
    struct TCPView {
      TCPHeader    header;
      ZuBSpan    options, payload;
    };
    
    inline unsigned tcpHead(ZiIPType::T type) {
      unsigned head = ipHead(type);
      return head ? head + 20 : 0;
    }
    
    inline unsigned tcpHead(ZiIPType::T type, const TCPHeader &header) {
      unsigned head = tcpHead(type);
      int options = header.options.encodedLength(header.flags & 0x02);
      return head && options >= 0 ? head + unsigned(options) : 0;
    }
    
    inline unsigned tcpPayload(unsigned mtu, ZiIPType::T type) {
      unsigned head = tcpHead(type);
      return head && mtu > head - 14 ? mtu - (head - 14) : 0;
    }
    
    // Construct TCP header/options over payload already at frame + tcpHead(type, header).
    // Includes IP framing and the mandatory TCP pseudo-header checksum. No payload
    // move or allocation; invalid geometry leaves the frame unchanged. Sequence,
    // ACK, flags and window semantics belong to the connection, not this codec.
    ZutcpAPI unsigned writeTCP(
      uint8_t *frame, unsigned capacity, const IPPath &, const TCPHeader &,
      unsigned payload, unsigned ecn = 0);
    
    // Consume the original IP payload, including any TCP options in its checksum.
    // The returned options/payload borrow that storage. Publish only on success.
    ZutcpAPI bool readTCP(const IPView &, TCPView &);
    
    } // namespace Zutcp
    
    #endif /* ZutcpIP_HH */

    name: egm-review-loop
    license: Apache-2.0
    disable-model-invocation: true
    description: >-
      Executes the Antagonistic-Review process from the Elephant-Goldfish
      Model (EGM) via an automated multi-agent review loop to audit documents
      against qualitative standards and structural templates, and automatically
      apply approved fixes. Use when reviewing design docs, READMEs, feature
      specifications, implementation plans, or verifying document completeness
      and tone.
    ---
    
    # Goldfish Review: Loop (Orchestration Driver)
    
    When running in Codex or ChatGPT Work, first read [Codex integration](../../docs/codex.md).
    In Claude Code or Cowork, read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/claude.md` first.
    
    ## Overview
    
    This skill acts as the central orchestration engine driving the multi-agent
    review loop. It coordinates two distinct agent memory models:
    
    *   **The Goldfish (Adversarial Auditors)**: Subagents spawned in isolated,
        fresh context windows to catch unstated assumptions without historical bias.
    *   **The Elephant (Persistent Resolver)**: The primary agent context holding
        institutional knowledge to evaluate findings and apply approved repairs.
    
    The driver manages argument intake, resolves paths for reviewers and standards,
    unconditionally re-parses target line ranges before every iteration, spawns
    concurrent specialized Goldfish auditors based on configuration, and coordinates
    with the Elephant context to resolve findings.
    
    ## Delegation
    
    A Goldfish runs in a fresh context with no conversation history. Spawn each
    subagent with your harness's subagent tool (Antigravity: `invoke_subagent`; Claude Code: `Agent`; Codex: `spawn_agent`). Each subagent is defined in `agents/<file>.md`, and its
    frontmatter `name` (for example `egm-zoom-out`) is the subagent type to request
    where your harness registers named subagents. Otherwise spawn a general-purpose
    subagent and tell it to read that persona file first. Pass the prompt verbatim
    and wait for the report. If your harness cannot nest subagents,
    use direct dispatch instead of the synthesizer. See `docs/harnesses.md`.
    If your harness has no subagent tool, stop and tell the user: a review in the same
    context is not a Goldfish review.
    
    ## Inputs
    
    The caller or user provides exactly these parameters:
    
    *   **`TargetFile`**: Absolute or relative path to target document.
    *   **`SemanticTarget`**: Descriptive targeting string (e.g., *"Target the H4
        block with SS-ID 'S1.12'"*), or `full file`.
    *   **`Reviewers`**: List of reviewer names (shortnames or paths).
    *   **`Standards`**: Mapping of reviewer names to standard names (shortnames or
        paths).
    *   **`GoldfishContext`**: A reading list (source files, directories, or
        documentation URLs) fed to reviewers to establish their baseline. An empty
        list from the caller counts as provided; do not ask for it again. Some
        reviewers cannot open URLs, so before the first round save the raw page of
        each URL as a new file in the working directory (or your harness's artifact
        directory) and pass its absolute path instead. If a page cannot be saved,
        ask the user for a local copy and end your turn; if no one can answer,
        as in a headless run, leave it out, tell the user, and keep going.
    
    ## Path & Standard Resolution Logic
    
    When resolving names in `Reviewers` and `Standards`:
    
    *   **Reviewer Shortnames**: Map reviewer shortname (e.g., `design_critic`,
        `structural`, `style`, `implementation_readiness`,
        `codebase_details`, `comprehension`, `zoom_out`) to `agents/{name}.md`.
        The persona file defines the reviewer's core mandates, audit vectors, and
        output format.
    *   **Standard Shortnames**: Map standard shortname (e.g., `feature-spec-standard`,
        `implementation-readiness-standard`, `zoom-out-standard`, `heilmeier-standard`,
        `re-implementation-standard`) to `resources/document_standards/{name}.md`.
    *   **Custom Paths**: If the name contains a slash (`/`), treat it as an
        absolute or workspace-relative path and read it directly.
    
    ## Execution Workflow
    
    ### Step 1: Intake & Configuration UX
    
    Evaluate the provided inputs (`TargetFile`, `SemanticTarget`, `Reviewers`,
    `Standards`, `GoldfishContext`).
    
    1.  **Identify Missing Inputs**: Determine which of the required parameters are
        missing.
    2.  **Interactive Onboarding**:
        *   If **all** inputs are present, proceed to Step 2.
        *   If **some or all** inputs are missing, interactively prompt the user
            **only for the missing inputs**, one at a time via chat messages.
    3.  **Reviewer Recommendations**:
        *   *Feature Specs*: Recommend `design_critic` (mapped to
            `resources/document_standards/feature-spec-standard.md`) and
            `structural` (mapped to `resources/document_standards/feature-spec-standard.md`).
        *   *Implementation Plans*: Recommend `implementation_readiness`
            (mapped to `resources/document_standards/implementation-readiness-standard.md`)
            and `codebase_details`.
    4.  **Confirm Configuration**: Display the consolidated plan (Target, Reviewers,

    bool Instance::unbind(const ZiSockAddr &local, void *owner)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      auto binding = m_endpoints->findPtr(local);
      if (!binding || binding->owner != owner) return false;
      m_endpoints->delNode(binding);
      return true;
    }
    
    bool Instance::resolvePath(IPPath path, RouteFn done)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (!ready() || !done) return false;
      unsigned worker = 0;
      for (unsigned i = 0; i < mx()->nWorkers(); ++i) {
        auto id = mx()->workerID(i);
        if (id != mx()->rxThread() && id != mx()->txThread()) { worker = id; break; }
      }
      if (!worker) worker = m_txSid;
      ++m_routePending;
      mx()->run([this, path = ZuMv(path), done = ZuMv(done)]() mutable {
        ZmAssert_(!mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()) && !mx()->invoked(mx()->txThread()));
        auto result = resolveIPPath(m_interface, ZuMv(path));
        mx()->rxRun([this, result = ZuMv(result), done = ZuMv(done)]() mutable {
          ZmAssert_(m_routePending);
          --m_routePending;
          if (!ready())
        result = ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "packet service stopped during route setup");
          done(ZuMv(result));
          if (m_state == Stopping && !m_endpointDrain && !m_routePending) {
        ZmAssert_(!cxnAdmission().total);
        mx()->txRun([this] { stopTx(); });
          }
        });
      }, worker);
      return true;
    }
    
    void Instance::start()
    {
      mx()->rxRun([this] { start_(); });
    }
    
    void Instance::start_()
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (ready()) { mx()->pluginStarted({}); return; }
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped);
      m_state = Starting;
      m_rxWakeQueued = 0;
      m_error = {};
      // A backend initializes once. Retain closed telemetry until this next start.
      if (m_backendInit) m_backend = Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Xdp);
      m_backendInit = true;
      Zxdp::Params config(
        Zxdp::Params::New<Zxdp::Params::Index<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>{}>{});
      auto &params = config.p<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>();
      params.ifindex = m_interface;
      params.netmask = m_netmask;
      params.rxPool = m_ingress->pool;
      params.rx = [this](uint8_t *p, unsigned n) { received(p, n); };
      params.spin = m_spin;
      params.scheduler = mx();
      params.txSid = m_txSid;
      params.txStopped = [this] {
        mx()->push([this] { senderStopped(); }, mx()->txThread());
      };
      for (auto p = m_providers; p; p = p->nextProvider)
        params.txPools.pushNode(p->pool.ptr());
      auto initialized = m_backend->init(config);
      if (initialized.is<ZeException>()) m_error = ZuMv(initialized.p<ZeException>());
      if (m_backend && m_backend->ready() && m_backend->mtu() == m_mtu) {
        m_current = m_backend.ptr();
        m_state = Running;
        mx()->pluginStarted({});
        return;
      }
      if (!m_error)
        m_error = ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "interface geometry changed before packet startup");
      m_startFailure = true;
      m_state = Stopping;
      mx()->txRun([this] { stopTx(); });
    }

    namespace Zutcp {
    
    class ZutcpAPI ISN {
    friend struct ISNTest;
    public:
      enum { SecretSize = 32, InputSize = 53 };
      ISN() = default;
      ISN(const ISN &) = delete;
      ISN &operator =(const ISN &) = delete;
      ~ISN();
    
      // Initialize once for the instance lifetime, including same-instance restart.
      // Failure leaves the primitive unavailable; there is no predictable fallback.
      bool init(unsigned interface);
      bool generate(const ZiSockAddr &local, const ZiSockAddr &remote, uint32_t &) const;
    
    private:
      bool init(unsigned interface, ZuTime origin, int (*random)(uint8_t *, int));
      bool init(ZuBSpan secret, ZuTime origin, unsigned interface);
      bool encode(const ZiSockAddr &local, const ZiSockAddr &remote, uint8_t *) const;
      bool generate(
        const ZiSockAddr &local, const ZiSockAddr &remote, ZuTime now, uint32_t &) const;
    
      uint8_t    m_secret[SecretSize] = {};
      ZuTime    m_origin;
      unsigned    m_interface = 0;
    };
    
    } // namespace Zutcp
    
    #endif /* ZutcpISN_HH */

    #include <string.h>
    #include <openssl/crypto.h>
    #include <openssl/evp.h>
    #include <openssl/hmac.h>
    #include <openssl/rand.h>
    
    #include <zlib/ZmTime.hh>
    
    #include <zlib/ZutcpISN.hh>
    
    namespace Zutcp {
    
    ISN::~ISN()
    {
      OPENSSL_cleanse(m_secret, sizeof(m_secret));
    }
    
    bool ISN::init(unsigned interface)
    {
      return init(interface, Zm::now(), RAND_priv_bytes);
    }
    
    bool ISN::init(unsigned interface, ZuTime origin, int (*random)(uint8_t *, int))
    {
      if (*m_origin || !*origin || !interface) return false;
      uint8_t secret[SecretSize];
      bool ok = random(secret, sizeof(secret)) == 1 &&
        init({secret, sizeof(secret)}, origin, interface);
      OPENSSL_cleanse(secret, sizeof(secret));
      return ok;
    }
    
    bool ISN::init(ZuBSpan secret, ZuTime origin, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (*m_origin || secret.length() != SecretSize || !*origin || !interface) return false;
      memcpy(m_secret, secret.data(), SecretSize);
      m_origin = origin;
      m_interface = interface;
      return true;
    }
    
    bool ISN::encode(const ZiSockAddr &local, const ZiSockAddr &remote, uint8_t *out) const
    {
      if (local.type() != remote.type() || !local.port() || !remote.port() ||
          (local.type() != ZiIPType::V4 && local.type() != ZiIPType::V6)) return false;
      memcpy(out, "Zutcp.ISN.v1", 12);
      out[12] = uint8_t(m_interface>>24);
      out[13] = uint8_t(m_interface>>16);
      out[14] = uint8_t(m_interface>>8);
      out[15] = uint8_t(m_interface);
      out[16] = local.type() == ZiIPType::V4 ? 4 : 6;
      if (local.type() == ZiIPType::V4) {
        memset(out + 17, 0, 12);
        memcpy(out + 29, &local.sin().sin_addr, 4);
        memset(out + 35, 0, 12);
        memcpy(out + 47, &remote.sin().sin_addr, 4);
      } else {
        memcpy(out + 17, &local.sin6().sin6_addr, 16);
        memcpy(out + 35, &remote.sin6().sin6_addr, 16);
      }
      out[33] = uint8_t(local.port()>>8);
      out[34] = uint8_t(local.port());
      out[51] = uint8_t(remote.port()>>8);
      out[52] = uint8_t(remote.port());
      return true;
    }
    
    bool ISN::generate(const ZiSockAddr &local, const ZiSockAddr &remote, uint32_t &out) const
    {
      return generate(local, remote, Zm::now(), out);
    }
    
    bool ISN::generate(
      const ZiSockAddr &local, const ZiSockAddr &remote, ZuTime now, uint32_t &out) const
    {
      if (!*m_origin || !*now) return false;
      uint8_t input[InputSize], digest[SecretSize];
      if (!encode(local, remote, input)) return false;
      unsigned length = 0;
      if (!HMAC(EVP_sha256(), m_secret, SecretSize, input, sizeof(input), digest, &length) ||
          length != sizeof(digest)) return false;
      uint32_t prf = (uint32_t(digest[0])<<24) | (uint32_t(digest[1])<<16) |
        (uint32_t(digest[2])<<8) | uint32_t(digest[3]);
      // The port uses the existing Zm time base, including its realtime semantics.
      out = prf + uint32_t((now - m_origin).microsecs()/4);
      return true;
    }

    4.  **Confirm Configuration**: Display the consolidated plan (Target, Reviewers,
        and mapped Standards) and ask the user to confirm before proceeding.
    
    ### Step 2: The Sharpening Loop (Iterative Cycle)
    
    Execute the following sequence in a continuous loop:
    
    #### 2.1 Unconditional Target Resolution
    
    Before every iteration, unconditionally re-scan `TargetFile` by reading it
    and using the stable `SemanticTarget` string (e.g., locating the target header) to
    dynamically determine the updated absolute start and end line numbers. This
    ensures absolute accuracy even if the file was edited in prior rounds. (If `full
    file` mode is specified, confirm full-file line bounds).
    
    #### 2.2 Review Swarm Execution
    
    1.  **Launch Subagent Swarm**:
        Spawn subagents to execute the review:
        *   **Hierarchical Dispatch (Synthesizer)**: Spawn the intermediate
            synthesizer subagent (`agents/synthesizer.md` / `egm-synthesizer`).
            The synthesizer spawns the Goldfish review swarm in
            parallel, deduplicates findings, writes the report artifact, and
            returns a single summary message to avoid context pollution in the root
            conversation. Pass it the Failed Reviewers rule below and
            `GoldfishContext`, and tell it to give those files to each reviewer.
            Its summary must give a status, `completed` or `not run`, for each
            requested reviewer.
        *   **Direct Dispatch (Flat Swarm)**: Alternatively, spawn each requested
            reviewer subagent in `Reviewers` directly.
            Instruct each subagent to first read its persona definition in
            `agents/{name}.md`, then audit `TargetFile` at the resolved line range
            against its designated standard in `resources/document_standards/`,
            supplying `GoldfishContext`.
        *   Each reviewer produces findings with severity (🔴 Blocker, 🟡 Major, 🟢
            Nit), line numbers, discrepancy descriptions, and rationales.
    2.  **Consolidate Findings**: Collect all findings across reviewers into a single
        flat `FindingsList`. Give each finding a stable id
        (`<reviewer>-<round>-<n>`) and record its reviewer, severity, and affected
        scope.
    3.  **Failed Reviewers**: A reviewer that times out, fails, or returns no report
        did not review. Retry it once. If it fails again, record it as **not run**
        in the report. Never count it as a reviewer with zero findings. If the
        synthesizer summary has no status for a requested reviewer, record that
        reviewer as not run.
    
    #### 2.3 Aggregated Resolution Hand-off
    
    1.  Pass `TargetFile`, the active line range, and the aggregated `FindingsList`
        to the **`egm-resolve`** workflow.
    2.  Execute the resolution workflow in the primary Elephant context:
        *   Categorize findings into `CONTEST` vs. `PROPOSE FIX`.
        *   Save `goldfish_review_report.md` with your file-writing tool.
        *   Present the interactive decision gate (Auto accept, Continue, Interactive
            breakdown).
        *   Apply approved text repairs to `TargetFile` using your file-editing tool.
    
    #### 2.4 Iteration Check & Turn Boundary
    
    Fresh reviewers sample differently each round, so a round with zero findings
    is rare even when the document improves. Use these rules instead:
    
    *   **Settled findings**: A finding is settled when it is contested or
        recorded without a fix (accepted risk). Keep the settled list across
        rounds. If a new reviewer raises a settled finding again (same affected
        scope, same issue), do not re-open it.
    *   **Fixed findings**: An applied fix does not settle a finding. If a later
        reviewer raises the same issue at the same scope, the fix failed or a
        later edit reintroduced the issue. Re-open the finding.
    *   **Clean round**: A round is clean when no reviewer raises a Blocker or
        Major finding that is not settled. Nits do not block. A reviewer recorded
        as not run makes the round not clean. Decide this from the review results,
        before you apply the fixes of that round.
    *   **Converged**: Two consecutive clean rounds. One clean round is not enough,
        because the next fresh reviewer can find a different gap in the same text.
    *   **Cap**: 5 rounds.

    static unsigned requireMTU(ZiMultiplex *mx, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (!mx) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "packet interface requires a multiplexer");
      auto result = interfaceMTU(interface);
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) throw ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      return result.p<unsigned>();
    }
    
    static unsigned ingressCount(ZiMultiplex *mx, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (mx->rxBufSize()) return mx->rxBufSize();
      auto result = Zxdp::Xdp::queryLink(interface);
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) throw ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      // Idle queues retain their FILL allocations. Each active queue needs room
      // beyond one connection's default retained list before its oldest can return.
      uint64_t count = uint64_t(result.p<Zxdp::Xdp::LinkState>().rxQueues) *
        (uint64_t(DefaultRxRetainPerCxn) + mx->rxQuantum());
      if (count > UINT_MAX) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "Rx pool count overflow");
      return count > ZiIOBuf_DefltCount ? unsigned(count) : ZiIOBuf_DefltCount;
    }
    
    static unsigned requirePackets(unsigned count)
    {
      if (!count) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "empty native packet pool");
      return count;
    }

    template <typename T>
    IOBufAllocFn tableBufAllocFn(ZiMultiplex *mx) {
      auto allocator = mx->allocator<Zi::IOBufType::App, IOBuf,
        ZdbBuf_Size<T>{}, ZiIOBuf_Align, ZdbBuf_HeapID<T>, MaxBufSize>();
      IOBufAllocFn fn{[allocator]() {
        ZmRef<IOBuf> buf = allocator->allocBuf();
        // Reserve the envelope before the backwards-growing row arena starts.
        buf->skip = Zfb::Wire::MaxAlign;
        return buf;
      }};
      fn.allocator(allocator);
      return fn;
    }

    static ZuUnion<IPPath, ZeException> resolvePath(int fd, unsigned interface, IPPath path)
    {
      auto family = path.remote.type() == ZiIPType::V4 ? AF_INET : AF_INET6;
      unsigned bytes = family == AF_INET ? sizeof(in_addr) : sizeof(in6_addr);
      const void *destination = family == AF_INET ?
        static_cast<const void *>(&path.remote.inAddr()) : &path.remote.in6Addr();
      // Each request has one protocol address plus one interface attribute at most.
      alignas(nlmsghdr) uint8_t request[NLMSG_SPACE(sizeof(rtmsg)) + RTA_SPACE(16) + RTA_SPACE(4)]{};
      alignas(nlmsghdr) uint8_t reply[4096];
      auto header = reinterpret_cast<nlmsghdr *>(request);
      header->nlmsg_len = NLMSG_LENGTH(sizeof(rtmsg));
      header->nlmsg_type = RTM_GETROUTE;
      header->nlmsg_flags = NLM_F_REQUEST;
      header->nlmsg_seq = 1;
      auto route = reinterpret_cast<rtmsg *>(NLMSG_DATA(header));
      route->rtm_family = family;
      route->rtm_dst_len = bytes<<3;
      routeAttr(header, RTA_DST, destination, bytes);
      routeAttr(header, RTA_OIF, &interface, sizeof(interface));
      auto result = queryRoute(fd, header, reply, sizeof(reply));
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      auto answer = reinterpret_cast<nlmsghdr *>(reply);
      if (answer->nlmsg_type != RTM_NEWROUTE || answer->nlmsg_len < NLMSG_LENGTH(sizeof(rtmsg))) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "missing route result");
      }
      route = reinterpret_cast<rtmsg *>(NLMSG_DATA(answer));
      if (route->rtm_family != family || route->rtm_type != RTN_UNICAST) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "route is not unicast on the configured interface");
      }
      uint8_t nextHop[16];
      memcpy(nextHop, destination, bytes);
      ZiIP source;

        }
          } break;
        }
      }
      if (output != interface)
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "route selected a different interface");
      if (path.local.type() == ZiIPType::Null || path.local.wildcard()) {

      }

      header->nlmsg_len = NLMSG_LENGTH(sizeof(ndmsg));
      header->nlmsg_type = RTM_GETNEIGH;
      header->nlmsg_flags = NLM_F_REQUEST;
      header->nlmsg_seq = 2;
      auto neighbor = reinterpret_cast<ndmsg *>(NLMSG_DATA(header));
      neighbor->ndm_family = family;
      neighbor->ndm_ifindex = interface;
      routeAttr(header, NDA_DST, nextHop, bytes);
      result = queryRoute(fd, header, reply, sizeof(reply));
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      answer = reinterpret_cast<nlmsghdr *>(reply);
      if (answer->nlmsg_type != RTM_NEWNEIGH || answer->nlmsg_len < NLMSG_LENGTH(sizeof(ndmsg))) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "missing neighbor result");
      }
      neighbor = reinterpret_cast<ndmsg *>(NLMSG_DATA(answer));
      if (neighbor->ndm_family != family || neighbor->ndm_ifindex != int(interface) ||
          !(neighbor->ndm_state & (NUD_PERMANENT | NUD_NOARP))) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "next hop has no static neighbor");
      }
      bool found = false;
      remaining = NLMSG_PAYLOAD(answer, sizeof(ndmsg));
      auto attr = reinterpret_cast<rtattr *>(
        reinterpret_cast<uint8_t *>(neighbor) + NLMSG_ALIGN(sizeof(ndmsg)));
      for (; RTA_OK(attr, remaining); attr = RTA_NEXT(attr, remaining))
        if (attr->rta_type == NDA_LLADDR && RTA_PAYLOAD(attr) == sizeof(path.remoteMAC)) {
          memcpy(path.remoteMAC, RTA_DATA(attr), sizeof(path.remoteMAC));
          found = true;
        }
      if (!found) return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "static neighbor has no Ethernet address");
      return path;
    }
    
    ZuUnion<IPPath, ZeException> resolveIPPath(unsigned interface, IPPath path)
    {
      if ((path.remote.type() != ZiIPType::V4 && path.remote.type() != ZiIPType::V6) ||
          path.remote.wildcard() ||
          (path.local.type() != ZiIPType::Null && path.local.type() != path.remote.type()))
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid route address family");
      auto mtu = interfaceMTU(interface);
      if (mtu.is<ZeException>()) return ZuMv(mtu.p<ZeException>());
      path.mtu = mtu.p<unsigned>();
      ifreq link{};
      if (!if_indextoname(interface, link.ifr_name))
        return osError("interface name query", errno);
      int query = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
      if (query < 0) return osError("interface query socket", errno);
      auto hardware = ioctl(query, SIOCGIFHWADDR, &link);
      auto saved = errno;
      close(query);
      if (hardware < 0) return osError("interface MAC query", saved);
      if (link.ifr_hwaddr.sa_family != ARPHRD_ETHER)
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "interface has no Ethernet address");
      memcpy(path.localMAC, link.ifr_hwaddr.sa_data, sizeof(path.localMAC));
      int fd = socket(AF_NETLINK, SOCK_RAW | SOCK_CLOEXEC, NETLINK_ROUTE);
      if (fd < 0) return osError("route query socket", errno);
      timeval timeout{1, 0};
      ZuUnion<IPPath, ZeException> result;
      if (setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, &timeout, sizeof(timeout)))
        result = osError("route query timeout", errno);
      else
        result = resolvePath(fd, interface, ZuMv(path));
      close(fd);
      return result;
    }

## Assistant

Yes—the neighbor lookup requirement is shared by both backends.

Currently, Zutcp uses Linux netlink to find the route’s next hop and read its MAC address. **It requires a static neighbor entry; it neither initiates ARP/ND nor accepts dynamically learned entries.** The AF_XDP fixtures configure those static entries explicitly. See [the lookup](/home/count0/src/z/zutcp/src/ZutcpIP.cc:164).

AF_XDP itself does not resolve neighbors. Its Linux interface remains available, but kernel ARP/ND also depends on the XDP filter allowing that traffic through; the current unfiltered mode redirects all ingress.

I should have separated the shared missing dynamic-neighbor support from the DPDK-specific question of how kernel control traffic reaches the link.
