    # Instance ownership boundary
    
    Applications statically construct/configure one Instance and install it through
    ZiMultiplex::plugin() before allocator registration. Transfer code uses Ztcp/Ztls
    or the generic Zi callback interface. There is no Zutcp Hub/Client/Server
    application transport hierarchy or nativeInstance() bridge. Instance directly
    owns outgoing/accepted protocol records, listener endpoints, admission, secrets,
    history and native pools. Internal listeners own only local bind/options,
    pending/live membership and listener drain state.
    
    Instance implements ZiMxPlugin and its inherited Ztc::Mx interface, not Ztc::Hub.
    allQueues() traverses existing internal objects to expose normalized queue
    telemetry, including Zxdp's existing allQueues(). Do not add queue containers,
    indexes, registries or tracking caches. Existing object-lifetime references during
    enumeration protect callbacks that request asynchronous connection closure.
    
    Destination route/static-neighbor lookup runs synchronously on mx Rx during
    outbound and passive setup. It is intentional bounded blocking netlink work,
    with no route-worker selection or round trip. This supersedes historical notes
    below that place lookup outside Rx/Tx. Preserve real Rx/Tx ownership and ordered
    teardown; test contexts cannot reintroduce a second production owner or mode.
    
    # Current Phase 8 execution boundary
    
    The live protocol uses standard
    TCP headers/options and raw application bytes over Instance/Zxdp. Endpoint ownership
    uses TCP tuples; accepted byte history, canonical backing and owner handoffs
    remain authoritative. Intermediate packet/frame codecs and peer packet-number
    acknowledgments are deleted. Providers reserve the maximum standard Ethernet,
    IPv6 and TCP headers (114 bytes); the intermediate extra64-byte reserve is gone.
    
    Keep the accepted whole-original send/recovery policy, including positive peer
    windows smaller than an original. RST receive policy is window-qualified, with
    silent out-of-window rejection and no reflection of accepted peer resets.
    
    Raw send returns accepted/refused without a commit callback. Tx publishes the
    packet's ACK monotonically through the atomic `sentAck` only after successful
    return, then finishes recovery bookkeeping before queued peer-ACK work runs.
    Rx admits peer ACKs without consulting a transmitted byte frontier. Keep
    generation checks and the independent receive-window and RST qualification.
    
    Native providers implement `Zi::IOBufPool` over storage injected from a selected
    `Zxdp::Instance` backend's `bufPool()` factory. Keep concrete pool classes internal
    to Zxdp. Configuration owns its pool list; initialization retains independent
    backend references so configuration-list membership can expire after `init()`.
    Tx buffer allocation failure drops the connection; producers do not wait for
    pool grants. Alignment changes physical stride without inflating logical buffer capacity.
    
    Build/test Zutcp and its dependency closure in explicit directory/target order.
    Use the five native drivers and separate independent-kernel interop runner while
    finishing TCP. Selected Ztcp/Ztls application checks follow TCP completion; they
    are optional consumers and are not dependencies of Zutcp. Preserve the existing mx/XDP ownership model throughout.
    
    The phase-specific notes below record earlier implementation boundaries. Current
    Phase 8 wire changes supersede their references to intermediate framing.
    
    # Historical Phase 1 execution boundary
    
    The live transport now uses Instance/Zxdp with TCP-aligned IP carriage. The native
    endpoint tests exercise the client/server cutover and working pairs. Do not restore a kernel UDP mode,
    fallback or separate backend. Cold interface/route/static-neighbor queries remain
    control work outside Rx/Tx.
    
    Allocator dependency is strictly one way: Zutcp supplies lower-level pool
    providers through the ZiMxPlugin allocator hook. Do not call
    `ZiMultiplex::allocator` from Zutcp, directly or through a helper. Instance owns its
    internal native packet pool and metadata adapters independently of that factory.
    Queued Tx ranges now retain their existing node through `TxBacking`. Keep stable
    base/extent and raw lease ownership there, separately from the queue's mutable
    offset/length. Retained frames must survive queue removal and submitted Zi
    metadata destruction without owning a connection. Before raw handoff the node's
    pending descriptor owns source storage; clear that descriptor after accepted
    detachment. Native writers now allocate through Instance's local producer adapter
    and first submission reuses the same registered slot. The inline TxData type and
    queue are removed. Preserve whole-buffer credit admission, bounded piggyback
    prefix space and unchanged application payload addresses. Restore producer view
    metadata on refusal. Preserve the copied recovery/packetization algorithms in
    Phase 1. Native first submission reuses its original registered allocation;
    recovery builds the inherited selected ranges using the existing source storage.
    Do not restore covering-packet retransmission, header movement into ACKed payload,
    queued path-cap migration or the CQ waiter extension as Phase 1 requirements.
    Backing-lifetime fixes remain: final ACK of all prepared native source bytes
    returns the caller lease before producer callbacks, while kernel retirement
    independently gates physical reuse. Historical frame metadata cannot resurrect
    ACKed native byte work or assemble retired payload storage.
    
    Phase 1 is stripping plus IP/Zxdp wiring and regression testing. No new recovery,
    congestion, flow-control or packetization behavior belongs in that phase. Broader
    pressure/fairness/lifecycle/observation matrices are later work, not extra exit
    gates. See the current boundary above.
    
    Framework/application callers request their own higher-level allocators from mx;
    factory exercises belong in tests or clients. The locally owned builtin byte
    adapter remains for receive heap replacement; it is not a native producer
    fallback. Shared source nodes own native data leases through their frame ranges;
    existing sent-record nodes own copied/control packet leases. Both are independent
    of kernel CQ. Keep temporary Zi handoff scoped to synchronous submission and
    clear it before refusal can discard its record. Provider owners drain all these
    references before provider destruction.
    
    # Select Zutcp or the regular kernel TCP backend
    
    Zutcp implements TCP for applications using this repository's `ZiMultiplex`
    connection and allocator interfaces. Install `Zutcp::Instance` on the multiplexer to
    select AF_XDP; leave the plugin unset to use regular kernel TCP. Existing Zi/Ztcp
    application framing and callbacks remain in use. Ztls can run above either TCP
    backend; it is not a dependency of libZutcp.
    
    This is an application integration choice, not an `LD_PRELOAD` library or a
    replacement implementation of arbitrary POSIX `socket()` calls. Applications
    using raw kernel sockets continue to use the kernel until adapted to Zi/Ztcp. `zutcpkernelpeer` deliberately uses ordinary kernel sockets;
    `zutcppair` deliberately uses the actual native Instance, without socket fallback.
    
    ## Select the backend before allocating or starting
    
    The following setup illustrates the existing public API; handle configuration
    and startup failures in the application's normal error path:
    
    ```cpp
    #include <net/if.h>
    #include <zlib/ZiRx.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZiTx.hh>
    #include <zlib/Zutcp.hh>
    
    ZiMultiplex mx{ZiMxParams{}.rxThread(1).txThread(2).scheduler([](auto &s) {
      s.nThreads(3)
        .thread(1, [](auto &t) { t.isolated(1); })
        .thread(2, [](auto &t) { t.isolated(1); })
        .thread(3, [](auto &t) { t.isolated(true); });
    })};
    
    // Native branch only. Check if_nametoindex() before constructing Instance.
    auto stack = new Zutcp::Instance{&mx,
      {.interface = if_nametoindex("OWNED_INTERFACE"), .txSid = 3}};
    Zutcp::InstanceConfig config;
    auto configured = stack->configure(config);
    if (configured.is<ZeException>()) {
      /* report configured.p<ZeException>() and stop setup */
    }
    
    mx.plugin(stack);
    
    // Factory calls follow plugin registration while mx is still stopped.
    auto rx = mx.allocator<Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP, ZiRxBuf, 2048>(4096);
    auto tx = mx.allocator<Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP, ZiIOBuf, 1024>(4096);
    // Initialize the Ztcp application while stopped.
    // Start mx, then use ordinary listen/connect entry points.
    ```
    
    For the kernel branch, omit Instance construction, `plugin()` and Instance configuration;
    use the same Zi connection/framing interfaces. Backend selection is fixed for the
    multiplexer lifetime. Do not attach the plugin after allocator factories: native
    providers must publish and register their geometry before start. For native Tx,
    use those registered Tx buffers and their published payload budget; do not substitute
    heap/network buffers. `rxBufSize` is kernel socket bytes in kernel mode and native
    ingress frame count with Instance, so do not pass a byte count as a native frame count.
    The factory count requests pool backing; kernel allocation does not emulate a
    fixed native pool. Log effective settings when comparing backends.
    
    Protocol Rx and Tx run on the selected mx owners. Keep application dispatch and
    buffer lifetime rules intact. The client/server examples use Ztcp streams and
    callbacks with static Instance bootstrap; they do not construct Zutcp connection
    classes. The binary [zutcppair.cc](zutcppair.cc) uses the same Ztcp path. Its
    server observes EOF through the existing generic Zi receive context, forwards
    data to Ztcp, and queues its reply on application Tx. Only the control caller
    waits for the Tx barrier and ZiConnection::sync() before requesting physical
    graceful disconnect. The Ztcp link remains attached while the peer finishes.
    
    Protocol-specific TFO authorization, tuple history, fault controls and native
    pool/drain checks are private roles of [zutcppairtest.cc](../itest/zutcppairtest.cc),
    not alternate application transport APIs. Fixtures select those roles when a case
    requires private protocol access. Ordinary application runs retain the Ztcp path.
    The [FIX benchmark](../bench/README.md) uses the mapped ZiConnection application path.
    
    Stop application work and listeners, drain callbacks, then stop mx. Instance is
    the single plugin transport owner. Do not free it or registered backing while
    queued I/O or kernel retirement can still reference them. No separate native
    Hub lifecycle exists.

    using IOBufAllocFactory = ZmFn<IOBufAllocFn(ZiMultiplex *)>;
    
    template <typename T>
    IOBufAllocFn tableBufAllocFn(ZiMultiplex *mx) {
      auto allocator = mx->allocator<Zi::IOBufType::App, IOBuf,
        ZdbBuf_Size<T>{}, ZiIOBuf_Align, ZdbBuf_HeapID<T>, MaxBufSize>();
      IOBufAllocFn fn{[allocator]() {
        ZmRef<IOBuf> buf = allocator->allocBuf();
        // Reserve the envelope before the backwards-growing row arena starts.
        buf->skip = Zfb::Wire::MaxAlign;
        return buf;
      }};
      fn.allocator(allocator);
      return fn;
    }

    ### Single Zutcp instance architecture — adopted
    
    The application path is `Ztcp → ZiMultiplex → ZiMxPlugin`, implemented by one
    `Zutcp::Instance` supporting outbound connections and listening/accepted
    connections together. The app statically constructs/configures Instance and
    installs it through the existing ZiMultiplex::plugin() setter. Instance implements
    ZiMxPlugin and thereby Ztc::Mx, not Ztc::Hub; do not add a Hub adapter or another
    lifecycle owner.
    
    The repair in `zutcp_repair3.md` removes the copied Hub/Client/Server application
    hierarchy and nativeInstance() bridge. Shared transport configuration, admission,
    secrets, history, connection ownership and pools belong to Instance. Internal
    connection records point directly to it; listeners retain only their local bind,
    options, pending/live membership and listener drain state. The implementation
    changes are present; complete native acceptance remains a gate before DPDK work.
    
    Ztc::Mx::allQueues() is an observational traversal of existing internal objects
    that exposes normalized telemetry for their actual queues, including queues
    within Zxdp through its existing allQueues(). No extra queue container, index,
    registry or tracking cache is permitted. Preserve existing callback/owner lifetime
    rules; telemetry does not create a second transport owner.
    
    Production examples use Ztcp/ZiMultiplex with static plugin bootstrap. Protocol
    fixtures use private connection/endpoint facilities against the actual Instance,
    without preserving the removed public application API. Preserve Rx/Tx ownership,
    asynchronous draining and independent unit/native/wire assertions. Resolve repair
    acceptance before finalizing DPDK consumer parameters; DPDK configures this same
    Instance used by AF_XDP.

    ## Consumer integration: Linux routes and static neighbors — adopted
    
    Preserve the existing Zutcp control-plane arrangement when substituting DPDK
    for AF_XDP. The application/fixture chooses endpoint IP addresses, configures
    Linux routes and installs permanent next-hop IP-to-MAC neighbor entries.
    Zutcp queries those routes and static neighbors through its existing cold
    netlink path, then constructs the Ethernet frames passed to Zxdp. Replies may
    use the return path derived from received Ethernet framing as they do today.
    Routing and neighbor resolution belong to Zutcp, not Zxdp.
    
    Keep a Linux routing-interface identity in Zutcp configuration and associate it
    explicitly with the selected named DPDK port. The fixture supplies this mapping;
    the Linux control-plane interface need not be the physical device owned by the
    PMD. Configure its source addresses, routes, MTU and neighbor MAC mappings to
    represent the DPDK link. Source MAC/MTU used for packet construction must match
    the selected DPDK port's established geometry. A DPDK port ID is not an ifindex.
    No packet forwarding through that control-plane interface is needed for static
    route/neighbor queries.
    
    For ring fixtures, choose fixed endpoint IPs and device MACs, install the
    corresponding Linux routes/permanent neighbors, and configure the associated
    DPDK ports consistently. The software peer still performs the adopted transfer

    Retain the instance's TCP secrets across restart
    and use its Linux control-plane identity where the existing ISN setup needs it.
    No ISN algorithm or scope API change is required by this resolution.

    usage() {
    cat << .
    Usage: z.config [OPTIONS] PREFIX
    
    Options:
        -a ARCH    specify architecture (default: x86-64-v2)
        -L        use clang / llvm (default: gcc)
        -k PREFIX    build QuickFIX interop from PREFIX (default: no)
        -c        force re-configure
        -d        debug build (default: release)
        -D        address sanitizer build
        -C        coverage build
        -p        profiling build
        -M        build for MinGW-w64
        -l        pass --enable-libtool-lock to configure
        -G        build without Gtk
        -P        build without PostgreSQL
        -S        build without SQLite3
        -F        include network traffic filtering (ZiMultiplex_FILTER)
        -Q        include QUIC diagnostics (Zquic_DEBUG)
    .
    }
    
    ARCH="x86-64-v2"
    OPREFIX=
    CLANG=0
    CONFIG=0
    DEBUG=0
    MINGW=0
    LIBTOOL_LOCK=""
    GTK="yes"
    PQ="yes"
    SQLITE="yes"
    COVERAGE=0
    PROFILE=0
    NETFILTER=0
    QUICDEBUG=0
    QUICKFIX="no"
    
    while getopts "a:k:LcdDCpMlGPSFQh" arg
    do case $arg in
      a) ARCH=$OPTARG;;
      k) QUICKFIX=$OPTARG;;
      L) CLANG=1;;
      c) CONFIG=1;;
      d) DEBUG=1;;
      D) DEBUG=2; CLANG=1;;
      C) COVERAGE=1;;
      p) PROFILE=1;;
      M) MINGW=1;;
      l) LIBTOOL_LOCK="--enable-libtool-lock";;
      G) GTK="no";;
      P) PQ="no";;
      S) SQLITE="no";;
      F) NETFILTER=1;;
      Q) QUICDEBUG=1;;
      h) usage; exit 0;;
    esac; done
    shift $(($OPTIND - 1))
    
    PREFIX=$1
    [ -z "$PREFIX" ] && { usage; exit 1; }
    
    if [ $DEBUG -eq 1 ]; then
      FLAGS="-march=$ARCH -g -DZDEBUG"
    elif [ $DEBUG -eq 2 ]; then
      FLAGS="-march=$ARCH -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fno-optimize-sibling-calls -DZDEBUG"
      SAN_IGNORELIST=`pwd`"/.clang-sanitize-ignorelist"
      [ -f "$SAN_IGNORELIST" ] && FLAGS="$FLAGS -fsanitize-ignorelist=$SAN_IGNORELIST"
    else
      FLAGS="-march=$ARCH -O3 -g $OPTFLAGS -DNDEBUG"
    fi
    LDFLAGS=""
      ]], [[FIX::DataDictionary dictionary; return dictionary.isMsgType("D");]])],
        [z_have_quickfix=yes], [AC_MSG_ERROR([QuickFIX headers/library with SSL required])])
      CPPFLAGS=$z_quickfix_CPPFLAGS
      LIBS=$z_quickfix_LIBS
      AS_IF([test ! -f "$QUICKFIX_DICT"], [AC_MSG_ERROR([Canonical FIX44.xml not found: $QUICKFIX_DICT])])
    ])
    AC_SUBST(QUICKFIX_CFLAGS)
    AC_SUBST(QUICKFIX_LIBS)
    AM_CONDITIONAL([HAVE_QUICKFIX], [test "x$z_have_quickfix" = "xyes"])
    
    # postgres libpq (optional)
    AC_ARG_WITH([pq], AS_HELP_STRING([--with-pq], [Build with PostgreSQL]))
    AS_IF([test ".$with_pq" = ".yes"], [
      PKG_CHECK_MODULES([PQ], [libpq >= 16], [], [dnl
        AC_MSG_ERROR([libpq unavailable])
      ])
      AC_SUBST(PQ_CFLAGS)
      AC_SUBST(PQ_LIBS)
    ])
    AM_CONDITIONAL([LIBPQ], [test ".$with_pq" = ".yes"])
    
    # sqlite3 (enabled by default)
    AC_ARG_WITH([sqlite],
      AS_HELP_STRING([--without-sqlite], [Build without SQLite3]), [],
      [with_sqlite=yes])
    AS_IF([test ".$with_sqlite" = ".yes"], [
      PKG_CHECK_MODULES([SQLITE], [sqlite3 >= 3.37.0], [], [dnl
        AC_MSG_ERROR([sqlite3 >= 3.37.0 unavailable])
      ])
      AC_SUBST(SQLITE_CFLAGS)
      AC_SUBST(SQLITE_LIBS)
    ])
    AM_CONDITIONAL([SQLITE], [test ".$with_sqlite" = ".yes"])
    
    # Gtk (optional)
    AC_ARG_WITH([gtk], AS_HELP_STRING([--with-gtk], [Build with Gtk]))

    Instance::Instance(ZiMultiplex *mx, InstanceParams params)
    : ZiMxPlugin{mx}, m_interface{requireTCPSecrets(m_isn, m_tfoKey, params.interface)},
      m_mtu{requireMTU(mx, params.interface)},
      m_spin{params.spin},
      m_txSid{params.txSid},
      m_netmask{params.netmask}, m_packet{ZuMv(params.packet)},
      m_backend{Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Xdp)},
      m_ingress{new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(
        ingressCount(mx, m_interface), m_mtu + 14)}},
      m_rxAllocator{mx, m_ingress},
      m_packets{new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(
        requirePackets(params.packetCount), m_mtu + 14, 14 + 40 + 60)}},
      m_control{new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(
        DefaultControlBufCount, m_mtu + 14, 14 + 40 + 60)}},
      m_packetAllocator{mx, m_packets}, m_dataAllocator{mx, m_packets},
      m_controlAllocator{mx, m_control},
      m_endpoints{new EndpointBindings{ZmHashParams{}.bits(5).loadFactor(1).cBits(3)
        .init("Zutcp.Endpoints")}}
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped);
      // TCP controls use separate native backing and never borrow application slots.
      m_tfoCookies.queueOwner(mx->id());
      m_closed.queueOwner(mx->id());
      m_ingress->returned = [this] {
        if (!ready() || this->mx()->invoked(this->mx()->rxThread()) ||
        m_rxWakeQueued.xch(1)) return;
        // Replenish an empty FILL ring even when no packet can make it readable.
        // Queueing through mx supplies both scheduler re-entry and backend wake.
        this->mx()->rxRun([this] { m_rxWakeQueued = 0; });
      };
      addProvider(m_packets);
      addProvider(m_control);
    }
    
    Zi::IOBufPool *Instance::allocator(
      Zi::IOBufType::T type, unsigned size, unsigned align, unsigned count)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped);
      // Providers reserve complete output framing before Zi copies their geometry.
      enum { Ethernet = 14, IPv6 = 40, TCP = 60 };
      unsigned head;
      switch (type) {
        case Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP:
        case Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP: head = Ethernet + IPv6 + TCP; break;
        default: throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported network allocator role");
      }
      if (head >= m_mtu + Ethernet || !align || (align & (align - 1)) ||
          align > unsigned(sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)))
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported packet allocator geometry");
      if (type == Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP)
        return new RxAllocator{m_ingress, head, count, align};
      uint64_t bytes = uint64_t(size) + head;
      if (bytes > m_mtu + Ethernet) bytes = m_mtu + Ethernet;
      auto p = new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(count, unsigned(bytes), head, 0, align)};
      addProvider(p);
      return p;
    }
    
    ZuUnion<void, ZeException> Instance::configureControl(unsigned count, unsigned credits)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped && m_state == Stopped);
      uint64_t capacity = m_txCapacity - m_control->pool->count + count;
      mx()->rxRun([this] { start_(); });
    }
    
    void Instance::start_()
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (ready()) { mx()->pluginStarted({}); return; }
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped);
      m_state = Starting;
      m_rxWakeQueued = 0;
      m_error = {};
      // A backend initializes once. Retain closed telemetry until this next start.
      if (m_backendInit) m_backend = Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Xdp);
      m_backendInit = true;
      Zxdp::Params config(
        Zxdp::Params::New<Zxdp::Params::Index<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>{}>{});
      auto &params = config.p<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>();
      params.ifindex = m_interface;
      params.netmask = m_netmask;
      params.rxPool = m_ingress->pool;
      params.rx = [this](uint8_t *p, unsigned n) { received(p, n); };
      params.spin = m_spin;
      params.scheduler = mx();
      params.txSid = m_txSid;
      params.txStopped = [this] {
        mx()->push([this] { senderStopped(); }, mx()->txThread());
      };
      for (auto p = m_providers; p; p = p->nextProvider)
        params.txPools.pushNode(p->pool.ptr());
      auto initialized = m_backend->init(config);
      if (initialized.is<ZeException>()) m_error = ZuMv(initialized.p<ZeException>());
      if (m_backend && m_backend->ready() && m_backend->mtu() == m_mtu) {
        m_current = m_backend.ptr();
        m_state = Running;
        mx()->pluginStarted({});
        return;
      }
      if (!m_error)
        m_error = ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "interface geometry changed before packet startup");
      m_startFailure = true;
      m_state = Stopping;
      mx()->txRun([this] { stopTx(); });
    }

    ### Single Zutcp instance architecture — adopted
    
    The application path is `Ztcp → ZiMultiplex → ZiMxPlugin`, implemented by one
    `Zutcp::Instance` supporting outbound connections and listening/accepted
    connections together. The app statically constructs/configures Instance and
    installs it through the existing ZiMultiplex::plugin() setter. Instance implements
    ZiMxPlugin and thereby Ztc::Mx, not Ztc::Hub; do not add a Hub adapter or another
    lifecycle owner.
    
    The repair in `zutcp_repair3.md` removes the copied Hub/Client/Server application
    hierarchy and nativeInstance() bridge. Shared transport configuration, admission,
    secrets, history, connection ownership and pools belong to Instance. Internal
    connection records point directly to it; listeners retain only their local bind,
    options, pending/live membership and listener drain state. The implementation
    changes are present; complete native acceptance remains a gate before DPDK work.
    
    Ztc::Mx::allQueues() is an observational traversal of existing internal objects
    that exposes normalized telemetry for their actual queues, including queues
    within Zxdp through its existing allQueues(). No extra queue container, index,
    registry or tracking cache is permitted. Preserve existing callback/owner lifetime
    rules; telemetry does not create a second transport owner.
    
    Production examples use Ztcp/ZiMultiplex with static plugin bootstrap. Protocol
    fixtures use private connection/endpoint facilities against the actual Instance,
    without preserving the removed public application API. Preserve Rx/Tx ownership,
    asynchronous draining and independent unit/native/wire assertions. Resolve repair
    acceptance before finalizing DPDK consumer parameters; DPDK configures this same
    Instance used by AF_XDP.

    static unsigned requireMTU(ZiMultiplex *mx, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (!mx) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "packet interface requires a multiplexer");
      auto result = interfaceMTU(interface);
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) throw ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      return result.p<unsigned>();
    }
    
    static unsigned ingressCount(ZiMultiplex *mx, unsigned interface)
    {
      if (mx->rxBufSize()) return mx->rxBufSize();
      auto result = Zxdp::Xdp::queryLink(interface);
      if (result.is<ZeException>()) throw ZuMv(result.p<ZeException>());
      // Idle queues retain their FILL allocations. Each active queue needs room
      // beyond one connection's default retained list before its oldest can return.
      uint64_t count = uint64_t(result.p<Zxdp::Xdp::LinkState>().rxQueues) *
        (uint64_t(DefaultRxRetainPerCxn) + mx->rxQuantum());
      if (count > UINT_MAX) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "Rx pool count overflow");
      return count > ZiIOBuf_DefltCount ? unsigned(count) : ZiIOBuf_DefltCount;
    }
    
    static unsigned requirePackets(unsigned count)
    {
      if (!count) throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "empty native packet pool");
      return count;
    }

    ## Quick commands
    
    - `./z.config /opt/z` configures the build with a prefix; use `./z.config -h` for options. Common flags include `-c` to rerun `autoreconf`, `-d` for debug, `-L` for clang, `-G` to disable Gtk, `-P` to disable PostgreSQL, and `-M` for MinGW.
    - `make -j8` builds all enabled modules plus their test binaries.
    - `make install` installs libraries/headers into the configured prefix.
    - `make test` runs tests.
    - Use `libtool exec` to run source-tree test binaries under `gdb`, `valgrind`, and similar tools; do not run binaries from `.libs` directly.
    - Some optional features (for example libbfd backtracing) require external builds; see [README.md](../README.md) for platform-specific steps.
    
    
    ## Testing Guidelines
    - Tests are built as standalone binaries under each module’s `test/` directory.
    - Run specific tests directly from the build tree, for example
      `./zt/test/ZtArrayTest` or `./zdb/itest/zdbsmoketest`.
    - Use `ZuTestUtil` and underlying `ZuTest` for TAP-emitting unit tests.
    - No top-level coverage target is defined; document any new test entry points in the module `test/` directory.
    
    
    ## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
    - For small commits, use a single commit-message line of 94 characters or fewer.
    - For large commits involving multiple changes, use a single overview line followed by `- ` bullets, one for each significant change. Keep each line to 94 characters or fewer.
    - Large global renames or cleanups may be summarized as such.
    - For PRs, include a short summary, list touched modules, and note tests run plus platform/toolchain details.
    
    
    ## Dependencies & Configuration Notes
    Core dependencies include `libck`, `hwloc`, `pcre`, and `zpicotls`. Canonical `flatbuffers` and `flatc` are used only by explicit FlatBuffers interop targets. Optional components include `libpq` (PostgreSQL) and `gtk+3`; enable/disable via `z.config` (`-P`, `-G`) or `configure` flags.

    # Zxdp implementation rules
    
    Follow the repository guidance in ../AGENTS.md and the caller-supplied
    [interface contract](INTERFACE.md). The contract supersedes earlier plans.
    
    * Select a cold backend with `instance(Type::Xdp)`, then call virtual
      `init(const Params &)` with backend `Xdp::Params` constructed in place using
      `Params::New<Params::Index<Xdp::Params>{}>{}`. Configuration: interface index,
      optional destination network mask,
      owning intrusive `Zi::IOBufPoolList` with at least one nonempty Tx pool
      supplying count, size and alignment,
      one dedicated unlinked `ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool>` Rx pool, receive callback.
      Create pool objects with the selected instance's virtual `bufPool`.
      Init retains one reference per pool through close, while node membership
      remains in the caller configuration list. A node belongs to one
      list at a time; retain pool references for packets that outlive the instance.
      The concrete arena pool is internal. No transmit-completion callback. Without a mask all traffic is selected.
    * Keep allocation and kernel leases distinct in preallocated slot bookkeeping.
      Explicit pool return may run before or after CQ. Recycle only after both leases
      end; safe close releases kernel leases while caller-held backing stays valid.
      One descriptor may be outstanding for a slot. Rejected send acquires no lease.
    
    * Application and transport adaptation belongs to the caller. This library owns
      arena provisioning, raw packet allocation/return and kernel ring service.
    * Preallocate arenas and all packet bookkeeping at setup. Recycle each pool with
      the non-sharded ZmHeap payload-overlay slist. Exhaustion returns null.
    * Packet lookup and completion use direct slot identity, with constant-time
      updates. No packet/buffer searches or hot-path heap allocations.
    * Query kernel ring mapping offsets and preserve SWSR ownership. The caller
      provides one Rx service owner and one Tx service owner; final pool return may
      run on any thread. Keep thread-exclusive mutable state on separate cache lines.
    * The application assigns a sender `txSid` in its `ZmScheduler` and configures
      that slot with `Xdp::Params::txThread` (`ZmSchedTParams`, isolated by default).
      The scheduler owns thread startup, waiting and teardown. Zxdp owns no sender
      thread or semaphore. Publish initialized descriptors immediately: increment
      the pending-descriptor counter before commit and use scheduler `run()` after
      commit only on a zero-to-one transition. The dedicated sender calls nonblocking
      `sendto()`, observes the kernel consumer delta, spins for `Params_::spin` when
      pending work is exhausted, then atomically subtracts that delta. Use the
      returned pending count to continue or return without losing racing publication.
      Keep a persistent consumer cursor; never count the same consumption twice.
      Tx service has no custom wake function, epoll/eventfd or wait timeout. Rx keeps
      its epoll/eventfd wake protocol. The caller remains the sole descriptor
      producer and CQ owner; consumption accounting does not release kernel leases.
      Check exit during service and idle spin, then drain sender callbacks with a
      FIFO continuation before socket retirement.
    * Construct payload directly in registered backing. No payload staging or copy.
    * Quiesce service before close. Retire kernel access before returning submitted
      backing. A caller-owned pool retains its arena through the last packet return.
    * Queue configuration and mask compilation are cold-path operations.
    * Own the required `rx()`/`wake()` pair: spin for a configurable count before
      blocking with the most efficient suitable kernel mechanism; receive packets
      until explicitly woken, then return. With epoll, post wakeups through an
      internal `eventfd` when Rx has published a wait attempt, following
      ZiEventLoop/ZiMultiplex, with no per-wakeup allocation. Active and preposted
      wake pulses remain in userspace. Own these descriptors and their lifecycle. Wake
      must interrupt spinning and blocking promptly, including under continuous
      traffic and at the transition into the wait. Internal batches do not cause
      `rx()` to return on their own. The caller owns scheduling and lifecycle retries.
       Drain queued Tx activity and accepted submissions there, including native
       device completion/reclamation. Keep the required drain service available
       while closing; gating new work must not disable completion progress.
    3. In the Tx continuation, complete safe queue retirement, stop the port and
       release instance ownership. Return pending while retirement remains in flight;
       report actual errors as `ZeException`. Do not block an I/O owner, discard
       accepted work to simulate a drain, or add buffer-to-owner reference churn.
    
    Keep raw owner back-pointers safe by draining their dependent work before owner
    destruction. Caller-held backing remains valid through its independent pool
    lifetime. Retain any backing required by device queue state until that state
    is retired/reconfigured/finalized.
    
    Ordinary instance close does not call destructive `rte_eth_dev_close()`, remove
    the device or finalize EAL. The next instance can configure/start the same named
    port. Failed-init rollback drains and unwinds only resources acquired by that
    instance and retains the handle until cleanup completes. Final EAL teardown
    closes its stopped ports before `rte_eal_cleanup()`.
    
    Software fixtures also gate and drain their producers/peers and queued mbufs
    before freeing rings; ring stop alone does not perform that drain. This stays
    within existing lifecycle test scope and adds no production Tx worker.
    
    Both backends require `txPools` to contain at least one nonempty Tx pool.
    There is no Rx-only instance mode or zero-Tx-queue provision. Fixtures supply
    Tx pools even when their assertions focus on receive/filter/wake behavior.
    
    ### Native pool backing and direct send
    
    Implement internal `Dpdk::BufPool : Zi::IOBufPool`, constructed by
    `Dpdk::Instance::bufPool(...)`. Keep `Xdp::BufPool` internal and unchanged in
    purpose. Both implementations expose the common pool geometry and only
    `alloc()`/`free()` over their own backing. Storage identity and backend lease
    bookkeeping remain private implementation details.
    
    The DPDK pool supplies native mbuf backing from allocation onward. A packet
    received by DPDK send already identifies its mbuf; submit it directly without
    payload copies or external-buffer attachment. True means accepted submission;
    false acquires no submission lease and preserves caller ownership. Use native
    mbuf ownership/reference counting for asynchronous driver reclamation and any
    caller-retained backing, just as Xdp implements the same lifetime contract for
    UMEM. Reclamation accounting for `pollTx()` is private backend implementation
    work. There is no public writable-permission API or replacement permission state.
    
    Derive queue/descriptor and preallocated bookkeeping capacity from `txPools` and
    `rxPool`, honoring driver constraints. Do not add duplicate public sizing knobs.
    Keep backend-private direct packet identity and allocation-free packet service. Backend-native
    pool implementations supersede the earlier shared-arena proposal.
    
    The verified receive flow is the existing AF_XDP flow, mirrored by DPDK:
    
    1. Application `mx->allocator(...)` requests route through the selected plugin
       to backend-native pool allocation. A DPDK physical pool contains its configured
       count of native mbufs; registration establishes MTU-constrained geometry. Rx uses the
       shared physical ingress pool; logical Rx allocator requests provide metadata
       for that backing rather than independent physical packet pools.
    2. The backend makes Rx backing available to its driver/kernel. AF_XDP publishes
       UMEM addresses in FILL; a hardware DPDK PMD posts mbuf addresses through its
       internal Rx queue. A descriptor is that driver queue entry referring to a
       buffer, not another packet buffer or application pool allocation.
    3. On receive, the backend calls `RecvFn(packetBytes, length)` on the Rx owner.
    4. Zutcp creates a `Zi::IOBuf` stub referring to those same bytes and processes
       the packet. Metadata creation does not copy packet payload.
    5. Final metadata/backing release returns through the original Rx allocator to
       its ingress pool, making the backing available for subsequent reception.
    
    The arbitrary half-Rx-pool descriptor split is withdrawn. Do not silently
    partition an application-supplied pool into descriptor and retention halves or
    add physical-pool transport accounting. Driver queue setup and replacement use
    native DPDK mechanisms over the supplied mbuf pool. Driver constraints remain
    cold-path implementation details rather than new application sizing policy.
    
    ### Adopted software loopback ownership

        # Zxdp DPDK implementation plan
        
        Status: finalized against the repaired Zutcp working tree. DPDK remains
        unimplemented. This is the execution plan; concepts_brief.md retains the adopted
        design and explicit EAL configuration declaration. dpdk.md and dpdk_loopback.md
        are historical conversation/reference material, not competing specifications.
        
        ## Baseline and fixed boundaries
        
        Use the current source, including the author's completed zutcp_repair3 repair.
        Zutcp.hh is a backend umbrella; Instance owns both connection directions and
        listeners, implements ZiMxPlugin's Ztc::Mx interface and has no separate Hub,
        Client, Server or nativeInstance layer. Static bootstrap constructs/configures
        Instance and installs it on a stopped mx before allocator registration. Transfer
        code uses Ztcp/Ztls through ZiMultiplex. Do not introduce module loading or redo
        this repair. Preserve all existing working-tree changes and their test artifacts.
        
        Zxdp already has the cold instance(Type::Xdp) factory, virtual bufPool/init/send/
        rx/wake/pollTx/stopTx/close/allQueues, the Params tagged union and private Xdp
        pools/UMEM. Extend those interfaces. No InstanceData, commitFn, external-buffer
        attachment adapter, shared UMEM/mbuf allocator, Rx-only instance or intermediate
        DPDK Tx submission queue is needed. Zi::IOBufPool stays geometry plus alloc/free;
        no pool occupancy/writable/wait/cancel API or backing-based TCP receive accounting.
        
        Direct Tx is mx/Zutcp Tx -> rte_eth_tx_burst -> PMD/NIC. Rx polling and completion
        service use the existing single Rx/Tx owners. No DPDK sender thread or EAL packet
        worker is required. Queue setup is backend implementation work under driver
        constraints; all supplied Rx mbufs remain available to the PMD. Slow application
        retention may exhaust the pool and cause packet loss. Do not create extra backing
        or reserve an arbitrary fraction of the pool to avoid that outcome.
        
        ## 1. Optional dependency and explicit EAL
        
        In configure.ac, add --with-dpdk=yes|no following --with-pq. Only explicit yes
        enables PKG_CHECK_MODULES([DPDK], [libdpdk >= 25.11]); enabled-but-missing fails
        configuration. Reject invalid option values and enabled non-Linux targets.
        Define HAVE_DPDK for C++ conditionals and Automake DPDK for sources/tests; export
        DPDK_CFLAGS/DPDK_LIBS. Keep them out of disabled builds. In z.config add -K to
        usage/getopts, default DPDK=yes on Linux and pass --with-dpdk through both compiler
        branches. MinGW disables DPDK. Preserve all existing wrapper options.
        
        Create installed ZxdpDpdk.hh and ZxdpDpdk.cc for Zxdp::Dpdk::EAL/EALParams.
        Use the exact owned aggregate EALParams and enum declarations in the brief's
        “Adopted explicit EAL parameters” section; that declaration is normative input
        to this plan, not an invitation to redesign it. It covers lcores/main lcore,
        PCI/vdev discovery, memory/NUMA/hugepages, IOVA, process isolation, diagnostics,
        VFIO and extra native argv tokens. Keep all strings/lists owned. No environment
        variable configuration is required.
        
        EAL is discovered through
        ZmSingleton<Dpdk::EAL, ZmSingletonCleanup<ZmCleanup::Platform>>. Its constructor
        does not initialize DPDK. Expose init(const EALParams &) returning
        ZuUnion<void, ZeException> and ready() const. The application must explicitly
        initialize it before requesting DPDK instances/pools. A second init attempt is
        an error, not silent configuration replacement or hidden on-demand initialization.
        Its destructor closes its stopped registered ports then calls rte_eal_cleanup()
        after successful initialization. Instances, pools and retained mbufs must retire
        first; do not rely on ordering within one singleton cleanup level.
        
        Build private writable argv, beginning with a program name. Translate named
        options to native EAL argv and append raw args as individual tokens without shell
        parsing. Empty strings/void numeric values/Default enums omit that option. Map
        allow/block/driverPath to -a/-b/-d, memoryMB/channels/ranks to -m/-n/-r; other named
        fields use their documented DPDK 25.11 long options. Reject named/raw duplicates
        of the same option (including aliases) and retain DPDK's native validation.
        Empty lcores selects one suitable allowed CPU for the main lcore; preserve the
        initializing thread's intended affinity and never assume CPU zero is allowed.
        Explicit mappings remain under application control. No packet work is launched
        merely because EAL workers were configured.
        
        ## 2. Zxdp selection and API
        
        In Zxdp.hh extend Type to Xdp, Dpdk and Params to
        ZuUnion<Xdp::Params, Dpdk::Params>. Preserve current macro and in-place union
        construction conventions. Add:
        
        ```cpp
        namespace Dpdk {
          struct Params : public Params_ {
            ZtString<> name;           // owned DPDK Ethernet device name
            unsigned rxInterval = 50;  // maximum idle park in microseconds; zero polls
          };
        }
        ```
        
        These parameter types and Type::Dpdk need only framework headers and remain
        expressible in disabled builds. EAL/concrete DPDK definitions and linking are
        conditional. Zxdp::instance(Type::Dpdk) throws a structured ZeException when
        support was not built or EAL is not ready, consistent with its ZmRef return
        signature. It never substitutes Xdp. Construct the private Dpdk::Instance when
        available; keep the Xdp factory behavior unchanged.
        
        Add pure virtual void status() and implement it in both backends using the
        normal ZiLOG(Info, logging-lambda) convention. Log backend/device, state, MTU/MAC,
        operating copy mode and useful queue information. Retain mtu(), mac() and
        zeroCopy(); do not restore public ifindex(). zeroCopy reports actual operation:
        classify the configured PMD's data path, not just the Dpdk selector. Software
        pcap copies; direct ring forwarding does not. A fixture's simulated wire copy is
        outside the production instance's data path. Do not claim zero copy for an
        unverified copy-capable PMD.
        
        ## 3. Private pools, device ownership and packet service
        
        Create private ZxdpDpdkInstance.hh/.cc and ZxdpDpdkPool.hh/.cc. BufPool derives
        from Zi::IOBufPool and provides native mbuf backing; its effective count/size/
        headroom/tailroom/alignment are the supplied geometry. Defer physical pool setup
        until instance init so stopped configuration, including control count changes,
        is frozen before materialization. Native pools must remain alive through final
        caller-held backing return, independently of the factory/instance handle.
        Disable per-lcore mbuf caching initially so mbufs returned on other threads are
        available to the bounded pool rather than stranded in another thread's cache.
        
        Resolve name once with rte_eth_dev_get_port_by_name and retain its numeric port
        privately. EAL owns port registration/lifetime; Instance acquires exclusive use.
        Reject concurrent instance binding with ZeException. Configure one Rx and one Tx
        queue for the existing owners. Use the supplied Rx mempool for Rx replenishment;
        require at least one nonempty Tx pool. Derive queue capacities from supplied
        counts subject to PMD descriptor limits/adjustment. No public descriptor-count
        knob, extra reserve pool or half-pool partition is introduced.
        
        Query device MTU/MAC and configure for the existing contiguous-frame contract.
        Rx backing fits MTU plus frame/native headroom; do not enable scatter, coalescing
        or other offloads requiring chained/oversized representation. Tx pools may be
        smaller than MTU. Preserve required alignment without enlarging logical capacity.
        Materialize setup storage and packet bookkeeping before publishing readiness.
        
        Use direct backend-private packet/mbuf identity, including packet pointers after
        headroom offsets; do not search pools or attach external backing on each send.
        Private setup-time address indexing is allowed. Each accepted packet has one
        outstanding device submission. Native references protect driver access separately
        from the caller/recovery allocation lease. False send acquires no submission
        lease and leaves caller bytes/ownership intact; true transfers a driver reference
        and leaves any independent caller lease valid. Roll back temporary references on
        refusal. Do not enable PMD fast-free assumptions that contradict these references.
        No submitted Zi metadata is retained solely for device completion.
        
        pollTx() drives available PMD completion cleanup and reports each retired
        submission exactly once, preserving Zutcp's pending-credit accounting. Keep
        bookkeeping allocation-free and Tx-owned; pool return may occur on other threads.
        Handle PMD unsupported/error results explicitly without treating them as proof
        of retirement. Accepted work remains owned until actual retirement or safe device
        teardown; close errors never authorize freeing backing still in use.
        
        rx() receives mbufs from the configured Rx pool, calls RecvFn with the packet
        pointer/length and transfers that received backing to the caller's existing
        metadata path. Zutcp attaches an IOBuf stub to those bytes; final return reaches
        the original pool. Do not add a payload copy to production Rx. Register existing
        scheduler threads with DPDK where required by the chosen APIs; do not launch
        EAL packet workers to replace them.
        
        Use the adopted idle order: bounded receive batches with wake checks, immediate
        next-burst service under sustained input, then Params_::spin empty probes. Use
        native arrival waiting when supported; bounded producer-head memory monitoring
        may help short idle but does not imply kernel descheduling. For extended idle,
        park on the internal counted-wake eventfd with short timed waits backing off to
        rxInterval microseconds; zero stays active. Probe after timeout and restore
        active service immediately on a packet. Preserve preposted/concurrent wake pulses
        and check during sustained input and wait entry. No per-packet syscall is required
        for fixture arrival notification; do not modify the stock ring PMD.
        
        stopTx() gates submission and honors txStopped completion without a sender
        thread. Keep completion progress alive while draining. Follow docs/IO.md: gate
        new Rx/setup work, complete the Rx continuation, then drain Tx/accepted device
        work on Tx and retire queues. close() returns true/pending/ZeException under the
        existing retry contract. On success stop the port and release exclusive use;
        ordinary close does not destructively close/remove the EAL-owned device.
        Failed-init rollback unwinds only acquired instance resources, retains the handle
        while pending, and keeps externally configured devices available for reuse.
        A subsequent instance can reconfigure the stopped port after prior retirement.
        
        allQueues() traverses actual configured queues/rings and normalizes available PMD
        stats/reads into Ztc telemetry. Unsupported individual stats remain unavailable,
        not fabricated. Reuse existing traversal/lifetime conventions; no extra queue
        registry, index or cache exists solely for observation. Diagnostic reads do not
        require accurate snapshots or new hot-path synchronization.
        
        ## 4. Repaired Zutcp integration: exact configuration
        
        Preserve InstanceConfig and all repaired TCP behavior. In ZutcpMx.hh add:
        
        ```cpp
        struct DpdkParams {
          ZtString<> name;
          unsigned rxInterval = 50;
        };
        
        struct InstanceParams {
          unsigned interface = 0; // Linux control-plane interface, in both modes
          Zxdp::Type::T type = Zxdp::Type::Xdp;
          DpdkParams dpdk;
          ZuCSpan netmask; // Xdp selection only
          PacketFn packet;
          unsigned spin = 1000;
          unsigned packetCount = ZiIOBuf_DefltCount;
          ZmSchedTParams txThread = ZmSchedTParams().isolated(true); // Xdp only
          unsigned txSid = 0; // Xdp only
        };
        ```
        
        Include direct ZtString dependency. Retain type and owned DpdkParams in Instance
        before backend construction. Existing AF_XDP designated initializers and default
        selection remain valid. Preserve the private test-instance constructor and its
        existing semantics. These are typed static bootstrap settings, not a module
        loader or an application-facing connection API.
        
        Construction branches once on type. Xdp keeps current interface/queue discovery
        and sender setup. Dpdk requires ready EAL and a nonempty name; it does not require
        or use txSid/txThread. Reject a nonempty Xdp netmask in Dpdk mode as unsupported
        filter configuration. Retain the common Linux interface for MTU/MAC/routes and
        ISN scope. Create the selected backend before native pools. Dpdk ingress count
        is mx->rxBufSize() if nonzero, otherwise ZiIOBuf_DefltCount; do not call Xdp's
        queryLink for DPDK. Physical ingress buffers are MTU/frame-sized. Internal
        packet/control and registered application Tx pools use the selected bufPool.
        
        Keep Instance::allocator's current registration-time bound:
        min(requested payload size + protocol headroom, MTU + Ethernet overhead).
        Smaller requests remain smaller. Zi copies the bounded effective pool geometry,
        so default allocBuf() calls need no new per-call MTU limit. Do not add generic
        pool queries or an allocation-time size API.
        
        In start_(), select the matching Zxdp parameter union alternative. Populate
        common rxPool/txPools/rx callback/spin/scheduler/txStopped identically; add Xdp's
        ifindex/netmask/txSid or Dpdk's name/rxInterval in its branch. Retain independent
        pool references and let temporary configuration-list membership expire as today.
        Publish readiness only after successful init and matching established MTU; for
        DPDK also verify the represented Linux link MAC matches the packet port. Return
        structured setup failure and run normal rollback if geometry differs.
        
        On restart recreate instance(m_type), not instance(Type::Xdp), and rebuild the
        same branch from retained settings. Reuse pools only when compatible with prior
        retirement and outstanding caller-held backing. Preserve existing error/close
        retries, provider lifetimes, watch callbacks, shared policy, secrets and tuple
        history. No new transport owner or lifecycle controller is introduced.
        
        Keep the repaired Instance::resolve(remote, local) -> ZuUnion<IPPath, ZeException>
        on mx Rx. Reuse Linux routes and permanent neighbor mappings, including explicit
        next-hop MAC for routed destinations. A Linux control-plane interface can
        represent a userspace-owned DPDK link; configure matching addresses/MAC/MTU and
        associate it with the named DPDK port at bootstrap. It need not forward packets.
        No ARP/ND feature, exception path, custom route resolver or non-I/O route worker
        is required for this existing static-neighbor contract.
        
        ## 5. Zdb network allocation and failure
        
        In zdb/src/ZdbBuf.hh change the mx overload of tableBufAllocFn<T>() from App to
        TxTCP, preserving table-requested size/alignment/heap/count. Guard allocBuf()'s
        null result before assigning skip; return null unchanged on exhaustion. Preserve
        localBufAllocFn and the standalone local allocator. Existing storage/header/table

        In zdb/test/ZdbFBTest.cc add a finite plugin-backed pool test using a local test
        ZiMxPlugin/IOBufPool implementation. It can implement unused operations as test

        Assert TxTCP dispatch, requested geometry handed to the plugin, effective bounded

        unchanged standalone allocation. Inspect zdbsagareptest's App/RxTCP receive and

        ## 6. Software fixtures and coverage
        
        Use net_ring and net_pcap following dpdk_loopback.md through normal DPDK calls.
        The ring PMD forwards existing mbuf pointers and ignores the Rx mempool supplied
        to queue setup. Therefore the fixture must not directly forward one endpoint's
        Tx mbuf into another's Rx path. Dequeue an outgoing mbuf, allocate a destination
        Rx-pool mbuf, copy packet bytes, enqueue that destination mbuf on its Rx ring,
        then release the outgoing submission reference. On allocation/enqueue failure,
        release applicable references and drop the packet. This copy is the fixture's
        simulated wire, not a production backend copy. Stop peer producers before
        draining queues and releasing remaining mbufs/rings.
        
        Provide private shared ring/pcap setup, independent peer progress and cleanup in
        zxdp/itest/zxdpdpdkfixture.hh/.cc. Set fixed software device names/MACs and build
        pcap input/output for byte verification. Run EAL initialization variants in fresh
        subprocesses; do not rely on reinitializing process-global EAL between test cases.
        No physical NIC/VFIO binding is required for software acceptance.
        
        | Existing scope | New DPDK driver | Required adaptation |
        | --- | --- | --- |
        | Pool allocation/lifetime | ZxdpDpdkPoolTest | mbuf identity, geometry, exhaustion/return, retained backing |
        | Instance init/close | ZxdpDpdkInstanceTest | explicit EAL, mandatory Tx, structured failures, close/recreate |
        | Native packet I/O | zxdpdpdkpackettest | direct submission, Rx pool provenance, exact bytes, independent retirement |
        | Wake/service | zxdpdpdkwaketest | counted wakes, sustained Rx and configurable bounded idle; no Xdp sender assertion |
        | Loopback transfer | zxdpdpdklooptest | independent software peer, normal send/receive and teardown |
        | BPF classifier/filter | no DPDK copy | remains Xdp-specific |
        
        In Zutcp add zutcpdpdktest.cc with its private fixture helper
        zutcpdpdkfixture.hh/.cc. Use paired named ring ports and fixed Linux dummy
        control-plane interfaces/routes/permanent neighbors in isolated network namespace
        setup. Configure their MAC/MTU to match their DPDK ports. Mirror the repaired
        zutcpmxtest's applicable connection, bidirectional bytes, shared ownership,
        start/stop/restart and pool retirement scope through ZiMultiplex; include Ztcp
        application transfer using zutcpapptest's established pattern. Do not copy its
        Xdp-specific sender/filter assertions or reintroduce the removed public API.
        Keep AF_XDP drivers unchanged except existing regression expectations legitimately

        performance; no new benchmark or physical-NIC acceptance project belongs here.

## User

explain the Zdb null guard issue

## Assistant

`Zdb_::tableBufAllocFn()` currently does this:

```cpp
auto buf = allocator->allocBuf();
buf->skip = Zfb::Wire::MaxAlign;
```

After changing that allocator request from `App` to `TxTCP`, it can use a finite native pool. When the pool is exhausted, `allocBuf()` returns null, so assigning `buf->skip` would dereference null.

The fix is simply:

```cpp
auto buf = allocator->allocBuf();
if (!buf) return buf;
buf->skip = Zfb::Wire::MaxAlign;
```

This preserves the existing allocation-failure path. It adds no waiting or fallback allocation, and applies to AF_XDP as well as DPDK.

    # Instance ownership boundary
    
    Applications statically construct/configure one Instance and install it through
    ZiMultiplex::plugin() before allocator registration. Transfer code uses Ztcp/Ztls
    or the generic Zi callback interface. There is no Zutcp Hub/Client/Server
    application transport hierarchy or nativeInstance() bridge. Instance directly
    owns outgoing/accepted protocol records, listener endpoints, admission, secrets,
    history and native pools. Internal listeners own only local bind/options,
    pending/live membership and listener drain state.
    
    Instance implements ZiMxPlugin and its inherited Ztc::Mx interface, not Ztc::Hub.
    allQueues() traverses existing internal objects to expose normalized queue
    telemetry, including Zxdp's existing allQueues(). Do not add queue containers,
    indexes, registries or tracking caches. Existing object-lifetime references during
    enumeration protect callbacks that request asynchronous connection closure.
    
    Destination route/static-neighbor lookup runs synchronously on mx Rx during
    outbound and passive setup. It is intentional bounded blocking netlink work,
    with no route-worker selection or round trip. This supersedes historical notes
    below that place lookup outside Rx/Tx. Preserve real Rx/Tx ownership and ordered
    teardown; test contexts cannot reintroduce a second production owner or mode.
    
    # Current Phase 8 execution boundary
    
    The live protocol uses standard
    TCP headers/options and raw application bytes over Instance/Zxdp. Endpoint ownership
    uses TCP tuples; accepted byte history, canonical backing and owner handoffs
    remain authoritative. Intermediate packet/frame codecs and peer packet-number
    acknowledgments are deleted. Providers reserve the maximum standard Ethernet,
    IPv6 and TCP headers (114 bytes); the intermediate extra64-byte reserve is gone.
    
    Keep the accepted whole-original send/recovery policy, including positive peer
    windows smaller than an original. RST receive policy is window-qualified, with
    silent out-of-window rejection and no reflection of accepted peer resets.
    
    Raw send returns accepted/refused without a commit callback. Tx publishes the
    packet's ACK monotonically through the atomic `sentAck` only after successful
    return, then finishes recovery bookkeeping before queued peer-ACK work runs.
    Rx admits peer ACKs without consulting a transmitted byte frontier. Keep
    generation checks and the independent receive-window and RST qualification.
    
    Native providers implement `Zi::IOBufPool` over storage injected from a selected
    `Zxdp::Instance` backend's `bufPool()` factory. Keep concrete pool classes internal
    to Zxdp. Configuration owns its pool list; initialization retains independent
    backend references so configuration-list membership can expire after `init()`.
    # Native TCP integration tests
    
    These Linux tests exercise actual Instance/Zxdp packet I/O, standard TCP headers
    and raw application bytes. They require usable AF_XDP/BPF, sudo/root, network
    namespaces, iproute2, ethtool, tcpdump, Python3 and Perl/prove. Missing privileges
    or fixture variables produce visible skips; a skip is not native acceptance.
    See the [kernel/native quickstart](../util/README.md) for application integration,
    provider lifetime, interface ownership, routes, static neighbors and sudo setup.
    Physical Ethernet operation remains unverified in the current environment.

    // Scalar timestamp clock; Instance samples it only on Tx using the existing clock.
    // A backward wall step adjusts the logical offset without freezing later ticks.
    class TCPClock {
    public:
      bool sample(ZuTime now, uint32_t &out) {
        if (!*now || now < ZuTime{0}) return false;
        uint64_t wall = uint64_t(now.microsecs()) / 1000;
        if (!m_known) { m_ticks = wall; m_known = true; }
        else if (wall >= m_wall) m_ticks += wall - m_wall;
        m_wall = wall;
        out = uint32_t(m_ticks);
        return true;
      }
    private:
      uint64_t    m_wall = 0, m_ticks = 0;
      bool        m_known = false;
    };
    
    struct RtoParams {
      ZuTime initial{1};
      ZuTime min{0, 200000000};
      ZuTime max{60};
      ZuTime granularity{0, 1000000};
    
      bool valid() const {
        return initial > ZuTime{0} && min > ZuTime{0} && max >= min &&
          initial >= min && initial <= max && granularity > ZuTime{0};
      }
    };

    ZuUnion<void, ZeException> Instance::configure(const InstanceParams &config)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped && m_state == Stopped);
      if (!config.rtoParams.valid())
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid RTO bounds or granularity");
      if (config.tlpPeerAckDelay < ZuTime{0})
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "negative peer ACK allowance");
      if (*config.heartBeat && (config.heartBeat < ZuTime{0} || config.heartBeat.nsec() < 0 ||
          config.heartBeat.nsec() >= 1000000000))
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid TCP heartbeat interval");
      if (!config.maxPayload || config.maxPayload > BufSize)
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid payload cap");
      if (!rxThread() || !txThread() || rxThread() == txThread() ||
          rxThread() > mx()->params().nThreads() || txThread() > mx()->params().nThreads())
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid multiplexer Rx/Tx owners");
      if (!positiveTimeout(config.connectTimeout)) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid connect timeout");
      }
      if (!positiveTimeout(config.closeDrainTimeout) || !positiveTimeout(config.finWaitTimeout)) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid close timeout");
      }
      if (!positiveTimeout(config.userTimeout) && config.userTimeout != ZuTime{0}) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid user timeout");
      }
      if (config.ackHoldTimeout < ZuTime{0} ||
          config.ackHoldTimeout >= ZuTime{0, 500000000}) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid TCP ACK hold timeout");
      }
      if (!config.maxCxns || !config.maxPendingCxns || config.maxPendingCxns > config.maxCxns) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid connection admission limits");
      }
      if (!config.tfoCookieCacheSize) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid Fast Open cookie cache size");
      }
      if (!config.closedTupleRingSize) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid closed tuple ring size");
      }
      if (!config.rxRetainFramesPerCxn)
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "invalid per-connection Rx retention limit");
      auto control = configureControl(config.controlBufCount, config.txControlCredits);
      if (control.is<ZeException>()) return control;
      m_closed.resize(config.closedTupleRingSize);
      m_tfoCookies.resize(config.tfoCookieCacheSize);
      InstanceParams next = config;
      next.interface = m_params.interface;
      next.netmask = m_netmask;
      next.packet = m_params.packet;
      next.spin = m_params.spin;
      next.packetCount = m_params.packetCount;
      next.txThread = m_params.txThread;
      next.txSid = m_params.txSid;
      m_params = ZuMv(next);
      if (m_params.heartBeat == ZuTime{0}) m_params.heartBeat = {};
      return {};
    }
    
    CxnAdmission Instance::cxnAdmission() const
    {
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped || mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      return m_cxnSlots.admission(m_params.maxCxns, m_params.maxPendingCxns);
    }

    # Instance ownership boundary
    
    Applications statically construct/configure one Instance and install it through
    ZiMultiplex::plugin() before allocator registration. Transfer code uses Ztcp/Ztls
    or the generic Zi callback interface. There is no Zutcp Hub/Client/Server
    application transport hierarchy or nativeInstance() bridge. Instance directly
    owns outgoing/accepted protocol records, listener endpoints, admission, secrets,
    history and native pools. Internal listeners own only local bind/options,
    pending/live membership and listener drain state.
    
    Instance implements ZiMxPlugin and its inherited Ztc::Mx interface, not Ztc::Hub.
    allQueues() traverses existing internal objects to expose normalized queue
    telemetry, including Zxdp's existing allQueues(). Do not add queue containers,
    indexes, registries or tracking caches. Existing object-lifetime references during
    enumeration protect callbacks that request asynchronous connection closure.
    
    Destination route/static-neighbor lookup runs synchronously on mx Rx during
    outbound and passive setup. It is intentional bounded blocking netlink work,
    with no route-worker selection or round trip. This supersedes historical notes
    below that place lookup outside Rx/Tx. Preserve real Rx/Tx ownership and ordered
    teardown; test contexts cannot reintroduce a second production owner or mode.
    
    # Current Phase 8 execution boundary
    
    The live protocol uses standard
    TCP headers/options and raw application bytes over Instance/Zxdp. Endpoint ownership
    uses TCP tuples; accepted byte history, canonical backing and owner handoffs
    remain authoritative. Intermediate packet/frame codecs and peer packet-number
    acknowledgments are deleted. Providers reserve the maximum standard Ethernet,
    IPv6 and TCP headers (114 bytes); the intermediate extra64-byte reserve is gone.
    
    Keep the accepted whole-original send/recovery policy, including positive peer
    windows smaller than an original. RST receive policy is window-qualified, with
    silent out-of-window rejection and no reflection of accepted peer resets.
    
    Raw send returns accepted/refused without a commit callback. Tx publishes the
    packet's ACK monotonically through the atomic `sentAck` only after successful
    return, then finishes recovery bookkeeping before queued peer-ACK work runs.
    Rx admits peer ACKs without consulting a transmitted byte frontier. Keep

    Native providers implement `Zi::IOBufPool` over storage injected from a selected

    backend references so configuration-list membership can expire after `init()`.

    class ZutcpAPI CxnSlot {

    public:
    // and the separately selected local sequence proof remain caller requirements.
    inline bool reusePeerTuple(
      const ClosedTuple &record, const TCPHeader &syn, bool timestamps, ZuTime now)
    {
      if (!record.fin) return false;
      bool newerSequence = reuseSequence(syn.seq, uint32_t(record.rxNext - 1));
      bool proposed = timestamps && (syn.options.flags & TCPOptions::TS);
      if (!record.timestamps) return proposed || newerSequence;
      if (!proposed) return newerSequence;
      bool recent = *record.tsRecentTime && (now < record.tsRecentTime ||
        now - record.tsRecentTime <= ZuTime{24*24*60*60});
      if (!recent) return newerSequence;
      uint32_t distance = syn.options.tsval - record.tsRecent;
      return (distance && distance < uint32_t(0x80000000)) || (!distance && newerSequence);
    }

      unsigned    capacity = 0, count = 0;
      uint64_t    inserted = 0, evicted = 0;
    };

    // Scalar timestamp clock; Instance samples it only on Tx using the existing clock.
    // A backward wall step adjusts the logical offset without freezing later ticks.
    class TCPClock {
    public:
      bool sample(ZuTime now, uint32_t &out)
      {
        if (!*now || now < ZuTime{0}) return false;
        uint64_t wall = uint64_t(now.microsecs()) / 1000;
        if (!m_known) { m_ticks = wall; m_known = true; }
        else if (wall >= m_wall) m_ticks += wall - m_wall;
        m_wall = wall;
        out = uint32_t(m_ticks);
        return true;
      }
    
    private:
      uint64_t    m_wall = 0, m_ticks = 0;
      bool        m_known = false;
    };

    void Instance::addProvider(Allocator *p)
    {
      ZmREF(p);

    Zi::IOBufPool *Instance::allocator(
      Zi::IOBufType::T type, unsigned size, unsigned align, unsigned count)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped);
      // Providers reserve complete output framing before Zi copies their geometry.
      enum { Ethernet = 14, IPv6 = 40, TCP = 60 };
      unsigned head;
      switch (type) {
        case Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP:
        case Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP: head = Ethernet + IPv6 + TCP; break;
        default: throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported network allocator role");
      }
      if (head >= m_mtu + Ethernet || !align || (align & (align - 1)) ||
          align > unsigned(sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)))
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported packet allocator geometry");
      if (type == Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP)
        return new RxAllocator{m_ingress, head, count, align};
      uint64_t bytes = uint64_t(size) + head;
      if (bytes > m_mtu + Ethernet) bytes = m_mtu + Ethernet;
      auto p = new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(count, unsigned(bytes), head, 0, align)};
      addProvider(p);
      return p;
    }
    
    ZuUnion<void, ZeException> Instance::configureControl(unsigned count, unsigned credits)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped && m_state == Stopped);
      uint64_t capacity = m_txCapacity - m_control->pool->count + count;
      if (!count || !credits || credits >= capacity || capacity > UINT_MAX ||
          m_txPending) {
        return ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", ([count, credits, capacity](auto &out) {
          out << "invalid or busy control reserve count=" << count
        << " credits=" << credits << " Tx capacity=" << capacity;
        }));
      }
      m_control->count = m_control->pool->count = count;
      m_controlCredits = credits;
      m_txCapacity = capacity;
      return {};
    }

      params.spin = m_params.spin;

    // Zi adapters retain this provider through final registered returns. Its pool
    // therefore outlives the packet instance and all application/DMA-held buffers.
    // Freeze geometry and intrusive links while the raw instance is active.
    struct Allocator;
    
    struct AllocatorData : public Zi::IOBufPool {
      using ReturnedFn = ZmFn<void(), ZmFnHeapID<"Zutcp.Returned">>;
      ReturnedFn returned;
      ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool> pool;
      Allocator    *nextProvider = nullptr;
    
      explicit AllocatorData(ZmRef<Zi::IOBufPool> pool_) : pool{ZuMv(pool_)} {
        ZmAssert_(pool);
        count = pool->count;
        size = pool->size;
        align = pool->align;
        headRoom = pool->headRoom;
        tailRoom = pool->tailRoom;
        ZmAssert_(headRoom <= size && tailRoom <= size - headRoom);
      }
    };
    
    struct ZutcpAPI Allocator : public ZmNHeap<Allocator>, public AllocatorData {
    friend inline ZuStringT<"Zutcp.Allocator"> ZmNHeapID(Allocator *);
      using ZmNHeap<Allocator>::operator new;
      using ZmNHeap<Allocator>::operator delete;
    
      using AllocatorData::AllocatorData;
      uint8_t *alloc() override;
      void free(uint8_t *) override;
    };
    
    // The caller allocation lease lives in an existing recovery/source node,
    // independently of copied SentPkt metadata and the raw kernel lease. Owners drain
    // recovery before releasing the provider; there is no per-packet owner ref.
    class ZutcpAPI PacketLease {
    public:
      PacketLease() = default;
      PacketLease(const PacketLease &) = delete;
      PacketLease &operator =(const PacketLease &) = delete;
      ~PacketLease();
    
      void adopt(Zi::IOBufAllocator *, uint8_t *, unsigned);
      void reset();
      bool operator *() const { return m_data; }
      uint8_t *data() const { return m_data; }
    
    private:
      Zi::IOBufAllocator *m_allocator = nullptr;
      uint8_t *m_data = nullptr;
      unsigned m_size = 0;
    };
    
    // Internal packet adapters and retained source nodes use this wire metadata.
    // The handoff is Tx-owned, valid for one synchronous submission, and cleared
    // by the builder before the sent record can be discarded on refusal.
    struct PacketBuf : public Zi::IOBuf {
      PacketLease *retained = nullptr;
      TCPHeader tcp;
      using Zi::IOBuf::IOBuf;
    };
    
    // Unregistered codec/recovery fixtures have no raw allocation lease.
    inline void bindPacketLease(Zi::IOBuf *, PacketLease *) { }
    inline void bindPacketLease(PacketBuf *buf, PacketLease *lease) {
      buf->retained = lease;
    }
