    # Zutcp: User-mode TCP/IP stack
    
    Zutcp is a Linux user-mode TCP/IP stack integrated with `ZiMultiplex`, using
    [Zxdp](../zxdp/README.md) for raw AF_XDP packet I/O. It targets short FIX order,
    execution and market-data messages while keeping the existing Zi connection,
    allocator and application framing interfaces.
    
    The native transport uses standard TCP headers/options and raw application payload.
    Selected IPv4/IPv6 native and real Linux-kernel peer fixtures validate transfer,
    recovery, options and lifecycle behavior. See [native tests](itest/README.md) and
    [independent-peer tests](interop/README.md) for runnable commands and coverage.
    Physical-Ethernet peer operation has not been validated in this environment.
    
    The current native path carries SYN/SYNACK sequence origins, connection byte
    sequence, cumulative ACK, FIN and negotiated receive windows in the TCP header.
    Standard options carry MSS, SACK/DSACK, window scaling and timestamps/PAWS.
    Initial sequence numbers use HMAC-SHA256 through OpenSSL's crypto library.
    Internal byte positions remain wide offsets relative to the chosen origins.
    Endpoint routing uses the TCP four-tuple. Intermediate packet/frame codecs,
    bootstrap IDs and packet-number acknowledgment formats have been removed.
    
    `InstanceParams::sackPermitted`, `windowScale` and `timestamps` default to enabled.
    Configure them before starting the multiplexer. SACK permission is directional;
    scaling and timestamps require both peers' offers. The receive scale derives
    from `maxData`. Without a peer MSS option, the send cap is 536 bytes for IPv4 or
    1220 for IPv6; actual TCP option bytes reduce the application budget.
    Establishment publishes that budget before callbacks.
    SACK retains original transmit backing until cumulative acknowledgment, including
    when a receiver reneges on its earlier report.
    
    The native pair uses RACK send chronology and one accepted TLP probe
    per episode when SACK is available. Timestamp-free recovery remains supported;
    without SACK it uses cumulative ACK recovery and RTO. Classic TCP ECN is
    configured through the existing default-off `ecn` setting. New DATA carries ECT
    only after negotiation; retransmissions and control packets remain Not-ECT.
    With congestion control enabled, accepted DATA sends create pacing debt;
    pure ACK/window traffic can proceed.
    
    `InstanceParams::congestionControl = false` disables congestion-window limits,
    congestion accounting and pacing for controlled low-latency networks. Set it before starting
    the multiplexer. The default is enabled; the setting is cached at initialization.
    Disabled mode suppresses ECN negotiation while retaining receiver flow control,
    bounded local buffer credits, ACK/SACK retirement, loss recovery and RTO backoff.
    Nagle remains disabled in both modes.
    
    `InstanceParams::ackHoldTimeout` configures the cumulative ACK hold. It defaults to 25
    milliseconds, accept zero to disable holding, and require a value below 500
    milliseconds. Eligible in-order DATA may hold one pending ACK; each receive
    updates it to the latest cumulative position. Outgoing DATA can carry that ACK
    before the deadline. A second full-size segment, FIN, receive gap, duplicate,
    ECN exception or receive-window reopening requests an immediate reply.
    
    After successful native submission, the Tx owner publishes the packet's cumulative
    ACK atomically, preserving its coordinate conversion and monotonic progress.
    Refused sends leave that ACK unchanged. Recovery bookkeeping finishes on the same
    Tx owner before queued peer ACK work runs. Incoming peer ACKs pass directly to
    ACK processing without validation against a published transmitted frontier.
    
    Without timestamps, an exact full sequence-cycle alias can be indistinguishable
    from current data. PAWS adds timestamp checks under its ordinary clock and
    segment-lifetime assumptions; it does not create an unlimited wire epoch.
    
    ## Application integration
    
    See the [kernel/native quickstart](util/README.md) for the stopped-multiplexer
    setup, actual command-line tools, sudo fixture commands and deployment prerequisites.
    
    `Zutcp::Instance` implements `ZiMxPlugin`. Register it on a stopped multiplexer
    before creating application allocators or starting I/O. One Instance owns both
    outgoing and accepted connections and all listeners for its multiplexer. The app
    using IOBufAllocFactory = ZmFn<IOBufAllocFn(ZiMultiplex *)>;
    
    template <typename T>
    IOBufAllocFn tableBufAllocFn(ZiMultiplex *mx) {
      auto allocator = mx->allocator<Zi::IOBufType::App, IOBuf,
        ZdbBuf_Size<T>{}, ZiIOBuf_Align, ZdbBuf_HeapID<T>, MaxBufSize>();
      IOBufAllocFn fn{[allocator]() {
        ZmRef<IOBuf> buf = allocator->allocBuf();
        // Reserve the envelope before the backwards-growing row arena starts.
        buf->skip = Zfb::Wire::MaxAlign;
        return buf;
      }};
      fn.allocator(allocator);
      return fn;

    # Instance ownership boundary
    
    Applications statically construct one Instance, configure it through
    init(Params params), and install it through ZiMultiplex::plugin() before allocator
    registration. There is no configure() method or public params() accessor. Transfer code uses Ztcp/Ztls
    or the generic Zi callback interface. There is no Zutcp Hub/Client/Server
    application transport hierarchy or nativeInstance() bridge. Instance directly
    owns outgoing/accepted protocol records, listener endpoints, admission, secrets,
    history and native pools. Internal listeners own only local bind/options,
    pending/live membership and listener drain state.
    
    Instance implements ZiMxPlugin and its inherited Ztc::Mx interface, not Ztc::Hub.
    allQueues() traverses existing internal objects to expose normalized queue
    telemetry, including Zxdp's existing allQueues(). Do not add queue containers,
    indexes, registries or tracking caches. Existing object-lifetime references during
    enumeration protect callbacks that request asynchronous connection closure.
    
    Destination route/static-neighbor lookup runs synchronously on mx Rx during
    outbound and passive setup. It is intentional bounded blocking netlink work,
    with no route-worker selection or round trip. This supersedes historical notes
    below that place lookup outside Rx/Tx. Preserve real Rx/Tx ownership and ordered
    teardown; test contexts cannot reintroduce a second production owner or mode.
    
    # Current Phase 8 execution boundary
    
    The live protocol uses standard
    TCP headers/options and raw application bytes over Instance/Zxdp. Endpoint ownership
    uses TCP tuples; accepted byte history, canonical backing and owner handoffs
    remain authoritative. Intermediate packet/frame codecs and peer packet-number
    acknowledgments are deleted. Providers reserve the maximum standard Ethernet,
    IPv6 and TCP headers (114 bytes); the intermediate extra64-byte reserve is gone.
    
    Keep the accepted whole-original send/recovery policy, including positive peer
    windows smaller than an original. RST receive policy is window-qualified, with
    silent out-of-window rejection and no reflection of accepted peer resets.
    
    Raw send returns accepted/refused without a commit callback. Tx publishes the
    packet's ACK monotonically through the atomic `sentAck` only after successful
    return, then finishes recovery bookkeeping before queued peer-ACK work runs.
    Rx admits peer ACKs without consulting a transmitted byte frontier. Keep
    generation checks and the independent receive-window and RST qualification.
    
    Native providers implement `Zi::IOBufPool` over storage injected from a selected
    `Zxdp::Instance` backend's `bufPool()` factory. Keep concrete pool classes internal
    to Zxdp. Configuration owns its pool list; initialization retains independent
    backend references so configuration-list membership can expire after `init()`.
    Tx buffer allocation failure drops the connection; producers do not wait for
    pool grants. Alignment changes physical stride without inflating logical buffer capacity.
    
    Build/test Zutcp and its dependency closure in explicit directory/target order.
    Use the five native drivers and separate independent-kernel interop runner while
    finishing TCP. Selected Ztcp/Ztls application checks follow TCP completion; they

    void Instance::addProvider(Allocator *p)

    Zi::IOBufPool *Instance::allocator(
      Zi::IOBufType::T type, unsigned size, unsigned align, unsigned count)
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->state() == ZmEngineState::Stopped);
      // Providers reserve complete output framing before Zi copies their geometry.
      enum { Ethernet = 14, IPv6 = 40, TCP = 60 };
      unsigned head;
      switch (type) {
        case Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP:
        case Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP: head = Ethernet + IPv6 + TCP; break;
        default: throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported network allocator role");
      }
      if (head >= m_mtu + Ethernet || !align || (align & (align - 1)) ||
          align > unsigned(sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)))
        throw ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "unsupported packet allocator geometry");
      if (type == Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP)
        return new RxAllocator{m_ingress, head, count, align};
      uint64_t bytes = uint64_t(size) + head;
      if (bytes > m_mtu + Ethernet) bytes = m_mtu + Ethernet;
      auto p = new Allocator{m_backend->bufPool(count, unsigned(bytes), head, 0, align)};
      addProvider(p);
      return p;
    }
    
    void Instance::initControl(unsigned count, unsigned credits)
    {
      m_txCapacity = m_txCapacity - m_control->pool->count + count;
      m_control->count = m_control->pool->count = count;
      m_controlCredits = credits;
    }

      params.spin = m_params.spin;

    `Zutcp::Instance` implements `ZiMxPlugin`. Register it on a stopped multiplexer
    before creating application allocators or starting I/O. One Instance owns both
    outgoing and accepted connections and all listeners for its multiplexer. The app
    constructs and configures it statically; no module loader or factory is involved.
    Instance implements the inherited `Ztc::Mx` telemetry interface, not `Ztc::Hub`.
    Select the interface and
    optional destination network mask at setup; backend selection stays fixed while
    the multiplexer runs. An mx without this plugin uses its normal kernel backend.
    
    Applications continue to use [Ztcp](../ztcp/README.md) and, for encryption above
    TCP, [Ztls](../ztls/README.md). Zutcp itself supplies TCP transport and has no
    Ztls dependency. Ordinary `ZiIP` addresses and `ZiResolver` remain available.
    Zutcp resolves routes and static neighbors synchronously on mx Rx during
    connection setup, constrained to the configured interface. This bounded blocking
    netlink setup work finishes before the first SYN or SYNACK; there is no resolver
    worker. With a destination mask, unmatched traffic stays with the
    host stack; without a mask Zxdp selects the whole interface.
    
    In the application bootstrap, initialize Instance before installing the plugin.
    Handle its structured initialization result before registering allocators or
    starting mx; this example returns false from a boolean bootstrap function:
    
    ```c++
    // mx already has distinct Rx/Tx owners and an assigned AF_XDP sender slot.
    ZmRef<Zutcp::Instance> plugin = new Zutcp::Instance{&mx};
    auto initialized = plugin->init({.interface = ifindex, .txSid = senderSid,
      .ackHoldTimeout = ZuTime{0, 25000000}});
    if (initialized.is<ZeException>()) {
      ZiLogEvent(ZuMv(initialized.p<ZeException>()));
      return false;
    }
    mx.plugin(plugin);
    ```
    
    Connection and transfer code uses Ztcp/Ztls or the existing generic Zi callbacks.
    The former Zutcp Hub, Client and Server application transport hierarchy is removed.
    Private protocol headers are available only in the source tree for backend tests.
    
    Each connection owns one ordered bidirectional byte flow: reassembly, delivery,
    receive-credit retirement, retained transmit backing, recovery and close state.
    # Select Zutcp or the regular kernel TCP backend
    
    Zutcp implements TCP for applications using this repository's `ZiMultiplex`
    connection and allocator interfaces. Install `Zutcp::Instance` on the multiplexer to
    select AF_XDP; leave the plugin unset to use regular kernel TCP. Existing Zi/Ztcp
    application framing and callbacks remain in use. Ztls can run above either TCP
    backend; it is not a dependency of libZutcp.
    
    This is an application integration choice, not an `LD_PRELOAD` library or a
    replacement implementation of arbitrary POSIX `socket()` calls. Applications
    using raw kernel sockets continue to use the kernel until adapted to Zi/Ztcp. `zutcpkernelpeer` deliberately uses ordinary kernel sockets;
    `zutcppair` deliberately uses the actual native Instance, without socket fallback.
    
    ## Select the backend before allocating or starting
    
    The following boolean application-bootstrap fragment uses the existing plugin
    setter and the single init(Params) configuration entry. Handle its structured
    error before installing the plugin or registering application allocators:
    
    ```cpp
    #include <net/if.h>
    #include <zlib/ZmRef.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZiLog.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZiRx.hh>
    #include <zlib/ZiTx.hh>
    #include <zlib/Zutcp.hh>
    
    ZiMultiplex mx{ZiMxParams{}.rxThread(1).txThread(2).scheduler([](auto &s) {
      s.nThreads(3)
        .thread(1, [](auto &t) { t.isolated(1); })
        .thread(2, [](auto &t) { t.isolated(1); })
        .thread(3, [](auto &t) { t.isolated(true); });
    })};
    
    // Native branch only. Check if_nametoindex() before constructing Instance.
    ZmRef<Zutcp::Instance> stack = new Zutcp::Instance{&mx};
    auto initialized = stack->init({.interface = if_nametoindex("OWNED_INTERFACE"), .txSid = 3});
    if (initialized.is<ZeException>()) {
      ZiLogEvent(ZuMv(initialized.p<ZeException>()));
      return false;
    }
    mx.plugin(stack);
    
    // Factory calls follow plugin registration while mx is still stopped.
    auto rx = mx.allocator<Zi::IOBufType::RxTCP, ZiRxBuf, 2048>(4096);
    auto tx = mx.allocator<Zi::IOBufType::TxTCP, ZiIOBuf, 1024>(4096);
    // Initialize the Ztcp application while stopped.
    // Start mx, then use ordinary listen/connect entry points.
    ```
    
    For the kernel branch, omit Instance construction, `plugin()` and Instance configuration;
    use the same Zi connection/framing interfaces. Backend selection is fixed for the
    multiplexer lifetime. Do not attach the plugin after allocator factories: native
    providers must publish and register their geometry before start. For native Tx,
    use those registered Tx buffers and their published payload budget; do not substitute
    heap/network buffers. `rxBufSize` is kernel socket bytes in kernel mode and native
    ingress frame count with Instance, so do not pass a byte count as a native frame count.
    The factory count requests pool backing; kernel allocation does not emulate a
    fixed native pool. Log effective settings when comparing backends.

    using IOBufAllocFactory = ZmFn<IOBufAllocFn(ZiMultiplex *)>;
    
    template <typename T>
    IOBufAllocFn tableBufAllocFn(ZiMultiplex *mx) {
      auto allocator = mx->allocator<Zi::IOBufType::App, IOBuf,
        ZdbBuf_Size<T>{}, ZiIOBuf_Align, ZdbBuf_HeapID<T>, MaxBufSize>();
      IOBufAllocFn fn{[allocator]() {
        ZmRef<IOBuf> buf = allocator->allocBuf();
        // Reserve the envelope before the backwards-growing row arena starts.
        buf->skip = Zfb::Wire::MaxAlign;
        return buf;
      }};
      fn.allocator(allocator);
      return fn;
    }

    CxnAdmission Instance::cxnAdmission() const
    {
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped || mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      return m_cxnSlots.admission(m_params.maxCxns, m_params.maxPendingCxns);
    }
    
    CxnSlot Instance::reserveCxn()
    {

      return m_cxnSlots.reserve(m_params.maxCxns, m_params.maxPendingCxns);

    void Instance::start_()
    {
      ZmAssert_(mx()->invoked(mx()->rxThread()));
      if (ready()) { mx()->pluginStarted({}); return; }
      ZmAssert_(m_state == Stopped);
      m_state = Starting;
      m_rxWakeQueued = 0;
      m_error = {};
      // A backend initializes once. Retain closed telemetry until this next start.
      if (m_backendInit) m_backend = Zxdp::instance(Zxdp::Type::Xdp);
      m_backendInit = true;
      Zxdp::Params config(
        Zxdp::Params::New<Zxdp::Params::Index<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>{}>{});
      auto &params = config.p<Zxdp::Xdp::Params>();
      params.ifindex = m_params.interface;
      params.netmask = m_netmask;
      params.rxPool = m_ingress->pool;
      params.rx = [this](uint8_t *p, unsigned n) { received(p, n); };
      params.spin = m_params.spin;
      params.scheduler = mx();
      params.txSid = m_params.txSid;
      params.txStopped = [this] {
        mx()->push([this] { senderStopped(); }, mx()->txThread());
      };
      for (auto p = m_providers; p; p = p->nextProvider)
        params.txPools.pushNode(p->pool.ptr());
      auto initialized = m_backend->init(config);
      if (initialized.is<ZeException>()) m_error = ZuMv(initialized.p<ZeException>());
      if (m_backend && m_backend->ready() && m_backend->mtu() == m_mtu) {
        m_current = m_backend.ptr();
        m_state = Running;
        mx()->pluginStarted({});
        return;
      }
      if (!m_error)
        m_error = ZeEXCEPT(Error, "Zutcp", "interface geometry changed before packet startup");
      m_startFailure = true;
      m_state = Stopping;
      mx()->txRun([this] { stopTx(); });
    }

    class Instance : public Zutcp::Instance {
    public:
      explicit Instance(ZiMultiplex *mx)
      : Zutcp::Instance{mx, 1500, new Pool, new Pool,
          new Pool{Zutcp::DefaultControlBufCount}} { }
      static Zutcp::InstanceParams parameters(const Zutcp::Instance &instance) {
        return instance.m_params;
      }
      static ZuUnion<void, ZeException> apply(
        Zutcp::Instance &instance, Zutcp::InstanceParams params)
      {
        auto bootstrap = parameters(instance);
        params.interface = bootstrap.interface;
        params.netmask = bootstrap.netmask;
        params.packet = bootstrap.packet;
        params.spin = bootstrap.spin;
        params.packetCount = bootstrap.packetCount;
        params.txThread = bootstrap.txThread;
        params.txSid = bootstrap.txSid;
        return instance.init(ZuMv(params));
      }
      bool init(const ZutcpTest::Params &params) {
        auto result = params.mx() == mx() ? apply(*this, params.config()) :
          ZuUnion<void, ZeException>{ZeEXCEPT(Error, "ZutcpTest", "fixture mx mismatch")};
        if (result.template is<ZeException>()) {
          if (params.errorFn()) params.errorFn()(result.template p<ZeException>());
          return false;
        }
        return true;
      }
    };
    
    inline ZmRef<Zutcp::Instance> makeInstance(
      ZiMultiplex *mx, Zutcp::InstanceParams params)

      ZmRef<Zutcp::Instance> instance = new Zutcp::Instance{mx};

      if (result.template is<ZeException>()) throw result.template p<ZeException>();

## User

"lazy native pool and allocator adapters"? explain

## Assistant

“Lazy” meant **created during explicit `init(Params)`, rather than in the constructor**.

- `Instance(mx)` creates the cold transport object.
- `init(Params)` creates the backend pool/provider objects and constructs the internal `Allocators` group: Rx, packet Tx, data Tx and control Tx adapters.
- Backend startup activates the native packet storage.

Nothing waits until the first packet. “Explicit initialization of pools and allocator adapters” would be clearer wording.
